388YE Autumn Asavean ambassador briefing.d: Lady Madrianna rejected the Ambassador's portrayal of the Plenum's relationship with the Salt Lords, calling the Grendel model allies whom Asavea would support for as long as the war with the Senate continued. She conceded that Asavean backing for the Empire's enemies, such as the Faraden Cinders and hired privateers, had been ineffective, and implied that the Plenum would now mobilise many fleets and warbands, echoing the burning of Chalonsio. Her minimum terms for peace were an apology and reparations for Chalonsio, an end to missionary work and Synod-backed rebellion with the names of contacts, the handing over of Rafael Barossa, and an end to the trade embargo with favourable tariffs.

n.Grendel: The Plenum declared the Grendel steadfast allies politically, economically and militarily, and pledged to keep supporting them while the war with the Empire lasts, though it is rethinking how that support is given.

t.Bay of Catazar: The civil service read Madrianna's note as a threat that the Plenum is exploring ways to send large numbers of fleets and military warbands into the Bay of Catazar instead of a handful of warships and mercenaries.

388YE Autumn Axos ambassador briefing.d: The Shield of Ipotavo contained Winter spirits in northern Sarangrave but resents defending it alone and will give ground unless Imperial armies fight alongside. The Axou are turning the Tower of the Skink into a settlement, possibly to be renamed New Solokah, at the cost of its defences, and offered 65 Thrones for 20 wains of weirwood. They declined to join a Sanath campaign unless promised land such as Leen Rarckan, but offered mercenaries. They suggested an appraisal for Axou-designed fortifications, sought action against trods in Sarangrave, refused help on a past-life vision, revealed Convocation interest in true liao for a Fintan Nighthaven consecration, and demanded an apology for an insulting letter.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Castle of Thorns is used as a benchmark for the reduced strength the Tower of the Skink is expected to have by Spring.
n.Druj: The collapse of Druj armies had unleashed Winter spirits in Sarangrave, the Axou resent protecting freed Druj slaves, and the Grand Ilarchs praised the Empire's planned drive into the Salt Flats of Sanath to end the Druj threat, without committing armies of their own.
n.Navarr: Axou fear of the vallorn led them to plan a ritual to sever trods in their lands and Sarangrave, and to ask the Empire to interdict the Dance of Navarr and Thorn or outlaw trods there; the Unified Convocation also sought true liao to consecrate a shrine to the executed Navarr Fintan Nighthaven.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Walls of Holberg are named as the only Imperial fortification the Tower of the Skink currently falls short of.
n.Urizen: The Axou are more willing to defend the Urizen in Sarangrave than the former slaves, though they would prefer them gathered in one place rather than across new spires, and Axou engineers might be commissioned to help expand the Walls of Cargo.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Castle of Thorns is the fortification the remodelled Tower of the Skink is expected to equal by the Spring Equinox.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Walls of Holberg are cited as the one Imperial fortification stronger than the Tower of the Skink as it currently stands.
t.Redoubt: The ambassador had asked for Axou help improving the Walls of Cargo, and Skopos suggested a Senate appraisal involving the engineers of the Gates of Ipotavo, an opportunity open until the end of the Summer Solstice 389YE.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Axos would commit no armies to the planned Imperial conquest unless offered land, but up to 10 Axou mercenary warbands could be hired to fight there for 100 crystal mana or 130 crowns.
t.Sarangrave: The Shield of Ipotavo held back Winter spirits and saved many former slaves, but the Axou resent defending the territory alone, will give ground under attack, and want trods there forbidden for fear of the vallorn.

r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Leen Rarckan: The civil service judged that Axos might join a Sanath campaign only if promised a region such as Leen Rarckan, where they would likely exile the inhabitants and rebuild it to their own design.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Bendol is visible from the highest towers of the new Axou citadel, sharpening Axou anxiety about the vallorn on their doorstep.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Axou are rapidly remodelling the Tower of the Skink into a citadel-settlement, possibly to be renamed New Solokah, sacrificing much of its defensive strength, while constant fighting slows its garrison and Skopos insists Thornfen matters go through his office.

388YE Autumn Beoraidh ambassador briefin.d: Beoraidh's ambassador, Rubhart (Kaltrin), declined to introduce the Empire to Sarcophan diplomats working the Delves. Rubhart corrected the view that the Grendel are 'old oppressors': Beoraidh has no wish to rejoin them, but they are not enemies. Beoraidh welcomed the General Assembly's support for a basilica, though the civil service suspect Sarcophan money behind the Aghnayadh Apothecaries' offer to buy the land. Beoraidh tolerates Imperial spying only on outsiders. Rubhart asked for written assurance that no large-scale curse except Rivers of Life will be cast on Mareave without Beoraidh's consent, and promised the same in return. Three thrones would buy six magical plants from Sinfoyard. Without Senate funding for an embassy, future briefings cannot continue.

n.Grendel: Beoraidh insisted the Grendel are not its enemies even though it will not rejoin them, and Rubhart hinted that Grendel and Sarcophan agents already spy on each other in the city. The civil service suggested Beoraidh could become a vantage point for watching Grendel politics while the Grendel keep trading there.

t.Mareave: Beoraidh asked that no large-scale curse other than Rivers of Life be raised over Mareave without its prior agreement. It named Rivers Run Red, Winter's Ghosts and Naeve's Twisting Blight as examples that would harm relations and lead to claims for reparations.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: The city-state welcomed the planned basilica and wants espionage there aimed only at outsiders. The civil service warned that Sarcophan and Grendel agents are already active in the city and will likely watch Imperial fleets once the dock investment draws more of them.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Since recent Spring magic, Sinfoyard's farms and herb gardens have begun producing magical plants, giving this long-arid region valuable produce that farmers now sell in Beoraidh. Six of these plants were offered to the Ambassador for three thrones.

388YE Autumn Commonwealth ambassador bri.d: Ludkhannah Schöningen resigned in disgrace. Her successor, Militärattache Otto Fuchsbach, accused the Empire of betraying the Commonwealth's trust by spying on it and exposing Cold Sun's origins to Jarm. He gave the Empire one season before sharing proof with Jarm that Imperial citizens supplied the mana Eva Giersan used. The Commonwealth will stay in the Liberty Pact but attend no meetings. It accepted a forced ceasefire with Jarm and began offering contracts to Imperial captains against Cold Sun. Commonwealth magicians trapped at the Lyceum have gone home, though few new ones came. Highguard may strengthen ties, possibly at Cyrus's expense.

n.Grendel: The Grendel still hold Professor Gelberg prisoner. Freeing him would help Highborn–Commonwealth ties, but the Grendel know his worth, so ransoming him would be costly and he is now well guarded.
n.Highguard: Highguard has a chance to strengthen ties with the Commonwealth military, building on Professor Gelberg's work. A Highborn Assembly statement condemning Ambassador Cyrus in virtuous terms would secure this, as would securing Gelberg's release.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the nation is not named directly, but the Lyceum discussed in the briefing lies in Madruga, which it holds.

t.Madruga: Through the Gates of Shadow, the Commonwealth magicians trapped at the Lyceum in Madruga have gone home, though few new ones have arrived. The civil service warned that the Commonwealth's privileged access could allow espionage or sabotage, while noting there is no evidence of such plans.

388YE Autumn Equinox Imperial elections.d: Senators were chosen for Casinea, Hahnmark, Kahraman, Morrow, Semmerholm, Tassato, Upwold and Volodmartz. The Senate appointed ambassadors to Axos, the Grendel and the Sarcophan Delves, nine army generals and many other stewards and keepers. The Synod returned Dagon Barossa as Cardinal of Loyalty with 304 votes and Jedediah Boon as Cardinal of Pride, along with several inquisitors and other judgements. The Military Council named Arturo di Sarvos Imperial Warcaster and filled the strategos posts for the League, Varushka and Wintermark. Bourse seats were auctioned or voted on, with Edd taking the Singing Caves on 882 votes. Ashborn Trosk and Nos Umbral Path declared candidacy for Archmage of Autumn and Imperial Censor.

n.Dawn: Aurianna du Meravon was elected to represent Dawn's territory of Semmerholm in the Senate.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Senate appointed Damian den Mhuir di Tassato-Mestra as the Empire's Ambassador to the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Asael was elected Senator for Highguard's territory of Casinea.
n.The Brass Coast: Velasco i Guerra was elected Senator for Kahraman, representing the Brass Coast in the Senate.
n.The League: Narciso Sybilo di Nessuno won the Senate seat for Tassato, and Vincenzo d'artevier de sarvos was appointed Strategos of the League.
n.The Marches: Honest Bobby Boarbridge was elected Senator for the Marcher territory of Upwold.
n.Urizen: Ismene of the Scarlet Guard was elected Senator for Urizen's territory of Morrow.
n.Varushka: Desilav Sergeyevich Jesen was elected Senator for Volodmartz, and Milo Caslav was appointed Strategos of Varushka.
n.Wintermark: Bronn Dunwolf was elected Senator for Hahnmark, and Verdehil was appointed Strategos of Wintermark.

t.Casinea: Asael was elected as Casinea's Senator.
t.Hahnmark: Bronn Dunwolf was elected as Hahnmark's Senator.
t.Kahraman: Velasco i Guerra was elected as Kahraman's Senator.
t.Morrow: Ismene of the Scarlet Guard was elected as Morrow's Senator.
t.Semmerholm: Aurianna du Meravon was elected as Semmerholm's Senator.
t.Tassato: Narciso Sybilo di Nessuno was elected as Tassato's Senator.
t.Upwold: Honest Bobby Boarbridge was elected as Upwold's Senator.
t.Volodmartz: Desilav Sergeyevich Jesen was elected as Volodmartz's Senator.

388YE Autumn Equinox Military Council or.d: Thirty-two armies received orders. In the Salt Flats, the Towerjacks sought to be first through the gates of Iskrid, the Druj capital, and the Northern Eagle moved to secure Beladrarsh. In Reinos, Brass Coast, League, Imperial Orc, Navarr and Wintermark armies attacked the Jotun, with the Red Wind Corsairs raiding Ribeira. In Mareave, seven armies stood against the Grendel, led by the Eastern Sky calling on the Mistress of Blizzards. In Bregasland, Marcher armies stood shoulder to shoulder, supported by healers and the Golden Sun's heroic stand. Elsewhere, the Granite Pillar defended Zenith, the Black Thorns reinforced Astolat and the Drakes stayed in Madruga. Only the Seventh Wave and Golden Axe offered supporting units a share of the Guerdon.

n.Dawn: Dawn split its four armies: the Eastern Sky defended Mareave under its new general Olivia Lucentia, and the Golden Sun made a heroic stand in Bregasland. The Gryphon's Pride and Lions of Adelmar pressed the Druj in the Salt Flats, the Lions with the aim of letting Dawn see the sea again.
n.Druj: Nine Imperial armies descended on the Druj-held Salt Flats of Sanath. They included overwhelming assaults aimed at Iskrid and a Varushkan push to end the Skinweavers' rule in Beladrarsh.
n.Grendel: Seven Imperial armies gathered in Mareave to meet an expected Grendel invasion, with Orc generals vowing to bleed the Grendel for every inch they tried to claim.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar held Zenith and the Pilgrim's Defiance protected innocents in the Salt Flats. The Seventh Wave defended Mareave with a share of the Guerdon, and the Valiant Pegasus tended the fallen in Bregasland.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm and Winter Sun defended the Orc homeland of Mareave against the Grendel, the latter with hit-and-run tactics. The Autumn Hammers marched through Kahraman to conquer Jotun land in Reinos.
n.Jotun: Seven Imperial armies attacked Reinos, including a Brass Coast raid on Ribeira, while six armies held Bregasland against Jotun counterattack.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns withdrew to reinforce Astolat, leaving Therunin to wait, and the Quiet Step joined the overwhelming assault on the Salt Flats. The Star Forged fought alongside Wintermark's Narwhal's Spear in Reinos.
n.The Brass Coast: Aracelis i Erigo handed the Burning Falcon to Shivana i Erigo for a triumphant charge into Reinos, and the Red Wind Corsairs raided Ribeira's wagons. The Fire of the South stood in defence of the Unshackled in Mareave.
n.The League: The Sparrows Reckoning sought conquest in Reinos and the Towerjacks aimed to be first through the gates of Iskrid in the Salt Flats. The Wolves of War defended Mareave.
n.The Marches: The Bounders, Strong Reeds and Tusks stood shoulder to shoulder to hold Bregasland against the Jotun. The Drakes remained in Madruga while their general urged them to come home.
n.Urizen: The Argent Sword marched from Zenith to defend Mareave. The Citadel Guard called down Winter's Mantle on the Druj in the Salt Flats.
n.Varushka: All three Varushkan armies struck the Salt Flats: the Boyar's Hasta plundered, seeking a black lotus, and the Golden Axe joined the overwhelming assault with a share of the Guerdon. The Northern Eagle moved to secure Beladrarsh.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks tended the fallen in Bregasland. The Green Shield and Narwhal's Spear fought with honour in Reinos, the latter partnering Navarr's Star Forged.

t.Astolat: Navarr's Black Thorns marched from the Salt Flats to give Astolat a desperate reinforcement.
t.Bregasland: Six armies held Bregasland: three Marcher armies shoulder to shoulder, Dawn's Golden Sun in a heroic stand, and Highguard's Valiant Pegasus and Wintermark's Bloodcloaks tending the fallen.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Aracelis i Erigo recalled the Burning Falcon claiming Feroz from Rahab in a single season.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks' general recalled the long march since they retook their homes in Holberg.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Autumn Hammers marched south through Kahraman on their way to Reinos.
t.Madruga: The Marcher army the Drakes remained in Madruga, standing shoulder to shoulder there, while the Star Forged left Madruga for Reinos.
t.Mareave: Seven armies defended Mareave against the expected Grendel invasion: five in solid defence, the Winter Sun with hit-and-run tactics and the Eastern Sky embracing the storm.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar's general recalled fighting from the Mournwold, and the Bounders invoked John of the Mourn.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Boyar's Hasta marched from Ossium to plunder the Salt Flats.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave's general urged the army to remember the refugees of Reikos.
t.Reinos: Seven armies attacked Jotun-held Reinos, combining steady conquest, a triumphant charge, a daring raid and Wintermark fighting with honour.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Nine armies converged on the Salt Flats: overwhelming assaults aimed at Iskrid, Dawnish pushes, plunder, Winter's Mantle, protection of innocents and an attempt to secure Beladrarsh.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar's general recalled fighting as far east as the Sarangrave.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky's previous general is referred to as the Star of Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Aracelis i Erigo recalled the Burning Falcon running across the ice of Sermersuaq.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe marched from Therunin, and the Black Thorns' general said Therunin would wait.
t.Zenith: Highguard's Granite Pillar mounted a strategic defence of Zenith, while four other armies departed Zenith for Mareave and the Salt Flats.

r.Mareave/Icarion: The Summer Storm's general warned that the Grendel were trying to get into Icarion and marched back to defend it.
r.Reinos/Ribeira: The Red Wind Corsairs targeted Ribeira's Jotun wagon raiders, and the Sparrows Reckoning named Ribeira as a goal of its conquest.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Beladrarsh: Varushka's Northern Eagle moved to secure Beladrarsh and end the rule of its Skinweavers.

388YE Autumn Equinox Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 834 thrones. Treaties ceded the Bleaks to the Karass, committed five armies to the Suranni conquest at Reinos, and, as amended, pledged war on the vallorn within five years to claim Bendol, with Bloodwater Marsh then ceded to the Nesustak rebels. Weirwater Vales was relinquished and reassigned as a Dawnish Bourse seat. The Palace of Orieb was ceded to Azoth for a year and Remember Exile was sold to Ephisis. Passed commissions included the Hall of the Soturi, the Kallavesa Marshways and the First Voice Glade gardens. Announcements included the Spark of Ignition in Whisperwood, Reeds Redoubt in Bregasland and an Apothecaries Guild effort to cleanse the Lower Tarn Valley.

n.Druj: The Nesustak rebels agreed to root out the remaining Druj hiding among Sarangrave's refugees and later to aid the Empire against them, and Remember Exile was sold to Ephisis on condition it never passes to the Druj.
n.Grendel: Damian den Mhuir di Tassato-Mestra of the League was appointed Ambassador to the Grendel, and Remember Exile was sold to Ephisis on condition it is not sold on to the Grendel.
n.Imperial Orcs: The expansion of Marr's Mine in Mareave, which would have created the Imperial Orc title Patron of Nadir, passed but was later abrogated. The Legion Engineer announced the Garden of Hope, giving the orcs of the Empire a new way to reach Hearkener's Hope.
n.Jotun: Bregasland, held by the Jotun that season, was assigned to the Marches, and an Imperial fortification called Reeds Redoubt was commissioned at Fishers Rock there, though it cannot be funded until the Empire controls the North Fens.
n.Navarr: Asthore Autumngale of Navarr became Ambassador to Axos, and the Senate commissioned the restoration of the Botanical Gardens at the First Voice Glade in Miaren, which the Cat's Graces also refined.
n.Thule: A motion that came from a Thule proposal, requiring the civil service to consult foreign powers holding Imperial land before beneficial magic is used there, failed.
n.Urizen: The Spark of Ignition, a mana sinecure and memorial to those who fell defending Sarangrave, was announced in Whisperwood. The Senate also passed the rebuilding of the Binding Oak Spire and the construction of Kespoena's Nadir in Zenith, and the Breadbasket was pledged to support Urizen's people in Sarangrave.
n.Varushka: The Merchant Boyar kept the Light Market mines at their current level, so mine owners in Miekarova and Volodmartz keep 36 extra rings a season. A Varushkan-funded upgrade of Aleksandra's Watch in Karsk failed, and Emperor Vesna Borkovna Prochnost ratified the relinquishing of Weirwater Vales.
n.Wintermark: The Senate commissioned the Hall of the Soturi in Kallavesa, which will let a new Wintermark army with the unique fearless quality be raised. It also passed the Kallavesa Marshways and the Atalaq Tradehall in Sermersuaq.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland was assigned to the Marches, with its senatorial election set for the Winter Solstice 388YE, and Reeds Redoubt was commissioned at Fishers Rock with Adamant's promised boon.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova's mine owners will keep receiving 36 extra rings a season from the Light Market, and its senator's proposed appraisal with Sadogua failed.
t.Sarangrave: The Empire treated with the Nesustak Forest rebels and declared the Druj's former subjects in Sarangrave foreigners. The Breadbasket will feed Sarangrave for two seasons, and the Spark of Ignition sinecure was announced in Whisperwood.
t.Therunin: The Apothecaries Guild voted unanimously to begin treating the poison in Therunin, with the Benefactor of High Chalcis covering the first season's cost.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz's mine owners will keep receiving 36 extra rings a season from the Light Market, and its senator's appraisal of repairs to the Blood Red Roads and Sunset Roads passed.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: Funding for the Reeds Redoubt commission cannot be provided until the Empire controls the North Fens, and the commission lapses if that condition and a season's funding are not met by the stated deadline.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: The rebels pledged to support the conquest of Bendol, and the amended treaty commits the Empire to begin war against the vallorn within five years with the aim of claiming Bendol.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Under the amended treaty, Bloodwater Marsh will be ceded to the Nesustak Forest rebels once Bendol is claimed, provided this does not cost the Empire dominion.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The rebels of Nesustak Forest became treaty partners of the Empire, promising to secure Sarangrave against the Druj and to leave Imperial movement through their regions unimpeded.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Imperial Breadbasket's produce will go to feeding the people forced out of Thornfen by the Axou.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: The Spark of Ignition, a mana sinecure with the title Lighter of the Forge, was announced in Whisperwood as a memorial to Sarangrave's fallen, funded by Sarangrave Reforged.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Members of the Apothecaries Guild with physick or apothecary skill can join an undertaking to cleanse the poison from the Lower Tarn Valley, supported by herbs redirected from Reikos.

388YE Autumn Equinox Synod judgements.d: Skywise Rykana's change of doctrine passed 2733-54. Navarr's attempt to veto ceding the Last Battle Wayhouse in the Barrens to the Karass failed 0-112. Enacted mandates consecrated Rebellion's Ridge in the Mournwold to Pride, ended the abandoned state of two Feroz regions, sent League bravos to court the Protectorate of Morajasse, staked a Marcher claim to Liathaven and reassured the Freeborn about the Marracossan exiles. A writ to consecrate the Beacons of Sermersuaq to Vigilance was upheld. Many statements of principle were passed, including several seeking friendship with Faraden. The Assembly also issued numerous inquisitions, sanctions and appointments, and the Virtue Fund distributed rewards such as Library funds and weirwood.

n.Dawn: The Dawn Assembly named its Champions of Virtue and asked the civil service to restart the Barrens Roads appraisal, covering the Rahvin and the Great Forest Orcs but not the Karass. It also appointed Tren Meals as Reeve of Greenforest Fair and Tristan Donatien Nicholas Reynauld as Lady of the Proffered Hand.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as the enslavers of the Great Forest Orcs whose rescue was praised, and as former patrons of the Karass.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Freeborn Assembly thanked the Varushkan fleets and vowed to defy the Grendel threatening the Bay.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly sought military advice for a Benefactors Court at Virtue's Rest and pledged support to Great Forest Orcs settling in Reikos. It also entrusted the Relic of Rhonwen to Dagon Nighthaven and backed an effort to destroy the labyrinth spirit threatening Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Doctrine of the Final Challenge, raised by the orc exemplar Skywise Rykana, replaced the Howling Abyss, and the Imperial Orc Assembly urged its people to reject reincarnation. It also sent Firesong Galath to learn about the Jotun ancestors, while a Navarr mandate pledged to share all it could with the orcs for the Vallornguard.
n.Jotun: Judgements celebrated the Jotun retreat from Bregasland and William Guildernstern's slaying of the Summerborn champion Sigrun. A Marcher mandate stirred ambitions to take Liathaven from the Jotun, and an Imperial Orc delegation set out to study their ancestors.
n.Navarr: Navarr's veto of the Karass cession failed, and the Navarr Assembly sent Father Dagda to help the Imperial Orcs prepare for the Vallorn fight. The Courage Assembly honoured the 433 Navarr who helped free the Great Forest Orcs, and Oleander Dreamsreach became Dreamspeaker of Seren.
n.The Brass Coast: A Freeborn mandate reassured the nation about trading with the Marracossan exiles, who will be defended in Madruga if they are persecuted. The Assembly also sought the Kohan's aid against the tyrants at its borders and called Gisli the Provider to inquisition after the magics on Madruga.
n.The League: A League mandate sent bravos to woo the Protectorate of Morajasse, while a rival bid to court Leen failed. The Pride Assembly recognised Lorenzo von Temeschwar as an Exemplar of Pride, pending the General Assembly, and the League Assembly celebrated Sarvos's five sacred sites.
n.The Marches: Rebellion's Ridge was consecrated to Pride, bringing disruption to the Mourn but letting its mine owners elect the next senator, and a Marcher mandate staked a claim to Liathaven. The Marcher Assembly also honoured William Guildernstern as a folk hero and proposed teaching foot-the-ball to Tsark.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are noted as having held the Bloodcloak for a century and as currently holding Varushkan regions.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly welcomed the Proffered Hand's work with the displaced septs of Sarangrave and exalted Orson BogMyrtle, calling for old grudges with the Marches to be buried. It also called Vespasian of Tropaion and Tiberius Stormspire Cascade to inquisition.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Assembly urged the nation to prepare for war while the Thule hold its regions, and imposed penance on Sigismund for a failed command. Its mandate to gather treasures in Tsirku was upheld but had no effect, as it lacked the greater majority Varushka requires.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark entered Nora Falcon's Light into the Chronicle of Heroes and Amberlain's oath into the Forge of Bonds, and celebrated the fearless army to be raised from the Hall of the Soturi. The Synod also upheld a writ to consecrate the Beacons of Sermersuaq, and the Assembly named new places in Tsirku.

t.Bregasland: Amberlain P. Black's oath that the Strong Reeds will never abandon Bregasland was entered into the Forge of Bonds. William Guildernstern's victory over Sigrun in the marshes was celebrated as Marcher folklore.
t.Feroz: A Prosperity mandate lifted the abandoned quality from Afarjasse and Oranseri, but new commissions here will cost four crowns a wain in labour until no region is impoverished. The League also began reaching out to the Protectorate of Morajasse.
t.Kallavesa: The Wintermark Assembly praised the Hall of the Soturi, commissioned to host the army to be raised here, and denied rumours of cruel training. The drum of the scop Theodric Mooting was laid to rest in Kallavesa.
t.Liathaven: A Marcher mandate created an opportunity for the Marches to work towards conquering Liathaven from the Jotun once Bregasland is secure. It also raised a popular expectation that the Marchers will get first claim, though the Senate is not legally bound.
t.Madruga: The Marracossan exiles in Madruga can trade as before, and its people will resist any move against them as if it targeted their Freeborn neighbours. Magics on Madruga prompted inquisitions of Gisli the Provider and Bakar i Riqueza.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Asthore Autumngale is to face inquisition over his time as Senator for Miaren.
t.Mournwold: Rebellion's Ridge was consecrated with true liao to Pride, so personal resources in the Mourn suffer a two-rank penalty for a season, but its mine owners will elect the next senator. Hamma the Lame and Harry the Axe were also called to inquisition.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Bronimir, Senator for Ossium, was issued a writ of inquisition over mustering an army in two seasons.
t.Sermersuaq: The Synod upheld a writ to permanently consecrate the Beacons of Sermersuaq to Vigilance, which the Stormcrows backed in memory of the Jotun invasion. The Wintermark Assembly called for a mediator for the Atalaq tradehall.
t.The Barrens: A veto against ceding the Last Battle Wayhouse to the Karass failed, and a mandate sent pilgrims to the Barrens, creating an opportunity to restore its people's dignity and prosperity. The roads appraisal was ordered to restart, and the Hounds of Glory's final path was recognised as a pilgrimage route.
t.Tsirku: Wintermark named a newly scouted region the Fractured Silence and the Great Pit Firefall. A Varushkan mandate to gather Tsirku's treasures was not enacted, and a condemnation of the Whisper Gallery's agents there was withdrawn.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Afarjasse lost the abandoned quality as a result of the Prosperity mandate encouraging investment in Feroz.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: League bravos will reach out to the Protectorate of Morajasse to try to bring it closer to the League.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Oranseri lost the abandoned quality as a result of the Prosperity mandate encouraging investment in Feroz.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Mentioned in passing: Harry the Axe of Alderly was called to inquisition over Pride, Loyalty and five wains of weirwood.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Mentioned in passing: Rebellion's Ridge was consecrated in memory of the Ore Hills Rebels.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Dawn Assembly asked that the restarted Barrens Roads appraisal include a road to the Rahvin here.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Dawn Assembly asked that the restarted Barrens Roads appraisal include a road to the Great Forest Orcs here.
r.Tsirku/Warriors' Gate: Claude Deeds led a band to Warriors' Gate to free the trapped ghost of the scop Theodric Mooting, a deed rewarded with ten thrones.

388YE Autumn Equinox event schedule.d: Eight nations held Saturday afternoon Senate elections in their camps. Urizen, Wintermark, Dawn, the League, the Marches, the Imperial Orcs, Varushka and the Brass Coast held Tally of the Votes elections for national titles between 3:30pm and 5:30pm. Dusk ran from 19:00 to 20:00. Bows and crossbows were barred in Anvil after 20:00, and Whispers through the Black Gate could only be performed in that hour. The timetable listed Senate, Military Council, Conclave and Synod sessions and deadlines, alongside battles, the Gilded Hammer Auction, a Bond Auction, the Grand Tourney to elect the Knight-protector of Autumn and many citizen-organised meetings.

n.Dawn: Dawn elected Semmerholm's senator at 2:30pm on Saturday, after returning from the grand tourney. At 4pm in Glory Square it elected the Castellan of Spiral Castle, Reeve of Boar's Market, Merchant of the Fangs and Warden of the Weary.
n.Highguard: Highguard elected Casinea's senator at 2pm on Saturday, beginning with an inquisition of the candidates.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs held their Tally of the Votes at the Fire Pit at 5pm. They elected the Sorrowful Tunnels, Legion Engineer, Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting and Bonesetter of the Delving Market titles.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast began its auction for Kahraman's senator at 1pm. At 5:30pm at the Waypoint it elected six titles, including the Quaymaster of the Municipal Docks and Hakima of the Rippling Marshes outside their regular cycles.
n.The League: The League elected Tassato's senator at 3:30pm with a presentation of collected bonds. It elected the Vardstein Vandal at the Plaza at 4pm.
n.The Marches: Upwold's landowners gathered at 1:30pm to elect their senator. At 4:30pm in the Community Hall the Marches elected the Singing Caves, Alder of Meade and Master of the Root and Stem.
n.Urizen: Urizen held a demos from 1pm to 1:30pm to elect Morrow's senator. At 3:30pm near the Net of Heaven it elected the Brilliant Star and Architect of Hammers.
n.Varushka: Varushka began questioning candidates for Volodmartz's senator at 1:45pm. At 5pm at the Central Hearth it elected five titles, including the Bargainer of the Iron Tower and Volhov of the Wyrding Tower.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark placed jars down for 15 minutes at 2pm to elect Hahnmark's senator. At 3:30pm at the Tree of Names it elected the Pride of Ikka's Tears, Keeper of the Runegrott and Kalpaheim Tradeholder.

t.Casinea: Casinea's senator was chosen by Highguard at 2pm on Saturday through an inquisition of candidates.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's senator was chosen by Wintermark at 2pm on Saturday, with jars set down for 15 minutes.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman's Senate seat was put to auction by the Brass Coast from 1pm on Saturday.
t.Morrow: Morrow's senator was elected by a Urizeti demos running from 1pm to 1:30pm on Saturday.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's senator was elected by Dawn at 2:30pm on Saturday, following the grand tourney.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting was among the titles the Imperial Orcs elected at 5pm.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Castellan of Spiral Castle was among the titles Dawn elected at 4pm.
t.Tassato: Tassato's senator was elected by the League at 3:30pm on Saturday through a presentation of collected bonds.
t.Upwold: Upwold's senator was elected by the Marcher landowners, who gathered at 1:30pm on Saturday.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz's senator was elected by Varushka, with the questioning of candidates beginning at 1:45pm on Saturday.

388YE Autumn Equinox interlude.d: The Guerdon stayed at 350 thrones and was shared among units supporting the Burning Falcon, Citadel Guard and Eastern Sky. New or continuing ventures included supporting Thule's White Mountain Fire in Ulnak, rescuing the Great Forest Orcs, scouting Tsirku or sabotaging that scouting for the Whisper Gallery, a treasonous Navarri campaign in Therunin backed by Agramant, a hunt at Treachers Dagger and Swords Against Darkness in Spiral. Fjorknae raiders troubled Marcher and Wintermark shipping, and trade terms with foreign ports were listed. Four lectures were offered to congregations. Enchantments affected Mareave, Ossium, Madruga, Upwold, the Barrens, Sarangrave, Mitwold and Sermersuaq, and three rituals were put forward for Imperial lore.

n.Dawn: Dawnish military units could join the hunt at Treachers Dagger and the Swords Against Darkness venture in Spiral, while an Autumn projection over Dawnguard in the Barrens drew traders and wanderers.
n.Druj: The Druj faced a Thule push into the Forest of Ulnak aimed at Bonewall and the Great Pit, along with a possible Imperial raid to free the Great Forest Orcs. They also faced a Navarri attempt, aided by Agramant, to retake nominally Druj-held Therunin.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page, but it shared Mareave, where Rivers of Life and three Frozen Citadel enchantments were in place.
n.Highguard: Pilgrims answering the Highborn Assembly's call were urged to travel to Bastion to labour on the Grand Inspiration, and units supporting the Citadel Guard in the Salt Flats of Sanath shared the Guerdon.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial orcs could join the effort to rescue the Great Forest Orcs from the Druj, and units supporting the Eastern Sky in Mareave shared the Guerdon.
n.Jotun: The roused Fjorknae harried Marcher and Wintermark shipping in the Gullet. Imperial scouting in Tsirku sought details of any Jotun presence and links to Tromsa and Skallahn.
n.Navarr: Navarri units could support Dochas Weeping Glade's Agramant-backed campaign to retake Therunin, which would be publicised as treason likely to end in execution. Navarr could also join the rescue of the Great Forest Orcs, while Navarr fleets suffered a penalty when trading in Axos.
n.The Brass Coast: Madruga was enchanted with a Night projection that brought strange forest dreams and increased Night activity.
n.The League: League units could fight the threats in Spiral, Temeschwari congregations could preach the Pride of Temeschwar, and Leaguers could convert resources to businesses or upgrade businesses more cheaply.
n.The Marches: Upwold's forges were enchanted with Hammers of Fury to muster a new army and Mitwold was regrown. Marchers could convert resources to farms cheaply, but Marcher fleets suffered from Fjorknae raiders.
n.Thule: Stürmherra's White Mountain Fire pressed into the Forest of Ulnak to claim Bonewall and the Great Pit, and Tathenon the Gyre offered mana crystals to Imperial units supporting it.
n.Urizen: Urizeni units could fight the threats in Spiral, and Urizeni congregations could discuss Prosperity with Adept Camilla and the Adepts of Tsark at Occursion.
n.Varushka: Ossium was enchanted with a Night projection that made its woods disorienting, and Varushkan units avoided the cold penalty when scouting Tsirku.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark units were called to secure Treachers Dagger in the Suaq Wastes, Sermersuaq was regrown and West Marsh received Dripping Echoes of the Fen. Wintermark fleets, however, suffered from Fjorknae raiders.

t.Bastion: Congregations foretelling the Second Age of Virtue would send pilgrims to Bastion to help raise the Grand Inspiration of the Way.
t.Bregasland: Military units supporting the Burning Falcon in Bregasland received shares of the Guerdon.
t.Fjorknae: The Fjorknae were roused, and their ships were active in the Gullet and the northern Sea of Snow, hampering Marcher and Wintermark voyages and trade with Caitun.
t.Forest of Ulnak: The White Mountain Fire campaigned in Ulnak as part of a wider invasion, with Tathenon the Gyre rewarding Imperial units that supported it.
t.Kallavesa: The Sussivari Frost Coven cast Dripping Echoes of the Fen on the West Marsh region.
t.Madruga: Madruga was enchanted with a magnitude 80 Night projection, bringing dreams of a shifting forest and more Night regio and heralds.
t.Mareave: Rivers of Life made Mareave's waters restorative, Frozen Citadel was cast on three of its regions, and units supporting the Eastern Sky there shared the Guerdon.
t.Mitwold: Regrow the Land's Heart brought soft rains and new growth to Mitwold's war scars, and children born or conceived there became more likely to show the briar lineage.
t.Ossium: A magnitude 80 Night projection made Ossium's woods confusing to travel and brought vivid dreams and more Night activity.
t.Otkodov: Stürmherra invoked the Druj fear of Otkodov's high peaks, and Imperial scouts sought any connections between Tsirku and Otkodov.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Units supporting the Citadel Guard there shared the Guerdon. A rescue of the Great Forest Orcs mustering at least 45,000 strength could push into the Salt Flats and the Grove of Woe.
t.Sarangrave: Sarangrave was enchanted with Hand of the Dhomiro, subtly guiding those fleeing or crossing the territory past enemy patrols and protecting small valuables.
t.Sea of Snow: Fjorknae raiding ships were active in the northern Sea of Snow, though fast Marcher and Wintermark ships could outrun them.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was enchanted with Regrow the Land's Heart, and Wintermark and Dawnish units were called to Treachers Dagger in the Suaq Wastes.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: Tsirku scouts at 3,000 strength would report any connections to Skallahn.
t.Spiral: Urizen, League and Dawnish units could attack the threats in Spiral. One more effective season would beat back the horrors of the Black Plateau, and sustained effort could permanently raise the territory's taxation.
t.Temeschwar: With Virtue's Respite remade and the Pride of Temeschwar raised, Temeschwari congregations could preach Pride in their city's history.
t.The Barrens: A magnitude 80 Autumn projection on Dawnguard drew traders and wanderers to Drycastle and the surrounding region.
t.Therunin: Dochas Weeping Glade's settlement of survivors, aided by Agramant, sought to retake the nominally Druj-held territory with treasonous Navarri support.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: Tsirku scouts at 3,000 strength would report any connections to Tromsa.
t.Tsirku: The Tsirku scouting network turned north after exploring Warriors' Gate, while the Whisper Gallery paid units to sabotage the scouting.
t.Upwold: Hammers of Fury enchanted Upwold's forges to speed the mustering of a new army, cutting each mine's ingots by two in exchange for warm ashes.

r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: The Sussivari Frost Coven cast Dripping Echoes of the Fen on West Marsh.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Phoenix Rising cast Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae on Clisearn.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Phoenix Rising cast Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae on Icarion.
r.Mareave/Nadir: Phoenix Rising cast Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae on Nadir.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: a ritual called The Arc of Sküld was put forward for Imperial lore by Yarvi Swiftwind for the Silver Chalice.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Hunters were sent against the servants of Agramant guarding the Winter regio of Treachers Dagger. With 5,000 strength the guardians would be scattered and the regio could be permanently severed.
r.Tsirku/Warriors' Gate: Warriors' Gate had been explored by the Tsirku scouting network, which was now heading north towards Sydanjaa.

388YE Autumn Equinox winds of fortune.d: Emperor Vesna addressed the Empire, and several assemblies pursued their highest callings. The Marches expanded the Imperial Breadbasket into the Mournwold. The League reached out to the Sand Fishers. The Brass Coast turned to defending its lands. Dawn and Navarr prepared for the final war against the vallorn. An Imperial army vanished in Madruga, while husks, Druj and the Kroll troubled Sarangrave. Night magic washed over Ossium, and a new star appeared above Anvil's regio. Professor Gelberg was kidnapped by Grendel at Couros Field. The Silver Flame abandoned its fane plans and sought farm rituals. Tsark invited Imperials to speak on Prosperity in Zenith. The Blades of the Semmerlak commission was reappraised.

n.Dawn: Dawn's highest calling prepares its people for the final war against the vallorn, and Greenwood Manor has been thrown open to all comers. A Dawnish knightly estate is proposed for the Blades of the Semmerlak.
n.Druj: The Druj are scattered through Sarangrave alongside rampaging husks, threatening to stir the Kroll. Their raiders failed to kidnap Lenna Karass, Prilak Gutdredger was killed, and the Fetid Heart in Ghul'thak Forest was not taken.
n.Grendel: Grendel assassins drove Imperials out of Couros Field and kidnapped Professor Gelberg. Elsewhere, Grendel were wiped out at Isaac's End, poisoned in Fleisardh and defeated at Frithstan's Fen, and they still compete with the Empire for the Bay of Catazar.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly set out its stance on the Grand Inspiration of the Way and offered peerless kinship to Wintermark. Navarr shared its vallorn expertise with Highguard, and Highborn advisors joined the Unshackled approach to the Dreamers of the Dark Forest.
n.Imperial Orcs: Pursuing their highest calling of seeking the ancestors of other septs, an Unshackled delegation led by Bloodcrow Meep received a guarded welcome from the Dreamers of the Dark Forest in Ossium, and with it a new dilemma for the Empire.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Marcher interest in Imperial steel sweeping into Jotun-held Bregasland is noted, as is a mildly irritating development concerning Liathaven/Ashvale.
n.Navarr: Seren has become the City of Dreams, giving rise to the dreamspeaker calling, and Thornsong refugees propose a new apothecary college. Navarr's highest calling supports the Vallornguard, while Agramant makes a pointed offer over the reconquest of Therunin.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Assembly made defending their lands their highest calling. Feroz was chosen by the Prosperity Assembly for help, and an Imperial army vanished in the Night-touched marshes of Madruga.
n.The League: The League's highest calling saw its princes reach out to the Sand Fishers of Misericorde. Apulian orcs and League Synod members made a pilgrimage to the Mournwold and were warmly welcomed.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly completed its highest calling by expanding the Imperial Breadbasket into the Mournwold and now weighs how to own and defend land. It also hosted League pilgrims and awaits the General Assembly's decision on Rebellion's Ridge.
n.Thule: The Thule of Otkodov remain at uneasy peace with the Empire while warring on the Druj and conquering western Ulnak. Their envoys negotiate over upcoming events in Ossium, and an attempt by the Eyes of the Dragon to use a boon of Kimus at Islet of Calm was prevented.
n.Urizen: Urizeni captains and Sarangrave residents face husks, Druj, famine and the threat of the Kroll. Members of the Urizen Assembly helped persuade the Tsarkoi adept Camilla of the value of Prosperity.
n.Varushka: Varushkan Ossium was washed by mixed Night magic blessings, and Varushkan advisors aided the Unshackled. A wardenhouse is proposed for the Blades of the Semmerlak, and the Sumisev Peegel in Volodmartz was destroyed.
n.Wintermark: Runegrott artisans propose a banner edifice and a new artefact banner to replace Foe-Slayer, and the Mystics of Ishal have reshaped their support for the Raven Seer. Wintermark explorers pressed into Tsirku, where Wemba the Bloody is loose, and Highguard offered peerless kinship.

t.Astolat: An effort to stop Igraine's Regio shifting back to Spring had an unclear result, though Éamon Ashenmourn de Cordraco might know more.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: its senator is flagged over Ephisis' contracts, and its congregations are noted in connection with Gelberg's appraisal.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are noted as competing with the Empire for dominance of the Bay.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Imperial steel is described as sweeping through Mitwold and into Bregasland.
t.Casinea: After the Summer Solstice, an awareness rippled out from the Imperial regio at Anvil, heralding a new star in the sky.
t.Feroz: The Prosperity Assembly chose Feroz, still scarred by Governor Rahab, as the first damaged territory to help, and a Freeborn architect has a pitch for doing so.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Forge the Wooden Fastness was cast at Moss End and the Eyes of the Dragon were thwarted at Islet of Calm, but the raid on the Fetid Heart was not taken. The Thule have been conquering western Ulnak.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the territory is linked only through Wintermark's wider national winds.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: its citizens are flagged as interested in the contracts offered by the City of Gold and Lead.
t.Holberg: The League reached out to the Sand Fishers living on Holberg's northern shores, and the Senator for Holberg is among those expecting visitors in Anvil.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: its constant invasions by the Lasambrians are cited as a reason for the Freeborn's sense of vulnerability.
t.Kallavesa: The Meeting Place in West Marsh was consecrated with true liao, and an Iontach was rescued from the Grendel in Wittal Grove. The people of Kallavesa are also flagged in offers from Sadogua and Ephisis.
t.Karov: The port of Korotny in Malimorzi is one possible site for the Varushkan wardenhouse of the proposed Blades of the Semmerlak.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: anyone with an interest in Liathaven/Ashvale is pointed to a mildly irritating development with a former Imperial territory.
t.Madruga: Night magic brought dreams of vanished forests, and one of two Imperial armies claiming the Siroc Bayou and Crucible has disappeared. The Snapping Face was retrieved, and the fate of a stranded Sumaah ship remains unclear.
t.Mareave: The Saltbound Stone was recovered from the Ruins of Sinat and the Grendel were poisoned in Fleisardh. Moves were made towards building a temple to the Way in neutral Beoraidh.
t.Miaren: With the Temple of the Waking Dream complete, Seren has become the City of Dreams and draws dreamers and displaced Thornsong apothecaries.
t.Mitwold: Jyll Longleys was stopped from cursing the Maiden Stone and Dusty Cobb from burning the Golden Fields, as Imperial steel swept through the territory.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: people with congregations in Morrow are flagged as interested in Gelberg's appraisal.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Tsark's Sage's Council has warmed to the idea of Prosperity, and the adept Camilla seeks inspirational Imperial figures to learn from.
t.Mournwold: The Imperial Breadbasket was expanded into the Mournwold, whose orcs welcomed League pilgrims. The General Assembly must now decide on consecrating Rebellion's Ridge as a memorial.
t.Necropolis: The waters of Siakha were spilled at the Veiled Garden and the bucket returned to Anvil, and local congregations are flagged in Gelberg's appraisal.
t.Ossium: Night magic from the Wondrous Forest brought mixed blessings amid lurking monsters, and an Unshackled delegation met the Dreamers of the Dark Forest. A curse on Ossium was prevented at Burned Glade, and Bittershore is a candidate wardenhouse site.
t.Otkodov: The Thule of Otkodov keep an uneasy peace with the Empire and are negotiating deals, including over upcoming events in Ossium.
t.Redoubt: Every Grendel at Isaac's End in Naris was killed. Redoubt congregations are also flagged in connection with Gelberg's appraisal.
t.Reikos: Grendel pushed Imperials out of Couros Field and kidnapped Professor Gelberg. Thornsong apothecaries who fled to Reikos are behind the new college proposal.
t.Sarangrave: Husks remain in the east after spirits at the Fens of Varreth went untrapped, and famine and the Kroll loom. Wards were cast in Bloodwater Marsh, but vallornspawn persist in Bendol.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: noted as only recently enjoying quiet after nearly two decades of warfare.
t.Semmerholm: Lacuve near Lacre is a candidate site for the Dawnish knightly estate of the Blades of the Semmerlak, and its senator proposed the Journeymage Towers.
t.Spiral: The Silver Flame of Cinion abandoned its fane for Sinokenon and now asks for farm rituals in return for defending Spiral. Mercenaries' pay at Alba's Lea was raided, with ten wains of mithril claimed.
t.Tassato: Heralds of Siakha and wreckers were killed at Campo Verdenta, and the Senator for Tassato is among those expecting visitors in Anvil.
t.The Barrens: Prilak Gutdredger and the manticore's vassals were killed, Lenna Karass was rescued, and Ser Gawain Amboise's schemes were thwarted. Most of the Servants of the Burnt survived.
t.The Semmerlak: The reappraised Blades of the Semmerlak would create a sodality and a Knight-Warden title to remove the threat of Dho'uala to ships and lakeside communities.
t.Therunin: Agramant still lurks in Therunin with a new offer to aid its reconquest. The miasma pillar at Rotwood Croft was consecrated, and the loss of Thornsong House is recalled.
t.Tsirku: Wintermark-led scouts continued exploring Tsirku, where Agramant's follower Wemba the Bloody is loose and further surprises await.
t.Upwold: Magistrates found no evidence for the rumour that Brother Orchard had put heads on pikes in the Upwold.
t.Volodmartz: The Sumisev Peegel in Livardz was destroyed with Wind of Mundane Silence.
t.Weirwater: Sandling near Culwich is a candidate site for the Dawnish knightly estate of the Blades of the Semmerlak.
t.Zenith: Eleven Imperials are invited to the Gardens of the Perfect World to speak on inspirational figures of Prosperity before the Tsarkoi.

r.Astolat/Withy: The attempt to stop Igraine's Regio shifting back to Spring had an unclear result.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Mentioned in passing: a Morajasse section was added to the Grendel diplomatic wind.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest: The raid on the Fetid Heart was not taken, leaving the black lotus and Taramid Skinwreath's treasures of unclear status.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Gloomsea: At the Islet of Calm, Wind of Mundane Silence was cast on the regio and the bodies destroyed, stopping the Eyes of the Dragon from using a boon of Kimus.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire: Acting on a scouting discovery, Forge the Wooden Fastness was cast at Moss End with eight rings of ilium.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: The League's princes reached out to the Sand Fishers of Misericorde about joining the Empire.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Erlend consecrated the Meeting Place with true liao.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: The Grendel were defeated at Frithstan's Fen and the Iontach Meddool Miniog was rescued and returned to Anvil.
r.Karov/Malimorzi: The port of Korotny is a candidate site for the Varushkan wardenhouse of the Blades of the Semmerlak.
r.Madruga/Crucible: An Imperial army was claiming the Crucible's marshes, one army has since vanished, and the Snapping Face was retrieved at Talpses Plat.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The effort to aid a stranded Sumaah ship at Hart's Cove had an unclear result; the Hand of Guerra should know more.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: Imperial armies were claiming the Siroc Bayou's wild marshes, and one of the two never came back out.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Movement has been made towards building a temple to the Way in the neutral free port of Beoraidh.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: The Vaults at the Ruins of Sinat were opened, the Saltbound Stone claimed by Terentia of Sarangrave Reforged, and the Ilium Jackals negotiated with.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: Grendel were poisoned from the Spring regio near Golden Wind's Encampment.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Mentioned in passing: noted as recognised, with Beoraidh, as a neutral state by the Senate.
r.Mitwold/Maiden Downs: Jyll Longleys was killed before cursing the Maiden Stone, and Dusty Cobb's rebels were killed before burning the Golden Fields.
r.Mountains of the Moon/Visoko: Mentioned in passing: shrines to great Tsarkoi sages are built into the Wall of the Luge around the sacred plateau of Visoko.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Mentioned in passing: the Leaders of the Ore Hills Rebellion would be memorialised by the proposed consecration of Rebellion's Ridge.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: The waters of Siakha were spilled at the Veiled Garden and the bucket was returned to Anvil.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: The Kostjyas Respite is a candidate site for the Varushkan wardenhouse of the Blades of the Semmerlak.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Heralds were killed at Burned Glade and Ossium was not cursed.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Telemachus's forces killed every Grendel at Isaac's End.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: Mentioned in passing: some Thornsong apothecaries stayed on Chalcis Mount after fleeing Therunin.
r.Reikos/Haros Water: Grendel assassins pushed Imperials out of Couros Field and kidnapped Professor Gelberg.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: The attempt to drive the vallorn from the Spring regio cost Imperial lives and vallornspawn remain, and Dance of Navarr and Thorn was not performed.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Permanent wards were cast at both the Eastern and Western Wards.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: Heralds at Slow Worm's Hill were killed and Sarangrave was not cursed, though the Kroll's threat looms.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: Mentioned in passing: the Empire has been trying to make diplomatic inroads with the rebels of Nesustak Forest.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Axou eviction of so many from Thornfen has raised the spectre of famine in Sarangrave.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: The spirits at the Fens of Varreth were not trapped, leaving husks and Het Trakaa's tortured souls, but treasure was recovered at the Breakteeth dais.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: Heralds of Surut were killed at Halfweir Grove, raising Fingers of the Devourer production, and the Depths of the Hungry Earth were investigated.
r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: Lacuve near Lacre is a candidate site for the Dawnish knightly estate of the Blades of the Semmerlak.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: A raid on the Legacy at Alba's Lea saw ten wains of mithril claimed by the Haurlatch Iron Consortium.
r.Spiral/Cinion: The Silver Flame of Cinion sent Sinokenon's heralds away and now seek farm rituals, offering their sentinels for Spiral's defence.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Mentioned in passing: the Steward of the Ossuary is flagged in the Beoraidh diplomatic wind.
r.Tassato/Cascatas: Heralds of Siakha and wreckers were killed at Campo Verdenta.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Answering General Utmar's call at Saltshore, Imperials killed the manticore's vassals.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Prilak Gutdredger and almost all his allies were killed at Troubadour's Glade.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: All but one of the Servants of the Burnt survived at the Dredging Flats, but Lenna Karass was rescued from Druj raiders at Gardenway.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: Ser Gawain Amboise's schemes were thwarted at the Glade of the Good Knight.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Reclaimed by the Golden Axe last season, the valley saw the miasma pillar at Rotwood Croft consecrated.
r.Volodmartz/Livardz: The Sumisev Peegel was destroyed by Wind of Mundane Silence.
r.Weirwater/Sandling: Sandling near Culwich is a candidate site for the Dawnish knightly estate of the Blades of the Semmerlak.
r.Zenith/Occursion: The Gardens of the Perfect World will host eleven Imperials and Sage Kristoph to discuss figures of Prosperity with the Tsarkoi.

388YE Autumn Equinox winds of war.d: As Summer faded, the Strong Reeds rose against the Jotun in Bregasland. Imperial and Grendel armies kept fighting over Mareave while Beoraidh looked on. The Golden Axe entered Therunin's poisoned Tarn Valley, and the Axou of Thornfen guarded the Sarangrave against Winter spirits. Four battle opportunities were offered, two to be chosen by the Military Council: Mareave against the Grendel, the Forest of Ulnak, Bregasland and the Salt Flats of Sanath. Conjunctions spanned the Empire, from Janon heralds cursing territories to Mirk Lizards and coral husks. Six conjunctions targeted small Druj raiding bands in tunnels, set on poisoning wells, sabotaging a mine and undermining a fortress.

n.Dawn: Dawn brought the second-largest force weight (66). The Strategos of Dawn was charged with stopping Druj well-poisoners at Endsfell, and Dawnish armies could use Triumphant Charge but not Steady Conquest against the Druj until Summer 389YE.
n.Druj: The Druj grew desperate as Imperial armies pushed into the Mallum, sending small suicidal raiding bands through tunnels to poison wells, burn and sabotage. They also faced battle opportunities in the Forest of Ulnak and the Salt Flats of Sanath.
n.Grendel: Grendel armies continued their long struggle with the Empire for Mareave. The Collapse the Tunnels battle opportunity was offered against them at Syagrian Haven in Icarion.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Strategos was tasked with dealing with a strange, ghost-haunted Druj incursion beneath an abandoned chapterhouse in Reikos, and a mysterious tomb in Necropolis was to be investigated. Highborn armies carried special rules, including a penalty for calling eternal heralds to fight alongside them.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: listed with a force weight of 6 for the battle opportunities and noted as able to take the Forge Hammers order in Skarsind.
n.Jotun: The Jotun faced a Marcher uprising in Bregasland after holding it for some time. They were the opposition for the Treat with Enemies battle opportunity, and conjunctions sought to intercept their supplies.
n.Navarr: With a force weight of 56, Navarr featured in Therunin, where heroes could rescue the popular guide Idwynn Summersong from Druj raiders. Druj raiders also threatened the water of Caedwynn's Hold, the new Navarr Wayhouse in the Barrens.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn titles were made responsible for several conjunctions, from stopping Janon heralds cursing Kahraman to raids in Bregasland. The Burning Falcon and Fire of the South carried special order rules tied to the Knights of Glory enchantment.
n.The Marches: The Strong Reeds rose with their allies to try to free Bregasland from the Jotun. Marcher armies kept their strength bonuses in their home territories, and any Imperial army could billet in Mitwold, Mournwold or Upwold.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Imperial soldiers in the north were said to fight alongside the blue-swaddled warlocks of Otkodov, who pursued their own inscrutable goals.
n.Urizen: Urizen interests centred on the Sarangrave, where the Axou of Thornfen guarded the territory and Druj raiders sought to undermine the Tower of the Skink. A cluster of conjunctions also opened in Zenith's Occursion region, and the borders of Morrow and Zenith remained patrolled by their citizens.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe ventured into Therunin's poisoned Tarn Valley, and the Strategos of Varushka had to stop Druj saboteurs in Ossium's mithril mine. Bandits troubled the Bittershore and Mirk Lizards troubled Karsk.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark brought the largest force weight (69) and kept its special rules for fighting the Jotun honourably. Conjunctions in Kallavesa dealt with strange coral husks, and another in Sermersuaq was a chance to attend the Festival of Autumn's Easing.

t.Bregasland: The Strong Reeds and their allies rose against the Jotun occupiers in a season of mud, blood and manacles. A battle opportunity to treat with the enemy was offered here, along with conjunctions against Janon heralds, Jotun supplies and the yegarra.
t.Forest of Ulnak: The Clear the Retreat battle opportunity was offered against the Druj at Reeth Plain, and conjunctions sent heroes to kill Mirk Lizards in Ghul'thak Forest.
t.Kahraman: Janon heralds threatened to curse Kahraman, and the Azure Sutannir was responsible for organising heroes to stop them.
t.Kallavesa: Strange coral husks were lurking in Kallavesa's marshes, with conjunctions to investigate them and to hunt them down.
t.Karsk: A conjunction sent heroes under Romand Reinetova Remislav to kill Mirk Lizards in Moresvah.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven is not discussed directly; the page refers only to the Jotun placing their stamp on conquered land such as Ashvale.
t.Mareave: Imperial and Grendel armies kept clashing over the land that was once Mahal while Beoraidh looked on. The Collapse the Tunnels battle opportunity was offered at Syagrian Haven.
t.Mitwold: Imperial armies could billet in Mitwold, the Drakes gained strength fighting here, and a small conjunction sought to recover an artifact from Sod's Spelunk.
t.Morrow: Morrow's borders remained patrolled by its citizens, so the Druj needed 25 victory points to claim a beachhead, and Highborn or Urizen armies attacking from it into Zenith gained bonuses.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory where any Imperial army could billet and where the Tusks gained extra strength.
t.Necropolis: A conjunction led by Danika Valentine was offered to investigate a mysterious secluded tomb at Coursmouth.
t.Ossium: Druj raiders tried to sabotage the Vale of Sunless Depths, and bandits troubled the Bittershore. The territory's borders remained patrolled by its citizens.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the warlocks of Otkodov were described as battling alongside Imperial soldiers in the north for their own inscrutable goals.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt itself is not discussed on this page.
t.Reikos: A puzzling band of Druj, far from their lands, was found in an abandoned underground chapterhouse haunted by at least one ghost. The Strategos of Highguard was charged with dealing with them.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Empire pushed forward into depthless dark here, with a Sunday battle opportunity against the Druj and conjunctions to kill Huk'nar Skintwister, recover the Chain of the Hammerwright and stop aquifer poisoners.
t.Sarangrave: The Axou of Thornfen protected the territory from Winter spirits loosed by collapsing armies. Conjunctions targeted a Druj column, a Druj spy, the sac of Kroll and raiders beneath the Tower of the Skink.
t.Sermersuaq: Fifty citizens could travel to Tanikipari to attend the Festival of Autumn's Easing.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: noted as where an Imperial Orc army can take the Forge Hammers order.
t.The Barrens: Janon heralds threatened to curse the Barrens, and Druj raiders sought to poison wells near Caedwynn's Hold. Citizen patrols kept the Druj threshold for a beachhead at 25 victory points.
t.Therunin: The Golden Axe ventured into the poisoned Tarn Valley still held by isolated Druj. Druj raiders took Navarr hostages, and a meeting with Dochas Weeping Glade was offered.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory where any Imperial army could billet and where the Bounders gained extra strength.
t.Zenith: A string of conjunctions in Occursion dealt with bandits, creatures, Disciples of Sulemaine and malaised sentinels. The territory's borders remained patrolled against Druj beachheads.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Janon heralds attempted to curse Bregasland from Graven Commons, and the General of the Burning Falcon was responsible for stopping them.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Conjunctions offered the chance to intercept Jotun supplies at Old Jill's Fallow and to claim the wealth of the yegarra on the Short New South Road.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: The Treat with Enemies battle opportunity against the Jotun was offered at Whelkquay.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: Heroes could find out what happened to missing scouts at Potter's Beach and defeat the yegarra at Bella's Bluff.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest: Two conjunctions sent heroes to kill Mirk Lizards at the Butcher Glade and the Razor Thicket.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire: The Clear the Retreat battle opportunity against the Druj was offered at Reeth Plain.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Janon heralds sought to curse Kahraman from Uthman's Field, with the Azure Sutannir responsible for a response.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: The Remembrancer of Blood and Salt was responsible for hunting down and destroying lurking coral husks at Freja's Rest.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: The Raven Seer was responsible for investigating strange coral husks at the Westerhal Fens.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: Heroes could kill Mirk Lizards in the Mirky Vale.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: The neutral city-state of Beoraidh looked on as Imperial and Grendel armies clashed around it.
r.Mareave/Icarion: The Collapse the Tunnels battle opportunity against the Grendel was offered at Syagrian Haven.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: William Guildenstern was named to lead a small party to recover an artifact from Sod's Spelunk.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: A mysterious secluded tomb awaited investigation by a party under Danika Valentine.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Bandits plagued the region, with conjunctions to deal justice at Holstein's Vale, spring a trap at Zhokhov's End and aid an injured patrol at Whisper Copse.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Druj raiders used an old tunnel to sabotage the Vale of Sunless Depths. Failure would kill scores of miners, permanently raise upkeep and cut mithril output by two wains a season until Summer 389YE.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: Druj were discovered in the abandoned underground chapterhouse of Elsbeth's Aegis at Nikal's Redoubt, in a strange encounter where at least one ghost was present.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Lower Saarnath: The Break the Shackles battle opportunity was offered at Rivenglade. Conjunctions targeted Huk'nar Skintwister, the Chain of the Hammerwright and Druj poisoners who could cost the Citadel Guard 200 lives.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: Two conjunctions sent heroes to interact with the sac of Kroll at Snaring Marsh and Shifting Gulch.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The Imperial Spymaster was responsible for identifying and executing a Druj spy at Gizzard's Meadow.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Axou of Thornfen guarded the territory against Winter spirits, while Druj raiders tried to undermine the Tower of the Skink. Failure to stop them would confine the Axou garrison to this region for the season.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: Eighty heroes under the Senator for Sarangrave could destroy a column at Tercia's Bluff.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: The Festival of Autumn's Easing was held at the Shaore of Atkonaroq, with the Mediator of Hyljehal responsible for the visit.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Druj raiders in the caves of Endsfell sought to poison groundwater serving Caedwynn's Hold. Wealthy locals offered four thrones if they were stopped.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Janon heralds sought to curse the Barrens from the Glade of the Rising Sun.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: Eskah Swift Hart was named to meet with Dochas Weeping Glade at the Weeping Glade.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Golden Axe ventured into this poisoned valley. Druj raiders held the Navarr guide Idwynn Summersong hostage in Slatefair Cave, and his rescue would lift Navarr morale.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Seven conjunctions opened here, covering Prosperous inspiration for Tsark, killing Disciples of Sulemaine, fighting bandits and creatures, and helping injured and malaised sentinels.

388YE Autumn Faraden ambassador briefing.d: The Faraden priest families feared renewed Synod persecution of the faith of the five flames, even though the proscription had been repealed. As a result, the proposed Firewind and Moonsong markets were to be treated as on hold, and Yakholme Grange risked becoming a yak market with no yaks. The Tseriyn and Salagiin families, who supply mithril to the Alder of Meade and ilium to the Mediator of Fisk, were under pressure to reconsider their ties. Assembly statements were suggested to reassure them, and the Azure Sutannir might also help, as fewer Faraden pilgrims were attending the Azure Chorus. Faraden had signed peace with the Jotun because Imperial and Suranni support could not be relied upon. The Asaveans had recalled their diplomats over Tomasso Triusti's execution.

n.Dawn: The proposed Moonsong Market in the Barrens, a Dawnish territory, was to be considered on hold until Faraden fears over Synod persecution were resolved.
n.Jotun: The Jotun had signed a peace treaty with Faraden at the Summer Solstice. Under it, neither side would fight the other, borders stayed as they were, and trade provisions were agreed. The Jotun could still take a tithe from Faraden caravans but could not forbid them other routes.
n.The League: The proposed Firewind Market in the League's territory of Holberg was put on hold amid Faraden fears about Synod interference with their traders.
n.The Marches: Two Marcher interests were exposed: the Alder of Meade's mithril supply was under pressure, and Yakholme Grange might lose its Faraden buyers. The civil service suggested that the Marcher assembly reiterate Sister Meredith's earlier statement of principle, while warning that urging defiance of Synod proscriptions would widen the Marches' rift with the General Assembly.
n.Wintermark: The briefing named Wintermark alongside the Marches as a nation whose assembly might be asked to urge people to ignore persecution of Faraden travellers. It warned that this would deepen Wintermark's distance from the General Assembly and could trigger a legal crisis.

t.Holberg: The Faraden proposal to build Firewind Market in Holberg was to be considered on hold, as there was no guarantee it would attract Faraden traders in the current climate.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Kallavesa is not named on the page, which refers to Wintermark only in general terms.
t.Mitwold: The Tseriyn family's supply of mithril, bought in Caitun for the market at Meade, was at risk of being reduced as the family came under pressure to reconsider its ties with the Empire.
t.Reinos: Under the new treaty, Faraden caravans will still pay a tithe to pass through Reinos but may use another route if one becomes available. Imperial reluctance to help conquer Reinos was a key reason Faraden chose peace with the Jotun.
t.The Barrens: The Faraden proposal to build Moonsong Market in the Barrens was to be considered on hold until the religious tensions were resolved.
t.Upwold: Construction of Yakholme Grange was still underway, and the Hakhandra family remained keen on Marcher cattle. However, a worsening situation could leave the Empire with a yak market with no yaks.

r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Mentioned in passing: Wittal Grove is not named on the page, which refers to Wintermark only in general terms.

388YE Autumn Grendel ambassador briefing.d: Prepared for Starlight Starchaser of Urizen, who was succeeded during the summit by Damian den Mhuir di Tassato-Mestra of the League, the briefing relayed Speaker Morna's responses. The Salt Lords refused to let Imperial forces occupy Ayereed but were less definitive about Mareave, where the Fundindelve mithril mine and the Fleisardh-supported Brine Turtles are likely sticking points. Morna suggested a Senate law admitting Grendel pilgrims to sites honouring Barabbas, the Kraken's Bane and newly consecrated Elos might prompt reciprocal invitations, though the civil service warned of espionage. He proposed both sides build embassies in Beoraidh, with the Salt Lords paying for the Imperial one, and asked after the missing iontach Leagsaidh Saim-garoth. Without funding, no further briefings can be prepared.

n.Grendel: The Salt Lords rejected the Empire's demands over Mareave and Ayereed, but offered to fund a matching Imperial embassy in Beoraidh, hinted at reciprocal pilgrimages, and demanded word on their missing healer Leagsaidh Saim-garoth.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Necropolis, home to the tomb of Barabbas, was named as a likely destination for Grendel pilgrims, which the civil service warned could also provide cover for Grendel spies.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast's Madruga was named among the territories Grendel pilgrims would visit, with the consecration of Elos having left Speaker Morna surprisingly positive, though the civil service warned of espionage risks.
n.The League: Damian den Mhuir di Tassato-Mestra of the League took over as Ambassador to the Grendel during the summit, and the Salt Lords showed little enthusiasm for an embassy in the League city of Sarvos.
n.Urizen: Starlight Starchaser of Urizen presented the proposals as ambassador before being succeeded at the summit, and Urizen's Redoubt was named among the territories Grendel pilgrims might be allowed to visit.

t.Ayereed: The Salt Lords declared there was absolutely no chance they would allow Imperial forces to occupy Ayereed, calling the request ludicrous.
t.Madruga: Madruga was listed among the territories Grendel pilgrims might freely visit under a proposed Senate law, a prospect the civil service warned would ease Grendel espionage there.
t.Mareave: The Grendel refused to cede Mareave but left the door ajar for negotiation, with the Fundindelve mithril mine and the Brine Turtles likely central, while an iontach healer went missing after Summer fighting there tied to an Uthni contract.
t.Necropolis: The tomb of Barabbas made Necropolis a proposed pilgrimage destination for Grendel, with the civil service cautioning that pilgrims could provide cover for spies.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt was named among the territories Grendel pilgrims might visit if the Senate passed a pilgrimage law, raising concerns about Grendel espionage there.
t.Sarvos: Speaker Morna was notably unenthusiastic about an Imperial offer to build a Grendel embassy in Sarvos, which the civil service took as a sign the Salt Lords now fear Imperial espionage.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Speaker Morna proposed that both the Empire and the Grendel build embassies in neutral Beoraidh, an idea Ehsan reportedly embraced to secure his city-state's status and prestige.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: The Fleisardh sept supports the Grendel army the Brine Turtles, whose future would likely need resolving before the Grendel would consider giving up Mareave.

388YE Autumn Iron Confederacy ambassador.d: With the Children of Wrecks dealt with, Baroness Lavasse sent Ser Marquette and Marquise Katerine Lavasse to Anvil to negotiate a treaty, which the Senate ratified. Talks were expected to cover Suranni holdings in the Brass Coast, which they would not surrender, and their invasion of the Lasambrian Hills. The dukes offered Imperial warbands a chance to fight alongside Baron Hendrick in Reinos, possibly as a test. Duke Harold Guiscard asked for help against the Hand of Dumon after a further curse on Kalino. Baroness Lavasse asked about Brother Luke, who was later fined ten thrones and branded, an outcome the Suranni may see as a miscarriage of justice.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Arbonne is described as a wealthy province next to its territory of Feroz.
n.Jotun: Three Jotun armies of the Lasambrian Hills were reportedly putting up significant resistance to the Suranni invasion, which threatened the Hierro and the Corazón. The dukes invited Imperial warbands to fight against them, and the civil service warned of the Suranni's poor record with captured orcs.
n.The Brass Coast: The Iron Confederacy's holdings in the Brass Coast were expected to feature in treaty talks, though the Suranni had made clear they would not give up conquered land. The Freeborn Synod assembly was judged too distracted by its highest calling to help against the Hand of Dumon.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Arbonne is noted as lying next to Feroz and controlling the overland trade routes into the heart of the Empire.
t.Kalino: Known to the Suranni as Arbonne, Kalino was cursed again by the Hand of Dumon. A warding temple built partly with Imperial ilium spared the Autumn harvest, and Duke Harold Guiscard sought Imperial help to find the culprits.
t.Madruga: The Suranni conquests here were expected to come up in treaty negotiations, but the Iron Confederacy remained unwilling to give up land it had taken.
t.Reinos: The Suranni were trying to conquer the Reinos hills against stiff Jotun resistance. The dukes offered Imperial warbands the chance to fight there alongside the brutal Baron Hendrick of the Black Eagle Banner, with a warning that obviously magical forces would anger the Suranni.

r.Madruga/Free Landing: Brother Luke was accused of encouraging Imperial fleet captains to aid the Children of Wrecks in Free Landing. That accusation prompted Baroness Lavasse to ask what had become of him.

388YE Autumn Jarmish ambassador briefing.d: Lord-Magister Anton Trescher praised the Empire for revealing that Commonwealth agents caused Lantir's destruction. The revelation forced the Commonwealth to accept a Jarmish ceasefire. Trescher proposed that a Senate denunciation of the Commonwealth during the Equinox would likely see Vezak and Kavor reopened to Imperial fleets, provided the Senate lifted its own embargo on Jarmish trade. The House of Princes invited Imperial mercenaries to fight Cold Sun. At least 10,000 effective strength would shorten the campaign by a season. The end of trade with Radosmo drew little reaction beyond Prince Mila, who sought to sell Jarmish goods through the City of Gold and Lead. The Celestial Arch and Sevenfold Path remained tolerated in Jarm, though Trescher had begun asking about the Path.

n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the page raises no League matters, and its only apparent link is that the briefing was prepared for Ambassador Thaumiel of Steeplechase Toll.

t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is not named; its only apparent link is the name of the Ambassador, Thaumiel of Steeplechase Toll, for whom the briefing was prepared.

388YE Autumn Sarcophan ambassador briefi.d: Annabele de Gouden of the House of the Jackal needs 70 thrones of investment to keep supplying triumph vis and star jewels, and would welcome a trading sodality like the Court of Far Horizons.
