The Kraft brothers have withdrawn from Hahnmark, ending easy access to vizesmaak, while the Zuredruiven vintners invest in its herb gardens; 5 thrones could secure a sample of an unshared third draaikolkbloem potion. Scholar Catharina Gjullit seeks vallorn-related goods, prompting Sarcophan safety concerns. The Synod's reputation in the Delves is wrecked after Highborn sold religious sculpture, and restoring the Cathedral would be very costly. The Ilium Jackals must be paid by the Boyar's Hasta's general, or passed to the Wolves of War or the Magpies.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: if the Ilium Jackals go unpaid they may seek work around the Bay of Catazar, possibly returning to fight for the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Highborn benefactors' sale of religious sculpture to a heretical Sarcophan group has turned Sarcophan pilgrims against the Synod, and Highguard's plan to send priests to rebuild the Cathedral of the Navigators is regarded by the Sarcophan as a lost cause.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark loses the Kraft brothers' investment and easy access to vizesmaak, but gains Zuredruiven investment in Hahnmark's herb gardens, though the vintners have not shared a third draaikolkbloem potion with Wintermark apothecaries.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: an unpaid Ilium Jackals company would look for other work in the environs of the Bay of Catazar.
t.Hahnmark: Having cut ties with the Kraft brothers in Spring, Hahnmark's farmers saw them withdraw their investment, while the Zuredruiven vintners invest enthusiastically in its herb gardens to grow draaikolkbloem.

388YE Autumn Sumaah ambassador briefing.d: The Republic will answer the Empire's mercantilist tariffs with its own on Imperial imports, felt by the Winter Solstice. Oxtitocszin judged the Wandering Port's prices too high and offered 3 thrones 1 crown a wain for weirwood, 3 thrones 6 crowns for mithril, or one-for-one trades in white granite, for up to 100 wains bought through heralds of the Polyptoton at the Winter Solstice. The High House of Vigilance offered to assess Imperial rituals drawing on eternals; the Conclave instead invited the High House of Wisdom to work with the Celestial Arch. The Commonwealth has effectively left the Liberty Pact, alarming Sumaah. The Cardinal of Prosperity asked why the two Synods differ over Zemress.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Cardinal of Prosperity notes that even the Grendel recognise Zemress's inspiration, though in a manner the Sumaah call twisted, heretical and blasphemous.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Zemress of the Isles is described as an inspirational figure to many across the Bay of Catazar, especially sailors, corsairs and merchants.

388YE Autumn Thule ambassador briefing.d: The Thule hired Imperial mercenaries for their campaign against the Druj in the Forest of Ulnak but received no Military Council support. They understood this was because the Dragons had offered the Empire too little incentive. Disappointed, though too proud to say so, they negotiated a two-season treaty with the Druj freezing current borders. They appear to have gained some or all of what they sought, and they deliberately kept the treaty short, expecting the Druj to want to extend it. The civil service noted that coordinating magic in shared territories would be imperfect, and warned that asking permission could create grievances. Runa Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided said the masters of Otkodov would handle the Circle of Zulgan Tash, the Painted Caves and the Malachite Casket themselves.

n.Druj: The Druj agreed a two-season peace treaty with the Thule that freezes their shared borders in the Forest of Ulnak, and the Thule expect them to be eager to extend it.
n.Thule: Disappointed by the lack of Imperial military support, the Dragons secured a short, deliberately limited peace with the Druj. They also told the Empire they would deal with the Circle of Zulgan Tash themselves, as a matter for wizards rather than diplomats.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Ossium, a Varushkan-held territory, is used as an example of where casting Hand of the Dhomiro against Thule wishes could cause offence.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Fighting between the Thule and the Druj was halted by a treaty freezing the current borders in Ulnak for two seasons.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; it is relevant only through the general guidance on coordinating magic in territories shared with the Thule.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: cited as a hypothetical case where the Empire performing Hand of the Dhomiro against Thule wishes would anger them more than not asking at all.
t.Otkodov: The masters of Otkodov announced they would personally resolve the matter of the Circle of Zulgan Tash, the Painted Caves and the Malachite Casket. They gave only an assurance that their response would be for the best and in line with existing treaties.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: listed in the further reading as a territory in Otkodov.

A fork in the path.d: The mystics revealed that the Raven's Dream, a shared vision, needs a dose of true liao. They withdrew support for the Parliament of Owls, which can no longer be cast, and will instead let the Witan choose one new Wintermark problem for them to appraise each year, starting at the Winter Solstice. They warned that no new Champion should take the Crown of Three Tears until Wemba the Bloody and Kaarina White-Eye are dealt with. After that, a Witan will choose a cause and the nation's mystics will choose and crown its Champion. Answering the Raven Seer's question about the Gullet, they reported that Rook's Feather has offered a proposal to defend the marshes. Sung offered to enfold the Aviary at Ishal if the Archmage of Night formally asks before the end of the Summer Solstice 389YE.

n.Jotun: The Jotun are named as one of the two known threats from the Gullet, having apparently called up allies from Fjorknae able to sail in and raid its shores. The aid offered to Wintermark is partly aimed at guarding against them.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Night Singer's apparent protection of the City from the Whisper Gallery after the Chamber of Euphony was built in Apulian is cited as a hopeful precedent.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are recalled as having captured the Crown of Three Tears about a decade ago and used fell magic on it.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark loses the Parliament of Owls but gains a yearly Witan-chosen appraisal by the mystics and a way to experience the Raven's Dream if it can supply true liao. The Crown of Three Tears is held back until Agramant's servants are slain, after which the nation's mystics will choose a Champion for a Witan-chosen cause. The Raven Seer may also accept Sung's offer to enfold the Aviary at Ishal.

t.Fjorknae: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun appear to have called up allies from Fjorknae who can sail into the Gullet.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Hahnmark is used as an example of how the Crown's doom might fall on a territory if its senator became Champion.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa is named as the territory most endangered by threats from the Gullet, both Jotun raiders and coral-encrusted creatures. Rook's Feather has offered a proposal to help defend its marshes.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page refers only to the mystics returning from their labours in the far frozen north.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Witan's exploration was of the wastes north of Sermersuaq, and the page notes the Jotun would attack Sermersuaq if they came overland.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Night Singer's apparent intervention to protect the City from the Whisper Gallery after the Chamber of Euphony was built in Apulian is cited as a precedent.
t.Tsirku: The Mystics of Ishal have finished their part in exploring Tsirku and will not return to it. Further exploration, likely years of work, now falls to others.

A friend like you.d: Meraud offered to help build the Highgrove Trail in Axmure, and Prospero agreed to patronise a Dawnish college, the Tower of the Loom. Estavus's architects proposed rebuilding Binding Oak Spire in Proceris. Roshanwe offered to swear an oath against the Cold Sun if the Throne swore the same, and proposed a Frozen Beacon in Suaq Fount. Zakalwe challenged the Hanuri Garrison's Quartermaster to defeat a yegarra warband in Bregasland and announced a symposium questioning the future of their pact. Janon, still under enmity, sent heralds threatening curses on Bregasland, the Barrens and Kahraman. Tharim offered a replacement for the Clarion Call ritual on conditions, Skathe set a bounty on cursing the Knight-protector of Winter, and the illegal Whisper Gallery offered Druj ritual texts.

n.Dawn: Dawn was offered Meraud's Highgrove Trail in Semmerholm and Prospero's patronage of the Tower of the Loom in Astolat, while Janon's heralds targeted the Barrens to test the Dawnish Maestro of the Cat's Graces and Skathe set a bounty on cursing Lady Aletheia, the Knight-protector of Winter.
n.Druj: The Whisper Gallery claimed the Druj gave it the Palace of the Sleepers to keep it from the Empire during the invasion of Sarangrave, and Zakalwe's heralds planned to discuss the war with the Druj, whose defeat they called imminent.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the reward for beating Cathan Canae's warhost was likened to the boon offered to the Unshackled in Mareave.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Polemarch of Highwatch was among those specifically invited to Zakalwe's symposium on the Empire's wars.
n.Jotun: A yegarra warband led by Abby the Feller, accompanied by heralds of Eleonaris, was marching across Bella's Bluff in Bregasland, and Zakalwe's herald challenged the Empire to defeat it or see her favour pass to the yegarra.
n.The Brass Coast: Janon's heralds crossed into Braydon's Jasse to test Freeborn passion, and the Azure Sutannir, João i Cabral i Riqueza, was charged with stopping them before they cursed Kahraman.
n.The League: Zakalwe's herald Telephysius spent the season in Temeschwar and offered prismatic ink to the Quartermaster of the Hanuri Garrison, Erikas Van Temeshwar, if he defeated the yegarra, while Jaheris noted that no League citizen had yet met the Argent Preceptor.
n.The Marches: Janon's heralds threatened to curse Bregasland from Gravenmarch, and Tharim sought the last artefact from a cave in Oddmire, Mitwold, entrusting its recovery to William Guildenstern.
n.Urizen: Urizen was offered plans to rebuild Binding Oak Spire in Zenith, with any cut to Zenith's business investment subject to the Urizen Assembly's veto, and was warned of consequences if Prospero-aided rituals entered Urizen lore.
n.Varushka: Tharim's legion of Ashen Knights remained camped outside Vorota and began fortifying its encampment with palisades and black-iron chains, still refusing to explain its presence.
n.Wintermark: Roshanwe proposed a Frozen Beacon in Suaq Fount to aid the Winterfolk quest to scout Tsirku, and Tharim demanded an apology from Eevi of the Gadrai as a condition of his ritual offer.

t.Astolat: Prospero asked that the Tower of the Loom, a proposed Dawnish college of magic, be built beside Silver Lake just outside Weaving, and requested dominion over its reflection in the water.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the name only appears in the title of Cathan Canae's herald, the Thane of the Enduring Bastion; nothing happened in the territory.
t.Bregasland: Janon's heralds threatened to curse Bregasland with violent emotions, and a yegarra warband with heralds of Eleonaris was marching across Bella's Bluff, where the Hanuri Garrison's Quartermaster was challenged to defeat it.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Roshanwe's herald searched Hahnmark, among other Wintermark territories, for a suitable regio before choosing Sermersuaq.
t.Kahraman: A band of Janon heralds entered Kahraman and threatened to curse it with violent emotions unless the Azure Sutannir defeated them.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Roshanwe's herald searched Kallavesa, among other Wintermark territories, for a suitable regio before choosing Sermersuaq.
t.Karov: Tharim's Ashen Knights remained camped outside Vorota and began fortifying their camp, giving no reason for being there.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the boon for beating Cathan Canae's warhost was compared to that offered to the Unshackled in Mareave.
t.Mitwold: A conjunction opened to a cave in Mitwold, where the bearer of the last artefact sought by Tharim died trapped, and William Guildenstern was made responsible for recovering it.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Roshanwe first offered a prismatic ink site in Operus, Redoubt, before the Archmage of Day steered it towards Wintermark.
t.Sarangrave: The Whisper Gallery revealed that the Druj handed it the Palace of the Sleepers to keep it from the Empire during the invasion of Sarangrave, and it offered some of the Palace's ritual texts to Night magicians.
t.Semmerholm: Meraud offered to enchant a Highgrove Trail of heraldic beast statues, raising mana site investment in Semmerholm and giving Dawnish mana sites an extra crystal each season, if the materials were provided and the Senate approved it.
t.Sermersuaq: Roshanwe proposed a Frozen Beacon on Sermersuaq's northern border, creating the Keeper of the Northern Light with an income of prismatic ink.
t.Temeschwar: Zakalwe's herald Telephysius stayed in Temeschwar and offered to remain, providing prismatic ink each season to the Hanuri Garrison's Quartermaster, if he defeated the yegarra.
t.The Barrens: Janon's heralds crossed into the Barrens, seen as the easiest Dawnish territory to enter, threatening to curse it unless the Maestro of the Cat's Graces defeated them.
t.Tsirku: The proposed Frozen Beacon would peer into the storm of Sydanjaa to aid the Winterfolk quest to scout Tsirku and guide those returning home.
t.Zenith: Estavus's architects offered plans to rebuild Binding Oak Spire to boost the Arch of the Sky's white granite, optionally redirecting Bridge of the Air profits by permanently cutting Zenith's business investment.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Janon's heralds occupied the Graven Commons in Gravenmarch and called out Aracelis I Erigo, General of the Burning Falcon, to face them.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Janon's heralds set themselves in Uthman's Field in Braydon's Jasse, less than a day from the Azure Chorus, to test the Freeborn.
r.Karov/Wieliczka: Tharim's Ashen Knights remained encamped outside Vorota and began fortifying the camp with palisades and black-iron chains.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: A four-person conjunction opened to a cave in Oddmire where the last of Tharim's sought-after artefacts lay with its dead bearer.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: Meraud's herald surveyed Axmure for the Highgrove Trail, whose statues would also animate to defend the region at House D'Fauntine's command, each with an effective strength of 300.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Suaq Fount was chosen as the site for Roshanwe's proposed Frozen Beacon, a lighthouse watching the storm of Sydanjaa.
r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Telephysius spent much of the season talking with the Hanuri garrison before challenging its Quartermaster to defeat the yegarra in Bregasland.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Janon's heralds planted their flag at the Glade of the Rising Sun in Saltmarsh, awaiting Lady Ralphine Sepulchre, the Maestro of the Cat's Graces.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The ruined Binding Oak Spire in Proceris could be rebuilt to house quarry workers, raising the Arch of the Sky's output to twenty wains a season and allowing extra white granite to be bought.

A greater darkness.d: The Druj had threatened to kill every enslaved Great Forest Orc unless the orcs of Peytaht betrayed the Empire. Led by Ioan Longshadow and Skywise Rykana, the raiders took watchtowers in Upper Saarnath, stormed the Grove of Woe, where a Buruk Tepel burned herself to death after her death fog failed, and escorted several hundred former slaves down the Lidless Stair to Imperial lines. In Deathsgate they broke Winter-bound guardians and stopped Nimon Rue's het from burning the slaves alive. The Karass then slipped away, claiming they would mount a diversion, and the fleeing column met a retreating Druj army. A Sentinel Gate conjunction to Grimfen Mire offered Anvil a chance to delay the Druj and save them.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Envoy to the Karass, Reynard of De Gauvin, persuaded the Karass to join the raid, and some of the humans freed from the Grove of Woe were Dawnish yeofolk taken in Druj raids.
n.Druj: The Druj lost the Grove of Woe and its enslaved tree-tenders, saw a Buruk Tepel and Nimon Rue's het killed, and lost the Lidless Stair gate. Their Amber Scorpion sept is now retreating towards the column of refugees fleeing the Sacred Grove.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Ioan Longshadow is described as a survivor of Grendel chains, and Grendel-held Mareave is named among the places whose Unshackled septs answered the call.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly sent Skywise Rykana, seconded by Bloodcrow Meep, to lead its warbands, whose orcs used Druj disguises and fought for their ancestors at both groves. Rykana shares a dozen wains of liberated weirwood with the Navarr commander.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Navarr gathered for the raid in hidden glens in Liathaven, beneath the blind eyes of the Jotun.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Assembly sent Ioan Longshadow to honour its oaths to the Great Forest Orcs, and Navarr from across their lands joined the raid. Their words broke the freed slaves' fear and their Spring magicians breached the Lidless Stair.
n.Thule: The Thule of Otkodov unwittingly shaped the raid: their curse on Ulnak weakened the Winter guardians, but their seizure of Bonewall drove a Druj army into the path of the fleeing refugees.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named; the page refers only to the Imperial campaign from Sarangrave and the earlier conquest of Whisperwood.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orcs in Ossium were previously liberated, Bloodcrow Meep of Ossium's Yerende sept went on the raid, and Varushka's Hunt of Alderei the Fair is the only weirwood forest named as larger than the Grove of Woe.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Navarr moved even in the tangled depths of Brocéliande to join the raid.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Raiders crossed Grimfen Mire into Deathsgate and freed some four hundred slaves from the Sacred Grove, but the refugees are now trapped between pursuers from Cassad Ûln and a retreating Druj army.
t.Hercynia: Navarr and Great Forest Orc steadings in Hercynia supported the raid with warriors and supplies, and some of the freed servants of the Druj may find a home there.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Navarr in the lost lands of Liathaven gathered for the raid in secret.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Unshackled septs in Mareave heard the call to fight the Druj, and its businesses and farms provided supplies.
t.Miaren: Miaren's Navarr and Great Forest Orc steadings gave warriors and supplies to the raid, and some freed servants of the Druj may settle there.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs of Ossium were freed from the Druj in earlier years, and Imperial forces rallied there.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Otkodov were considered as uncertain allies on the northern route, and the fleeing refugees headed towards their front line.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Raiders scaled Upper Saarnath, liberated the Grove of Woe and fought their way down the Lidless Stair to the Imperial armies in Lower Saarnath.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: Imperial forces rallied in northern Sarangrave, and the earlier conquest of Whisperwood had freed the orcs held there.
t.Skarsind: Unshackled septs of Skarsind answered their ancestors' call with warriors and supplies, and some freed servants of the Druj may find a welcome there.
t.The Barrens: The raid was mounted to rescue the kin of the Barrens' Great Forest Orcs, and the Barrens is the intended refuge for those freed. A hundred Karass hunters joined the Imperial forces on its borders.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Navarr in Therunin answered the call, and memories of the Druj atrocities there spurred the raiders on.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Mentioned in passing: only as part of a participant's name, Aldred Boar's Dell.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Deathsgate: Beneath Cassad Ûln the raiders shattered the binding stones of Winter guardians, killed Nimon Rue's het and freed the Great Forest Orcs penned in wooden pyres at the Sacred Grove.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest: The raiders avoided crossing Gul'thak but marched along its border with Bonewall, destroying a retreating Deadly Blade cohort and other Druj stragglers.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire: The raiders crossed the cursed mire unopposed but unwelcomed, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction to the Reeth Plain offers the chance to delay the Amber Scorpions so the refugees can escape.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt: Navarr covens permanently gave Oerwealt the woodward quality, letting heralds of Irra Harah enter there more easily to aid those who fear oppression.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Shifting Basin: Mentioned in passing: the Karass proposed escaping south through it, but the route was rejected because it holds one of Ulnak's largest Druj settlements.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Leen Rarckan: Mentioned in passing: a Druj force approaching the Grove of Woe may have come up from Leen Rarckan.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Lower Saarnath: With the Imperial armies fighting in Lower Saarnath, the rescued slaves descended the Lidless Stair to safety behind the victorious Imperial lines.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Upper Saarnath: Raiders captured watchtowers, stormed the Grove of Woe, killed its Buruk Tepel and broke through the Lidless Stair's gate to lead several hundred freed slaves out.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: Mentioned in passing: its conquest by the Empire is cited as having freed the Great Forest Orcs held there.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Great Forest Orcs here had defied the Buruk Tepel's ultimatum, and the Heart of Peytaht is the intended refuge for their rescued kin.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Mentioned in passing: the Karass proposed fleeing south to Saltmarsh, but the plan was rejected.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish envoy who recruited the Karass deals with the sept of the Bleaks and the Untrod Groves.

A habit I can't break.d: The rakshasa gifted in 380YE died in Holberg, ending the Keeper of the Imperial Menagerie's supply of Winter vis and rare consumables. Claude of Holberg will preserve it for the Sculpture Garden unless the Conclave accepts the Thrice-Cursed Court's offer of 8 vials of heart's blood. Agramant also asked for it, which would be illegal while he is under enmity. The hakima sent *Dust, Glass and Flame* to Anvil because the City of Wonders was finished early. The Ode to Blood and Sacrifice song ended. The two Rivers rituals now replace each other permanently rather than cancelling out. Three skirmishes against coral husks were offered, each with a crown reward.

n.Dawn: Kay Griffinsbain of Dawn, Keeper of the Imperial Menagerie, lost the Winter vis and rare consumables the rakshasa once provided. Kay would receive 8 vials of heart's blood if the Conclave let the Thrice-Cursed Court take the body.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Agramant offered to animate the rakshasa's corpse with a winter spirit to run amok in the Salt Flats eating Druj. The offer is illegal while he remains under enmity.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: drakes from Mareave, held by the Grendel, are among the newer Menagerie attractions that eclipsed the rakshasa.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun are not named, but the coral husk skirmish takes place in Ottermire in Bregasland, which they held alongside the Marches.
n.Navarr: The magical song carried along the trods from Brocéliande finally faded. Navarr wayhouses debated whether it echoed Nathair Autumngale's judgement, spoke to the coming final battle against the vallorn, or needed no meaning at all.
n.The League: Claude of Holberg is set to receive the rakshasa's body for the Sculpture Garden unless the Conclave chooses otherwise. Doing so would raise the Financier of Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mementoes' income by two crowns a season.
n.The Marches: Beaters from Sallow went missing hunting coral husks in Ottermire. Biggest Peter asked the Keeper of the Dour Fens, Bill of Middleton, to find them and offered four crowns if he succeeds.
n.Wintermark: Two coral husk threats arose in Kallavesa. The scop Seaxwulf asked the Raven Seer Elena to investigate strangely huddled husks, and the thane of Freja's Rest asked Remembrancer Hodwyn Aevardson to destroy husks lurking near the village.

t.Bregasland: Coral husks set upon a band of beaters from Sallow in Ottermire. This led to a combat-likely skirmish for the Keeper of the Dour Fens.
t.Brocéliande: The song raised in Brocéliande by *An Ode To Blood And Sacrifice* a year earlier finally came to an end, leaving only faint echoes.
t.Holberg: The rakshasa died in Holberg's Imperial Menagerie, and its body may be preserved for the city's Sculpture Garden or claimed by the heralds of the Thrice-Cursed Court.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa hosts two coral husk skirmishes: strangely huddled husks for the Raven Seer to investigate, and a lurking gaggle near the fishing village of Freja's Rest for the Remembrancer of Blood and Salt to destroy.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: drakes from Mareave are cited as Menagerie attractions that eclipsed the rakshasa.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: beasts captured in northern Sermersuaq are cited as Menagerie attractions that eclipsed the rakshasa.

r.Bregasland/Ottermire: Beaters who went looking for coral husks in Ottermire were ambushed and have not returned. Biggest Peter asked Bill of Middleton to find out what happened, warning that husks are likely in the area.

Accomplices.d: The heralds mocked the Synod, the Empress and the Military Council, complaining that only Towlen Nighthaven (Deadfall) and Mirella of the Twisted Rose (Amber Lance) had backed the Golden Axe, and that no guerdon was paid. Agramant offered two pawns of heart's blood to every unit supporting an Imperial army in Therunin, although accepting it is illegal while it remains under enmity. If no army attacked, it would again offer a Reconquer Therunin venture, allowing pseudonyms on its roll. Dochas, summoned to inquisition by Eskah Swift Hart, refused to surrender until the work was done. He offered a conjunction to the Weeping Glade and the recovered Iron Helms standard as a gift. The Chief Magistrate ruled that lawful cooperation with him was permitted.

n.Druj: The Druj still held Peakedge Song, Upper Tarn Valley and East Ashes in Therunin, where their remnant leadership continued to oppress the Navarri, but they had lost Lower Tarn Valley to the Golden Axe.
n.Navarr: Agramant's heralds urged the Navarri to question whether the Empire truly cared about Therunin, despite the Navarr National Assembly's repeated rejections of its offer. Meanwhile, Dochas Weeping Glade pressed on with his own plan to liberate the territory.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the heralds jeered that four Imperial armies were 'having a holiday' in the Urizen territory of Zenith.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: a quoted Navarr Assembly statement directed people to the Stormcloaks of Wintermark for help against Blood on the Snow.

t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: the heralds noted that six Imperial armies were fighting there, and Dochas lamented that the crushing of Sanath seemed to come before Therunin.
t.Therunin: Heralds of Agramant worked throughout the territory, aiding the fight against the Druj and the vallorn while spreading propaganda. Agramant offered heart's blood to units supporting any Imperial army attacking there, and Dochas sought Imperial help to retake the rest of the territory.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the heralds mocked the four Imperial armies stationed there as being on holiday.

r.Therunin/East Ashes: The region remained under Druj control, but a Sentinel Gate conjunction opened for four people to the Weeping Glade there, where Dochas and his allies would meet Imperial representatives.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Mentioned in passing: listed as completely dominated by the vallorn.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Mentioned in passing: listed as completely dominated by the vallorn.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Golden Axe, supported by Deadfall and Amber Lance, made progress in retaking this region from the Druj.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Mentioned in passing: noted as still under Druj control.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Mentioned in passing: listed as completely dominated by the vallorn.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: Mentioned in passing: noted as still under Druj control.

All I can do.d: Beoraidh, a neutral free port under Sarcophan protection, offered to halve the basilica's 27-Throne labour cost if an orc commissioned it. Elsbeth di Sarvos noted that an army enchanted with Bound by Common Cause on a defensive order could supply 108 crowns of labour. The Weavers of Culwich offered tapestries of weltsilver and iridescent gloaming in place of mithril. Tibisi of Shelah's Bounty suggested redirecting the Grand Ossuary of Reikos's donations to provide 10 wains of white granite. The Aghnayadh Apothecaries offered to fund the land if the Senate devolved drug legality to the Imperial Apothecaries Guild. Ambassador Kaltrin also tacitly welcomed discreet Imperial spies, through a proposed 12-Throne Regario Dossier motion.

n.Dawn: The Weavers of Culwich, a Dawnish cabal, offered to replace the basilica's mithril with tapestries depicting moments of Virtue, at a cost of 400 ingots of weltsilver and 400 measures of iridescent gloaming. The Cat's Graces could reduce this cost.
n.Grendel: Beoraidh had broken from the Grendel but welcomed their merchants. Proposed Imperial agents there could gather intelligence on the Grendel, and any Grendel shift to aggression in Mareave would stop an Imperial army from helping with construction.
n.Highguard: Highborn ambassador Melkior championed the basilica, and the Benefactors Council was urged to pause the Grand Inspiration to fund it. Reikos's Grand Ossuary donations were offered as an alternative source of funds.
n.Imperial Orcs: Beoradhi investors offered to cover half the basilica's labour costs if an orc commissioned it. Bloodcrow Rasp, Senator for Skarsind, co-funded the land purchase after the Equinox.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name the Bay directly. It is linked only through the maritime trade and docks of nearby Beoraidh.
t.Mareave: Mareave was the proposed site of a grand Basilica of the Way in Beoraidh, with Imperial soldiers potentially labouring there under defensive orders. Any campaign in Mareave would halt that help.
t.Reikos: The Steward of the Ossuary could divert the Grand Ossuary's donations from Reikos's congregations for six months to supply white granite for the basilica. In return, the Steward would receive four doses of liao each season.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's Senator, Bloodcrow Rasp, had earlier pushed through investment in Beoraidh's docks and helped pay for the basilica's land.
t.Weirwater: Culwich in eastern Weirwater, famed for its flax and wool, is home to the Weavers of Culwich, who offered tapestries for the basilica. Artists may have been drawn to Dawn to help them.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: The city-state was the site of the planned Basilica of the Way, and its land was paid for after the Equinox. Its Aghnayadh Apothecaries sought influence with the Imperial Apothecaries Guild, and its docks were proposed as a listening post for Imperial spies.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Mentioned in passing: Sinfoyard is recognised by the Senate, together with the city of Beoraidh, as part of the neutral state.

Arrows and clay.d: Entry required being the target of the Summer ritual Challenge the Iron Duke; ten covens cast it the previous season. Winners in the past year may not compete again. In the Challenge of the Black Web, challengers and one attendant each had thirty minutes to gather glowing lights from hedge-lined glades at Widowsglade while avoiding venomous spider heralds of Jaheris. One hit ended a challenger's attempt, and the top half by lights collected would win. In the Challenge of the Painted Gallery, Barien posed for artists, who then had until evening to create any form of art for judging by his heralds and Ralphine, Maestro of the Cat's Graces, with a grand prize for the favourite piece.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: five of the ten covens listed as having cast Challenge the Iron Duke last season were Dawnish.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Eternal Family, a Navarri coven, was listed among last season's casters of Challenge the Iron Duke.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Glass Mantle and the Tempest Flame, both Freeborn covens, were listed among last season's casters of Challenge the Iron Duke.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Prosperous Pigs, a Marcher coven, was listed among last season's casters of Challenge the Iron Duke.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Voices of the Unbound Storm, a Wintermark coven, was listed among last season's casters of Challenge the Iron Duke.

t.Weirwater: Weirwater hosted the Challenge of the Black Web, with a conjunction opening to Widowsglade where challengers stalked glades patrolled by spider heralds of Jaheris.

r.Weirwater/Weirmoor: Widowsglade in Weirmoor was the site of the stealth challenge, reached by a conjunction from the Sentinel Gate for up to a hundred people at 22:30 on Saturday.

Come together.d: Survivors of Thornsong House, lost when Therunin fell to the Druj, inspired the proposal. Commissioned by Senate motion before the end of Summer Solstice 389YE, the Gardens would cost 90 weirwood, 40 white granite, 20 mithril and 450 crowns, take a year, and have a 10-throne upkeep. Each Miaren herb garden would gain two true vervain and one cerulean mazzarine a season, and the Apothecaries Guild would vote on which of three research options to pursue, or four if all four nations helped. Reassigning four great works for a year could remove the need for wains entirely. New sinecures were also offered in Holberg, Ossium and Skarsind. This supersedes the Winter 387YE opportunity.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: their conquest of Therunin destroyed Thornsong House, the loss that inspired the proposal.
n.Highguard: The Benefactor of High Chalcis, Enoch of Atun's Sanctuary, could redirect the Gardens of High Chalcis for a year with a Senate announcement, cutting the weirwood needed by 50 wains. The skilled apothecaries of Reikos would also broaden the college's research if they took part.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Yerende sept is eager to help: redirecting the Red Blade Memorial would remove the need for mithril. A House of the Lost sinecure could create Rhyv's Blade to support Unshackled warriors with herbs and potions, and the earlier Yerende opportunity has lapsed.
n.Navarr: The proposal comes from Navarr dreamspeakers seeking to restore the herbal expertise lost with Thornsong House, though its great cost and the Guild's control of research are clear drawbacks. Bronwen urges the nation to embrace the Apothecaries Guild and use its wayhouses to win support from other nations.
n.The League: Holmauer Park could be redirected for a year to remove the need for white granite, and League doctors could widen the college's research. The League could also build a Holmauer Watchhouse to create the Holmauer Watchcaptain.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Doyen of the Spires is cited as a justified exception to Imperial bodies directing college research, because it relies on unique Urizen magic.
n.Varushka: Krustrozi's Lumbermill could be redirected to cut the weirwood needed by 40 wains, and Varushkan wise ones would broaden the college's research. A Darkwoods Wagonhouse could create the Kurstrozi Lumberjack title to serve Ossium's forest owners.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the accompanying story recalls an old Wintermark scholar, Topi, who moved his books to Gildenheim with the help of beavers.

t.Holberg: The Gates of Holmauer Park could be redirected for a year to cover the white granite needed, and a sinecure could be commissioned there to oversee the park's safety and funds.
t.Miaren: The Gardens of the Heart would raise the investment in Miaren's herb gardens, giving each two extra true vervain and one extra cerulean mazzarine a season, and would make Seren a centre for potion research.
t.Ossium: Krustrozi's Lumbermill could be redirected for a year to supply tools and materials for the Gardens, and the territory was offered a sinecure to support its forest owners.
t.Reikos: Many Thornsong House survivors fled here. The Gardens of High Chalcis could be redirected for a year to cut the weirwood needed for the Gardens of the Heart by 50 wains.
t.Skarsind: The Red Blade Memorial could be redirected for a year so its bonesetters' contributions remove the need for mithril, and the territory was offered a sinecure to support Unshackled field medicine.
t.Therunin: Thornsong House, the Navarr herbmastery college here, was burned when the territory fell to the Druj, and the proposal seeks to restore what was lost.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: A Holmauer Watchhouse could be built at the Gates of Holmauer Park for 10 white granite and 30 crowns. It would create the Holmauer Watchcaptain, who would receive 9 crystal mana a season, guard against threats from the cursed park and could redirect its funds.
r.Miaren/Serenael: The proposed Gardens of the Heart would be built here in Seren, the City of Dreams, drawing masters of the natural sciences to research new potions under the Apothecaries Guild.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: A Darkwoods Wagonhouse could be built at Kurstrozi's Lumbermill for 10 weirwood and 36 crowns. It would create the Kurstrozi Lumberjack, who would receive 11 crowns a season and could redirect the mill's bounty.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: Mentioned in passing: some survivors of Thornsong House stayed on Chalcis Mount after fleeing to Reikos.
r.Skarsind/Gildermark: A House of the Lost, a school of field medicine at the Red Blade Memorial, could be built for 10 weirwood and 30 crowns. It would create Rhyv's Blade, who would receive weltsilver, ambergelt and beggar's lye each season and could redirect the memorial's bounty.

Construct Atalaq Tradehall.d: Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer, Senator for Sermersuaq, proposed the motion and Mel Bleak, Senator for Mournwold, seconded it. The tradehall had recently resurfaced during an appraisal of non-coin trades that ministries could make, which strayed into past opportunities to bring more money into the Anvil economy. The motion passed. After the Autumn Equinox, Jambert Wulfgar provided the 50 wains of weirwood with 4 thrones 2 crowns, and Kanute Adelaar van Holberg gave 14 thrones. Four others each added a crown. Once complete, the tradehall would raise business investment and taxation in Sermersuaq, add 7 crowns to the Custodian of the Bloody Great Sausage's income, and give Wintermark fleets extra income when trading abroad.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark fleet owners stood to earn an extra 36 rings for a year whenever they traded with foreign nations, and Wintermark's senator for Sermersuaq led the motion.

t.Sermersuaq: Once built, the tradehall would increase business investment in Sermersuaq by one and raise the territory's taxation by 4 thrones.

r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Sealtoq was chosen as the site of the Atalaq Tradehall, a great work taking three months to build once the weirwood and labour costs were met.

Construct Bakers' Bowl.d: The commission, announced in Autumn 388YE, required 20 wains of weirwood and 60 crowns in labour and took three months to build. Lula and Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund each provided 10 wains of weirwood and 2 thrones. Morlock and several Holbergers, along with Emilio Marsana Saverio di Sarvos, contributed further coin. Once complete, the Senators of the League can appoint the Sponsor of the Holberg Hammers, a lifetime position with an income of at least 216 rings per season, responsible for the well-being of the stadium and the team. The position is revocable by the Assembly of Nine, the General Assembly and the League National Assembly. Calcio and Foot-the-Ball teams from towns without their own stadiums were invited to train and play fixtures there.

n.The League: The League gains a new lifetime national sinecure, the Sponsor of the Holberg Hammers, appointed by League Senators, along with a stadium for its calcio and foot-the-ball teams.

t.Holberg: Holberg was to host the Bakers' Bowl stadium and its team, the Holberg Hammers, with several Holbergers contributing coin to the construction.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: The Bakers' Bowl stadium was to be built in Holmauer, where teams from towns without their own stadiums were invited to train and play fixtures.

Construct Botanical Gardens of First Voi.d: Rhisiart Heartsbane, Senator for Miaren, proposed the restoration of the gardens, and Bronimir Ranedzkah Pinewheel, Senator for Ossium, seconded it. The project was to be self-funded. Its cost was 30 wains of weirwood and 90 crowns in labour, and it would take three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox, several donors began contributing: Vick Dagger gave 8 wains of weirwood and Mharen Splitroot gave 2 wains. Others gave thrones and crowns, including Drysfa Broken Bough, Merewen Splitroot and Lady Mercy Goldvein. Once complete, the Dean of the First Voice Glade would again receive 27 drams of herbs each season. The Dean could also upgrade one basic herb garden belonging to a member of the Vallornguard each season.

n.Navarr: The gardens would restore a seasonal supply of herbs to the Dean of the Navarr First Voice Glade school. They would also let the Dean improve herb gardens belonging to members of the Vallornguard, and Navarr donors were among the first to contribute weirwood and money.

t.Miaren: Miaren's own senator proposed restoring the botanical gardens of the First Voice Glade School in the Navarr-held territory, and the motion passed.

r.Miaren/Oakways: The restored gardens were to be built in Oakways, with materials and funds still being gathered after the Autumn Equinox.

Construct Dima's Light of Ossium.d: The great work, whose plans were first presented by one of the koboldi shortly before the Spring Equinox 387YE, was announced as fully self-funded, with thanks to King-under-the-Mountain and the forekoboldi Drageer. It was costed at 40 wains of white granite, 10 wains of mithril, 5 rings of ilium and 150 crowns in labour, and takes six months to build. Dima, Kostjya and a number of other citizens contributed money, white granite and mithril after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the beacon will warn of threats against Kostjyas Respite and increase the investment of fleets in Ossium, giving any fleet there that trades a bonus.

n.Varushka: Varushkan citizens led by Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Kostjya and others pooled their own money and materials to raise this beacon in Varushkan-held Ossium, strengthening the nation's coastal and maritime interests.

t.Ossium: Once complete, the beacon will raise the investment of fleets in Ossium by one and give any fleet trading from the territory a bonus.

r.Ossium/Bittershore: Bittershore is the site of the new beacon, which will warn of threats against Kostjyas Respite once its six months of construction are finished.

Construct Effervescent Brook.d: The Effervescent Brook was suggested by Gwinthav who speaks with Majesty, herald of Meraud, and announced under an Imperial Wayleave by Wistan Goodledger. It costs 4 wains of weirwood, 4 rings of ilium and 12 crowns in labour, takes three months to build and carries no upkeep. The cost was to be met by the Tender of the Phoenix Flame and the Vallorn Guard. Enchantress Areloe Larmallevés provided the 4 wains of weirwood and Farren Silver Streams 1 crown after the Autumn Equinox. Custodianship was later amended to rest with the Tender of the Phoenix Flame, who, once the ministry is complete, will be able to buy Vials of Whitesmoke for tempest jade.

n.Dawn: Dawnish figures, including Enchantress Areloe Larmallevés, drove the commission and supplied its weirwood, and the Dawnish Tender of the Phoenix Flame was to gain custody of a new source of tonics against the vallorn.

t.Astolat: A new ministry was being raised in Astolat to channel the Whitesmoke Brook to the Phoenix Flame, adding a resource for the territory's struggle against the vallorn.

r.Astolat/Grovesyard: Grovesyard is the site of the Effervescent Brook, where the Whitesmoke Brook was to be diverted to the Phoenix Flame to produce Vials of Whitesmoke.

Construct Garden of Hope.d: The Garden of Hope was presented as part of the Imperial Orcs' highest calling, and the announcement thanked the Black Tillers for listening to Bloodcrow Meep. It cost 25 wains of white granite, 25 wains of weirwood and 150 crowns in labour, and took three months to build. After the Autumn Equinox Erlend Gunnulfsson supplied all the weirwood and white granite, while Bloodcrow Rasp, Karrak, Farren Silver Streams, Rhys Nighthaven and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov contributed money. Once complete, the garden provides two doses of Hearkener's Hope to each congregation in Skarsind and increases investment in Skarsind's congregations by one.

n.Imperial Orcs: The great work answers part of the Imperial Orcs' highest calling, giving orcs of the Empire a new way to obtain Hearkener's Hope in their own lands, in the spirit of learning from their ancestors.

t.Skarsind: Once complete, every congregation in Skarsind receives two doses of Hearkener's Hope and has its investment raised by one.

r.Skarsind/Gildermark: Gildermark is the site of the Garden of Hope, a great work designed by the local Black Tillers and built over three months.

Construct Grand Lodge of Sevenfold Path.d: The grand lodge was first presented shortly before the Winter Solstice 387YE. It required 65 wains of weirwood, 45 of white granite, 15 of mithril and 375 crowns in labour, with five thrones of upkeep and nine months to build. Several individuals made small crown donations after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete it will add 15 mana crystals to the Conclave font each season, house a grand basilica to the Way, cut the Grandmaster's mana costs, and supply true liao and liao to the order. It will also raise congregation investment in the territory, let Highguard support an additional navy, and add the Voice of the Paragons to Imperial lore while Net of Gossamer Chains is interdicted.

n.Highguard: Once complete, the grand lodge will allow Highguard to raise and support one additional navy beyond current limits, and will raise the investment level of congregations in its Necropolis territory by one.

t.Necropolis: The Grand Lodge of the Sevenfold Path and its extended basilica are being built in Sanctuary Sands, Necropolis, and on completion will raise the investment level of congregations in the territory by one.

Construct Hall of the Soturi.d: Proposed by Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa, and seconded by Delara of the House of the Wanderer, Senator for Zenith, the motion commissioned the Hall of the Soturi as a self-funded project. First suggested by the Mystics of Ishal in answer to a call to action from the Raven Seer, it required 20 wains of white granite, 20 wains of weirwood and 15 thrones in labour, and would take three months to complete. Early contributions after the Autumn Equinox included two wains of white granite and two crowns from individual donors. Once complete, Wintermark can raise a single new army based on the Kallavesi tradition with the fearless quality.

n.Wintermark: Once the hall is complete, Wintermark will be able to raise one new army rooted in the Kallavesi tradition and bearing the unique fearless quality.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's own senator proposed the edifice, which is to be built on Kallavesi soil and will shape a new army in the territory's mystic tradition.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: The Hall of the Soturi is to be raised in the Kallavesa Marsh, with construction taking three months once the white granite, weirwood and labour costs are met.

Construct Kallavesa Marshways.d: Proposed by Delara of the House of the Wanderer, Senator for Zenith, and seconded by Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa, the motion passed. The work required 80 wains of weirwood and 30 thrones in labour, taking six months to complete; Gisli i Phovas i Guerra provided the full materials and money after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the marshways raise investment in Kallavesa's businesses by one level (an additional 36 rings) and its herb gardens by one level, yielding extra herbs each season, and create a guarding venture in which Wintermark and Dawnish military units protect merchants using the marshways in exchange for herbs.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a great work in one of its territories that enriches its businesses and herb gardens there, and its military units become eligible to guard the marshways' merchants in exchange for herbs, alongside Dawnish units.

t.Kallavesa: The marshways are built in Kallavesa, raising investment in its businesses and herb gardens by one level each once complete, and bringing merchant traffic guarded by Wintermark and Dawnish soldiers.

Construct Kespoena's Nadir.d: Proposed by Aurianna du Meravon, Senator for Semmerholm, and seconded by Ismene of the Scarlet Guard, Senator for Morrow, the motion commissioned a new mithril seat at Kespoena's Nadir in Occursion. It cost 300 thrones in labour with 10 thrones a season upkeep, and took three months rather than six because of the existing exploits under Kespoena's Reach. Funding came from five donors giving just over 50 thrones each, 48 thrones from the Kespoena's Reach exploits, and two smaller one-crown gifts after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, an administrative motion was to be raised to allocate the bourse resource.

n.Urizen: Urizen gains a new mithril seat within its own territory of Zenith, building on the existing workings at Kespoena's Reach.

t.Zenith: Zenith becomes home to a second mithril seat, Kespoena's Nadir, which will add to the Empire's mithril supply once its bourse allocation is decided.

r.Zenith/Occursion: Occursion is where the new mithril vein was uncovered and where Kespoena's Nadir was built, with work speeded by the nearby exploits under Kespoena's Reach.

Construct Printers' Guild Bibliopole.d: Proposed by Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar, Senator for Temeschwar, and seconded by Mary Birchsmith, Senator for Mitwold, the motion followed the civil service record "truth but tell it slant" from Winter 387YE. The opportunity was first suggested by Professor Gelberg while the Printers' Guild were patrons of the Beurteilung. The edifice required 8 wains of white granite and 3 thrones in labour, with the motion stating the Printers' Guild would pay, and would take three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 388YE, Jonah Yakovitch provided the 3 thrones and 8 wains of white granite. Once complete, Printers' Guild publications, including treatises on the Way, will be accessible worldwide.

n.The League: A League senator proposed the motion, and the Printers' Guild's publications held in the League's Tassato will be carried abroad to readers across the world, including treatises on the Way.

t.Tassato: The copies of Printers' Guild publications stored in Tassato are the collection the new bibliopole will make accessible across the world once complete.

Construct Printers' Guild Stadium.d: Inspired by renewed interest in foot-the-ball after the pilgrimage of Apulian orcs to the Mournwold, the stadium was commissioned in Regario, across the river from the Printers' Guildhouse in Mestra. It cost 12 wains of white granite, 12 wains of weirwood and 3 thrones in labour, and takes three months to build. Jonah Yakovitch provided all of these after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the stadium will host matches against Marcher teams and possibly the Mestrans. Its sinecure, the Captain of the Regario Byliners, will be appointed by Tally of the Votes of the League's business owners.

n.The League: League business owners gain a new sinecure, the Captain of the Regario Byliners, to be appointed by Tally of the Votes once the stadium is complete. The announcement also playfully casts Regario as having upstaged Mestra.
n.The Marches: Marcher teams are expected to play matches at the new stadium, whose inspiration lay in sporting interest stirred by the Apulian orc pilgrimage to the Mournwold.

t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the pilgrimage of Apulian orcs to the Mournwold is credited with renewing interest in foot-the-ball and other sports.
t.Tassato: Tassato gains a new stadium in Regario, near the Printers' Guildhouse in Mestra, which will host matches and house the Regario Byliners.

r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: The Printers' Guild Stadium is being built in Regario as the home ground of the teal-clad Regario Byliners, with materials and labour provided after Autumn Equinox 388YE.

Construct Rose's Respite.d: Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, Master of Rings, used his authority to announce the building of Rose's Respite, a sinecure producing herbs, in The Chase region of Astolat. The project cost 16 wains of weirwood and 6 thrones in labour, and was expected to take three months to construct. The announcement was self-funded, and Laughlan provided the full weirwood and thrones after the Autumn Equinox 388YE. Once complete, the title of Keeper of Rose's Respite would be appointed by the Senators of Dawn.

n.Dawn: Dawn's senators would gain the right to appoint the Keeper of Rose's Respite, a new herb sinecure built on Dawnish land in Astolat.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the announcement was made and paid for by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, whose name ties him to the League city of Temeschwar.

t.Astolat: Astolat was to gain a new herb sinecure, Rose's Respite, taking three months to build.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the territory appears only in the name of the Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar.

r.Astolat/The Chase: The Chase was chosen as the site of Rose's Respite, a herb sinecure whose Keeper would be appointed by the Senators of Dawn.

Construct Spark of Ignition.d: The motion was announced by Berrak of The Phoenix Reach, Crystal Architect of the Spires, and was to be funded by Sarangrave Reforged. Standard costs applied: 16 wains of mithril and 76 crowns 16 rings in labour, with three months to build. The labour cost was raised by the presence of outlaw Druj in the territory. After the Autumn Equinox, Able the Taller, Esteban Ezmara, Abel the Rounder, Hector, Terentia and Vossk of Sarangrave Reforged, together with Bartimaeus, contributed mithril and money, together supplying the full 16 wains of mithril. Once complete, the Senators of Urizen will appoint the Lighter of the Forge.

n.Druj: The presence of outlaw Druj in Sarangrave raised the labour cost of building the Spark of Ignition.
n.Urizen: Urizen gains a new mana sinecure in Sarangrave, and its Senators will appoint the Lighter of the Forge once the Spark of Ignition is complete. It was funded largely by Sarangrave Reforged and announced by Berrak of The Phoenix Reach.

t.Sarangrave: Sarangrave is to receive the Spark of Ignition, a memorial to those who fell defending it. Construction cost more because outlaw Druj remain in the territory.

r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: Whisperwood is the site chosen for the Spark of Ignition, with three months of building work funded by Sarangrave Reforged and other donors.

Domain expansion.d: Ursula Smith's Assembly saw the Breadbasket reach Mournwold. Three opportunities followed. A 30-throne Overton Smithy commission would turn the Singing Caves' mithril into a thousand points of resupply for armies in Mournwold. Alternatively, a Senate amendment could merge the Quartermaster General with the Caves' custodian as a Marcher national title. A Synod mandate could stake a Marcher claim to Jotun-held Liathaven, creating an expectation, though not a legal right, of receiving it. Jotun reshaping had made Imperial maps of Liathaven useless for scrying until a new one is made. In Bregasland, the Imperial Orc demand for their dead in Grave Wood inflamed Marchers; an appraisal might find a way to recover them without disturbing Marcher graves.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher Assembly cited the Dawnish 'fancy magic castle' that resupplies armies as something they meant to outdo.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the war to eradicate the Druj in the east is described as drawing Imperial attention away from the Marches, and the Sarangrave is joked about as a worse place to live.
n.Imperial Orcs: Their Assembly's demand for the bones of the Autumn Hammers in Grave Wood angered many Marchers. Orcs caught approaching the wood with axes and shovels were turned back, and only an appraisal seemed likely to find a way to recover their dead without uprooting Marcher graves.
n.Jotun: Their slash-and-burn clearing of Liathaven, which they call Ashvale, had made it fertile and unrecognisable to Imperial maps, and the Marchers eyed it as their next conquest once Bregasland was retaken from them.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven is noted as a former Navarr territory where no Navarr have lived for years.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Freeborn dead are among those taken into Grave Wood, and the transfiguration of Madruga is cited as the last time an Imperial map stopped working.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the prestige of the Spiral Castle is what the Overtonians hoped to rival with their forges.
n.The Marches: Having completed their highest calling, the Marchers were offered forges at the Singing Caves, control of the Quartermaster General and a Synod claim to Liathaven for a possible sixth army. Their Assembly also faced pressure to defend Grave Wood against Imperial Orc demands.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark dead are among the fallen whom Marchers believe were reborn as the trees of Grave Wood.

t.Bregasland: Grave Wood, which sprang up overnight over nearly three thousand fallen soldiers, became a flashpoint after the Imperial Orc demand. The Marches were noted as taking Bregasland back from the Jotun, with victory in the Dour Fens promised.
t.Liathaven: Transformed by Jotun clearing and the heralds of the City of Fire and Stone, it could no longer be scried with existing maps, and a proposed Marcher mandate would stake a claim to conquer it. The vallorn and the Feni remain there.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: its transfiguration two years earlier is cited as the last time an Imperial map ceased to work for scrying.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: a tidal wave of Imperial steel is said to have swept through Mitwold, and it is among the four territories now covered by the Breadbasket.
t.Mournwold: The Breadbasket was completed here, and the Singing Caves at Overton could become an industrial district of smithies resupplying armies, or be tied to a Marcher Quartermaster General.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: a Marcher jokes that even Ashvale is better than living in the Sarangrave.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Spiral Castle's prestige is the benchmark the Overtonians wanted to compete with.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named; the only Dawnish reference is the Assembly's comparison with a Dawnish magic castle that resupplies armies.

r.Liathaven/Liath's Heart: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher Assembly's statement looked to Liath's Heart next door and the coming final battle with the vallorn.

Dream on.d: Enis's 383YE judgement sought recognition of Seren as a city equal to any other nation's, and work on the Temple began in Summer 386YE. Every congregation in Miaren now receives a dose of Goosewhisper Infusion and an extra liao. The Navarr Assembly can appoint a Dreamspeaker of Seren, and the dreamspeaker archetype is open to Navarr. The Temple could become a major pilgrimage site if it were consecrated with true liao, but this would need a Synod writ from a virtue assembly and general assembly support. Deryn of Vision's End asked the brands to vote on whether the Navarr should explore ways to show their importance to the Empire, such as ceasing to carry messages. Eirwen of Mountains Slumber asked the wayhouses to choose one territory and a shared dream to pursue there.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Eirwen recalls Navarr messengers helping the First Empress build her alliance with Dawn, and notes that defeating the vallorn is the shared highest calling of the Navarr and the Dawnish.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: dreamspeakers list the destruction of the Druj as a worthy dream and cite the effort to free the Great Forest Orcs from them, while Deryn blames Therunin's fall to the Druj on Imperial choices.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: victory over the Grendel and the freeing of slaves in Axos are cited as dreams as important as purging the vallorn.
n.Highguard: Reikos hosts the Navarr wayhouse Micah's Stand, so it could be chosen as the territory to benefit from a shared dream. Eirwen also disputes the Highborn claim that the Empire is uniquely their destiny.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind hosts the Ashen Tears wayhouse, so the Imperial Orcs could be the hosts of any shared dream the Navarr wayhouses choose to pursue.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: defeating the Jotun is named as a dream, and Deryn asks why there is no drive to recover Liathaven when the Empire rallies whenever the Jotun threaten Marcher lands.
n.Navarr: The nation gains a Dreamspeaker of Seren to appoint, a new archetype, liao and Goosewhisper Infusion for Miaren's congregations, and the chance to seek a true liao consecration. Its brands and wayhouses must each decide on Deryn's call for leverage and Eirwen's call to build civilisation.
n.The League: Holberg hosts the Splintered House wayhouse in Utterlund, making it a possible focus for the Navarr wayhouses' shared dream.
n.The Marches: Deryn holds up Marcher generals' oaths to defend their home territories, and the Marchers' sheathed threat to withhold grain, as the model of leverage the Navarr should emulate.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Deryn cites the Urizeni readiness to tear apart the Citadel Guard if Zenith were abandoned as an example of a nation fighting for its interests.
n.Varushka: Ossium hosts the Awstin's Rest wayhouse and could benefit from the Navarr wayhouses' dream. Deryn also praises the Varushkans who refused to let the Senate take the Iron Roads.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the Temple is compared with the grand stone basilicas of Bastion.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Deryn notes that the Empire threw itself into the fray whenever the Jotun threatened Bregasland.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: freeing Brocéliande from the taint of Spring magic is cited as one dream among many.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Eirwen of Mountains Slumber, who urges the Navarr to build civilisation, is based in Hercynia.
t.Holberg: The Splintered House wayhouse makes Holberg one of the territories the Navarr wayhouses could choose as the focus of a shared dream.
t.Liathaven: Deryn lived in Liathaven until Vision's End steading was lost. He asks why there is no drive to recover the territory and what might have been had Navarr generals sworn to die defending it.
t.Miaren: The completed Temple of the Waking Dream has made Seren the City of Dreams, drawing visionaries to it and giving every congregation in Miaren Goosewhisper Infusion and an extra liao.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is cited as one of the Marcher lands the Empire always rallies to defend against the Jotun.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold is cited as one of the Marcher lands the Empire always rallies to defend against the Jotun.
t.Ossium: The Awstin's Rest wayhouse makes Ossium a possible focus for the Navarr wayhouses' shared dream.
t.Reikos: The Micah's Stand wayhouse makes Reikos a possible focus for the Navarr wayhouses' shared dream.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is not named on the page; the League's only stake here is the wayhouse in Holberg.
t.Skarsind: The Ashen Tears wayhouse makes Skarsind a possible focus for the Navarr wayhouses' shared dream.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens hold the Last Battle wayhouse and the newly built Caedwynn's Hold. Caedwynn's Hold's Keeper, due to be appointed by the Navarr senators, could join the wayhouse meeting if appointed in time.
t.Therunin: Deryn cites Therunin's fall to the Druj and the vallorn as proof of Navarr sacrifice. Thousands of Navarr died, Thornsong House and Peakedge Stead were destroyed, and the Thimble was lost.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Urizeni readiness to fight if the Empire abandoned Zenith is cited as an example of leverage.

r.Holberg/Utterlund: Home to the Splintered House, one of the five Navarr wayhouses eligible to be chosen for the shared dream.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: Home to Awstin's Rest, one of the five Navarr wayhouses eligible to be chosen for the shared dream.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: Home to Micah's Stand, one of the five Navarr wayhouses eligible to be chosen for the shared dream.
r.Skarsind/Skogei Glens: Home to the Ashen Tears, one of the five Navarr wayhouses eligible to be chosen for the shared dream.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Last Battle wayhouse stands here on lands the Karass claim as their own, and is one of the wayhouses that could be chosen for the shared dream.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Deryn laments that all the work clearing the vallorn from Eastring has been undone in a way that cannot be resolved without uniting the vallornhearts.

Fair share of labour.d: The Guild's manifesto covers artisans and the study, innovation and creation of magic items, without conflicting with the Apothecaries' Guild or the Conclave. If ratified, it would take the power to enjoin magic items and disseminate schemas from the Senate, resolving what the magistrate called the Conclave's overreach in interdicting items. Four titles would automatically be appointed by the Guild, and seven more could be. Estavus offered schemas, the Carmine Band promised donations to the Golden Pyramid for its support, Treji's artisans proposed a great work in Hercynia, and Jasna Kazimerczyk urged the Pride Assembly to back the Guild. The magistrate also warned that the name was confusingly similar to the Apothecaries' Guild and risked suggesting League ties.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Pyramid's grandmaster, expected to rally Conclave support, is named as Terentia of Sarangrave Reforged.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Prosperity Assembly is noted as having a highest calling to discharge in Feroz, after which it may have views on sodalities.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Jasna recalls years of travelling to Anvil in Casinea to campaign for artisans' recognition.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting is listed among titles that the Senate could make appointable by the Guild.
n.Navarr: The artisans and brokers of Treji hope to win over Navarr senators to back the Guild, and offered a great work to boost Hercynia's mines and forests if it passes.
n.The League: The magistrate warned that the term 'Guild', common in League business, risked giving the sodality an apparent League affiliation and narrowing its appeal to other nations.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are recalled as having enslaved Treji's artisans to make weapons and magic items after conquering Hercynia.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Jasna reflects that had Urizen been a nation of artisans rather than magicians, the Conclave would have been a hall of craftspeople.
n.Varushka: Jasna Kazimerczyk, a Varushkan artisan and former Assembly preacher, wrote to her old allies across the north and urged the Pride Assembly to make supporting new sodalities its highest calling.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Jasna remembers travelling to Casinea each season to lobby in Anvil before giving up in frustration.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Prosperity Assembly's highest calling is noted as being discharged in Feroz.
t.Hercynia: If the Guild became a sodality, the Empire could commission a great work at Treji to raise investment in Hercynia's forests and mines, overseen by the Broker of Treji Wayhouse.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Jasna gives a Biting Blade each year to young schlacta defending the vales of Perumaki in Miekarova from wolves.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave appears only in the name of the Golden Pyramid's grandmaster, Terentia of Sarangrave Reforged.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting could be made a Guild appointment by Senate motion.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Seer of the Spiral Sword is one of four titles that would automatically become Guild appointments if the sodality is created.

r.Hercynia/The Glen of Shadows: Treji in the Glen of Shadows would host the proposed Starsrest or Goodfellow Brokerage, costing 12 weirwood and 36 crowns, which can only be built if the Senate approves the Guild.
r.Miekarova/Perumaki: Mentioned in passing: the vales of Perumaki are Jasna's home, where she arms young schlacta against wolves.

Forward into depthless dark.d: The Gryphon's Pride, Lions of Adelmar, Quiet Step, Black Thorns and Citadel Guard fought the White Lions, Hidden Widow, Jagged Claws, Red Lizard and Black Wind. The Northern Eagle's sabotage kept the garrisons of the Witness, Spires of Rarckan and Beacon of Iskrid out of the fighting. Lower Saarnath fell, costing a thousand Imperial lives, while the Druj suffered far worse. The Vileshrike sept, with Night heralds, hid Dripping Tor behind a magnitude 120 shroud and raised three Night Shackles. These threatened to make Lower Saarnath, Upper Saarnath and Beladrarsh terror-stricken. An Autumn Equinox battle offered a chance to break the shackles and finish off the Beacon.

n.Dawn: The Gryphon's Pride spearheaded the conquest, while the Lions of Adelmar, fighting beside Elodian's Knights of Glory, shielded their Navarri and Urizeni allies. The Lions' general was charged with recovering the Chain of the Hammerwright.
n.Druj: The Druj lost Lower Saarnath, suffered heavy losses and saw the Beacon of Iskrid in Leen almost destroyed. Meanwhile the Vileshrike ghulai prepared to curse their own subjects with the Delirium King's terror.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns advanced cautiously to preserve lives, while the Quiet Step used ambushes and poison and set a watch on the shrouded Dripping Tor. The Thorns' general must kill the het Huk'nar Skintwister.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard spent the season working the Technique of the Transcendent Claw, which left the Beacon of Iskrid barely standing. An Urizeni Spring coven could finish it by casting Thunderous Deluge on a broken shackle.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle collapsed passes and bridges and destroyed caches, so that the Druj fortification garrisons could not intervene. They also scouted for the other armies before vanishing to plan their next strike.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which lets captured or vallorn-stricken citizens choose a painless death, extends into Brocéliande.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: the Druj armies were still battered from fighting there, and similar Night heralds had been met there months earlier.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: some of the armies joining the invasion marched from Ossium.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Empire seized Lower Saarnath, and the Beacon of Iskrid was left in ruins. Dripping Tor now lies hidden under Night magic while the Vileshrikes threaten neighbouring regions with a terror curse.
t.Sarangrave: The invading armies marched out of northern Sarangrave. The Axou of Thornfen mobilised in the hope of keeping the supply route into the Salt Flats open.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: some of the armies joining the invasion came from Semmerholm.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step's general left its defence to Varushkan cousins and hoped the campaign would draw its citizens away from Agramant; Kaela's Gift also extends there.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: some of the armies came from Zenith, and the season's nightmares were said to be worse than those reported during its liberation.

r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Beladrarsh: Druj armies passed through its marshes with little help from the ruling Skinweavers. Its seven subject septs face the Shackle of Anguish curse unless the Empire breaks it, which could win a diplomatic victory.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Leen Rarckan: In the city of Leen the Beacon of Iskrid, seat of Prince Tristain the Golden, was battered by Urizeni storm magic and left barely standing. Scouts confirmed that armies cannot move between Leen Rarckan and Upper Saarnath without an opportunity.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Lower Saarnath: The region was conquered entirely by the Empire after a season of forest fighting. Its people now face terror from the Shackle of Sorrow unless the curse is stopped.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Sydathian Fens: Mentioned in passing: the Northern Eagle's general named the Sydathian Fens as the army's destination in his address.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Upper Saarnath: Imperial forces fought Vileshrike-backed Druj on the slopes rising toward this plateau, the gateway to Ûrinth. It is threatened by the Shackle of Misery curse and cannot be used to reach Leen Rarckan directly.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Ûrinth: Mentioned in passing: described as the centre of the Salt Flats and a remaining Druj stronghold, reached through Upper Saarnath.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: Mentioned in passing: the Axou of Thornfen were mobilising to advance to the Fens of Varreth, hopefully keeping the supply route open.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial armies marched through the Turan Flats on their way into Sanath.

Good as gold.d: Shortly before the Summer Solstice, Grendel wave riders seized Gelberg near the mouth of the Couros; someone had clearly betrayed his whereabouts. An attempted rescue through the Sentinel Gate ran into a trap, and he remains a living prisoner. His team published their report: the Visitors Docks of Hedra in Hedrossan, Necropolis, costing 100 white granite, 20 mithril and 360 crowns, taking 12 months. It would give congregations in Necropolis, Bastion, Morrow and Redoubt 36 rings each per season, but only once the Grand Inspiration of the Way is complete. It is available until the end of Summer 390YE. A student revealed Gelberg had an unfinished idea for creating coastal access where geography forbids it.

n.Grendel: Grendel wave riders penetrated Imperial defences to abduct Professor Gelberg, foiled the rescue attempt with a trap, and show no sign of releasing him.
n.Highguard: Gelberg judged Highborn Necropolis and Bastion the lands most in need of investment, blaming the Grand Inspiration of the Way for absorbing Highguard's wealth, yet the proposed docks depend on that monument's completion to draw pilgrims.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr-held Therunin marked one end of the stretch of the Couros the appraisal was asked to consider.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Morrow and Redoubt already benefit from significant great works, but would still gain 36 rings each season for their congregations if the Hedra docks are built.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark merchants are listed among the traders who use the port of Hedra.

t.Bastion: Bastion, home of the Grand Inspiration a short journey from Hedra, would see its congregations receive 36 rings each season from pilgrims once the docks and the monument are complete.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar marked the far end of the river stretch the appraisal was asked to examine.
t.Morrow: Morrow's congregations would gain 36 rings each season from pilgrim donations if the proposed Hedra docks are built and the Grand Inspiration finished.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis, judged the place where the most good could be done, is the proposed site of the Visitors Docks, which would give its congregations 36 rings each season after the Grand Inspiration is complete.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt's congregations would receive 36 rings each season from the pilgrim trade if the Hedra docks great work is completed.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Therunin was named as the starting point of the Couros stretch the scholars were tasked to appraise.

r.Necropolis/Hedrossan: The port-town of Hedra in Hedrossan, already a trading hub boosted by the diplomatenschloss, is where the Visitors Docks great work would be built to receive passenger vessels bound for the White City.

Goodwill.d: Dawn opened Greenwood Manor so that units across the Empire could quest against the vallorn, subject to a Senate motion. Gwinthav offered vials of Whitesmoke if Whitesmoke Brook is diverted at the Flame of the Phoenix. Hayaak offered the Eastern Sky the Slay the Monsters order if its general swears to oppose tyranny. The Earl's Council was asked to endorse the highest calling. Navarr visiting Highguard prompted proposals for a Vallornguard office in Tabernacle, an appraisal for a grand chancery, and having the Vallornguard elect the general of the Pilgrim's Defiance. The Necropolis Stewards recovered Rhonwen's cursed wand. The Great Forest Orcs urged the Conclave to interdict magical deforestation or place Surut under enmity.

n.Dawn: Dawn gained several vallorn-focused opportunities: an Effervescent Brook ministry, Hayaak's offer to the Eastern Sky, and an invitation for the Earl's Council to back the Assembly's highest calling to unlock further preparations.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the current war with the Druj is cited as a conflict that would become a lesser priority if Dawn's earls endorse the vallorn as its highest calling.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: battles against the Grendel in the south are named among conflicts Dawn would deprioritise by focusing on the vallorn.
n.Highguard: Highguard welcomed visiting Navarr and offered to host the Vallornguard, with proposals for an office in Tabernacle, a grand chancery appraisal, and letting the Vallornguard elect the general of the Pilgrim's Defiance.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: battles against the Jotun in the west are named among conflicts Dawn would deprioritise by focusing on the vallorn.
n.Navarr: Navarr shared their accumulated wisdom with Highguard to support the Vallornguard, aided the Necropolis Stewards in recovering Rhonwen's wand, and relayed the Great Forest Orcs' appeal against Surut and magical deforestation.

t.Astolat: Diverting Whitesmoke Brook through the regio of the Flame of the Phoenix in Astolat could create a ministry yielding vials of Whitesmoke for vallorn-fighting rituals.
t.Casinea: Casinea was named as one of two possible sites the Senate could appraise for a grand Vallornguard chancery.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Miaren is listed as a possible recipient of Rhonwen's cursed wand.
t.Necropolis: The Stewards of the Necropolis, aided by Navarri historians, recovered Rhonwen's cursed wand and asked the Highborn Assembly who should receive it to speak with her shade.
