t.Reikos: Reikos could host a Vallornguard headquarters in the rebuilt Unbound Steel Hall in Tabernacle, and was proposed as a possible site for a grand Vallornguard chancery.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr character laments that folk are dying in Therunin while the fight against the vallorn stalls.

r.Astolat/Grovesyard: The Effervescent Brook ministry would be built in Grovesyard, giving the Tender of the Phoenix Flame access to vials of Whitesmoke for one year.
r.Reikos/Riverwatch: A Vallornguard Office sinecure could be commissioned in Riverwatch, rebuilding the ruined Unbound Steel Hall as the sodality's headquarters and providing an income to its Speaker.

Here you come again.d: Sinokenon could not help find black lotus, which the Druj conceal, but offered aid with one of three projects if the Conclave accepted. Eleonaris asked the Freeborn to host a soiree for her heralds before a parley with Archmage Mirella. The Lictors judged that the anti-sacrifice proscription was not a jurisdictional overstep, offered three bounty bonds to Beaters, Thief-Takers and Wardens, and arranged trade through the City of Gold and Lead. A wounded Lashonar agreed to an informal parley. Surut agreed to parley but vowed to keep supporting the Druj. Llofir questioned the trod-network interdiction and offered a magnitude 100 Hallow of the Green World on the Mallum to hasten the Druj collapse.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris praises her friends in Dawn and the balls of Astolat and Semmerholm, and Llofir asks what the trod interdiction means for Dawnish magicians.
n.Druj: Surut vowed never to withdraw support from the Druj, while Llofir offered a Hallow of the Green World over the Mallum to bring sickness and ruin and speed their collapse. Sinokenon noted that their wards make black lotus almost impossible to locate.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Mareave, which the Grendel held, was named as a place Sinokenon would send ministers to help the Imperial Orcs if the Conclave chose that option.
n.Imperial Orcs: Sinokenon told the orc Archmage of Day, Skywise Gralka, that it could not find black lotus, but it offered to send ministers to help the Unshackled build their nation. Unshackled Thief-Takers were among the few permitted to bid for the Lictors' bonds, and the orc Bloodcrow Arora won a parley with Surut.
n.Jotun: Llofir warned that the coral husks are evolving new strains and that the Jotun, like the Winterfolk and Marchers, must adapt their tactics or be subsumed.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Archmage of Spring, Arwydd Clearbramble, was invited to parley with Llofir over the interdiction on completing the trod network. Lashonar said it had recently sung with the Navarr and sent servants to aid them in Therunin.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage of Day could approach the Dragons of Otkodov, then held by Thule, about black lotus, though Sinokenon doubted it would help.
n.Varushka: Varushkan Wardens were among the only citizens allowed to bid green iron for the Lictors' three bounty bonds, and Llofir questioned what the trod interdiction meant for Varushkan magicians.
n.Wintermark: Llofir confirmed that the coral husks haunting the Gullet between the Marches and Wintermark come from Spring, and warned that the Winterfolk must adapt as the husks grow more complex.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris's courtiers are said to love the grand balls held in the castles of Astolat.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Lashonar recalled aiding the Navarr in Brocéliande shortly before the Conclave declared enmity against it.
t.Forest of Ulnak: If the Empire cast Llofir's proposed Hallow of the Green World on the Mallum, its effects would also be felt in the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Mareave: Under one of Sinokenon's proposals, the eternal would send ministers to Mareave to help the Imperial Orcs build their nation, if the Conclave accepted.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Dragons of Otkodov were suggested as a possible source of help with black lotus, though Sinokenon was not confident of success.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Citadel Guard stationed in the Salt Flats could serve as the focus for Llofir's proposed Hallow of the Green World, and the ruinous effects would be concentrated there.
t.Sarangrave: Eleonaris demanded an explanation for the delayed frieze celebrating the joint victory in the Sarangrave as the first item of her parley.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris's courtiers are said to love the grand balls held in the castles of Semmerholm.
t.Skarsind: Under one of Sinokenon's proposals, the eternal would send ministers to Skarsind to help the Unshackled build their nation, if the Conclave accepted.
t.Therunin: Lashonar said it had already sent servants to Therunin so that those fighting the darkness there could speak to one another.

Hidden inventory.d: Brittashal was offered as an edifice in Valasmark, Hahnmark, costing 14 white granite and 42 crowns and available until Autumn Solstice 389YE. If built, it would add the Defiant Jackdaw banner schema to Runesmith's Law and create the Warcaller, a martial title chosen by the Wintermark Assembly. The runesmiths asked the Cat's Graces to find a weaver for a new war banner, paying five thrones, and asked the Benefactor of Regalia to make it the Warcaller's regalia. They would then enchant it as a Defiant Jackdaw. The Empire could also research the lost banner Foe-Slayer. Koskinen invited Winterfolk to a conjunction to Tanikipari, which Raal Dunn will allocate.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Empress Britta is recalled as having died in Skarsind, now held by the Imperial Orcs.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, though the hylje speak of the mysterious orcs of Fjorknae and of an Imperial smugglers' cove in Tromsa, both lands held by the Jotun.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Empress Britta is remembered as having died at the hands of the Thule.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's artisans proposed a banner hall, a new Warcaller title and an artefact banner to inspire a new generation of banner-bearers in Britta's mould. The hylje also invited the Winterfolk to share stories of their heroes at the Festival of Autumn's Easing.

t.Fjorknae: The hylje reaffirmed their wish to help the Empire learn about the mysterious orcs of Fjorknae and their monstrous akhlut allies, through the Sail into the Cold voyage once the Tromsa cove is complete.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark would host Brittashal, an expansion of Valashal in Valasmark to display banners and record Wintermark's martial history, if the commission is built.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Kallavesa is not directly named on the page.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the Sea of Snow is not directly named on the page.
t.Sermersuaq: A conjunction to the shore of Atkonaroq in Sermersuaq was identified for the Festival of Autumn's Easing, when Koskinen is to be married and crowned as one of the Palliko.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as the place where Empress Britta met her untimely death.
t.Tromsa: The Palliko welcomed the Empire's commission of another smugglers' cove in Tromsa, which once complete will open the Sail into the Cold voyage towards Fjorknae.
t.Tsirku: The hylje cannot aid exploration of Tsirku against its baleful Northern lights without three measures of stardust, though Koskinen said two rings of ilium would suffice instead.

r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: Valasmark is the proposed site of Brittashal, an expansion of Valashal to display banners and paintings of the Empire's great banners and inspire new heroes.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: A 60-minute conjunction for 50 people to the shore of Atkonaroq in Tanikipari opens at 20:15 on the Saturday of the Autumn Equinox, with the Mediator of the Hyljehal choosing who goes.

If we never meet again.d: Jarm publicised the Empire's confirmation that a Volkevaar coven under Professor Eva Giersan conjured Cold Sun, and the Commonwealth had to accept a ceasefire fixing their borders. The two powers are not cooperating, and Jarm is extending protection to neutral border states. Both nations offered paid mercenary ventures to Imperial military units. Fuchsbach put all Commonwealth opportunities on hold and dismissed the Rod and Shield and Golden Pyramid. Imperial fleets were barred from Murolosch and faced worse trade at Volkavaar and Leerdam. In Jarm, the Celestial Arch helped secure the ceasefire. The Sevenfold Path deepened ties with the Convocation of Virtue, but Lord-Magister Trescher grew suspicious. Professor Gelberg remains a Grendel prisoner.

n.Dawn: The House of Princes particularly sought Dawnish warrior-wizards for its Jarm Against Oblivion venture, and Dawnish military units taking it gain a bonus to their effective rank.
n.Grendel: Grendel captors still hold Professor Gelberg after a failed Imperial rescue. The attempt convinced them he is worth more alive, and a ransom remains possible but likely expensive.
n.Highguard: Highborn ambassadors Thaumiel and Cyrus delivered the revelations that reshaped eastern diplomacy. The Commonwealth still sends Soldatentrunk to the General of the Granite Pillar and seeks Highborn soldiers as mercenaries, while the Hexenjäger Academy opportunity is on hold. A strongly supported Assembly statement denouncing the disclosure might salvage relations.
n.The League: Both Jarm and the Commonwealth particularly sought League professionals for their campaigns against Cold Sun, offering League military units a rank bonus. Meanwhile, Jarmish pilgrims began using the new pilgrim's house in the League city of Apulian.
n.Urizen: Jarm especially sought Urizeni warrior-wizards for its campaign against Cold Sun. Prince Mila singled out Ibiss Briarheart and the Urizeni for their wisdom in seeing the value of trade with the Principalities.

t.Spiral: The Wayward House, a pilgrim's house in Apulian, was completed and welcomed the first Jarmish pilgrims in some time. They brought star jewels for the Sevenfold Path's vault, a gift that will continue each season while the house stands.

Islands in the dream.d: Lost in woods confounded by Ossium's dream enchantment, the party was guided by a herald of the Night Singer to Dimmorden, now a walled village twice its former size after several hundred kin left Thule-held Webwood. Three dimwalkers lead the sept. They believe ancestors dwell in a dream-world called the Dark Forest, that bad ancestors rise from the Nightmare, and that six precepts mark a good ancestor. They do not count the Thule as people. They refused to let the Illarawm build bridges to their ancestors. Their missing families remain scattered across Ghul'Thak, and conquering the region this season would bring 2,000 strength from the Dreamers and 2,000 from Irra Harah. It would also let the Winter Sun issue a Break the Chains order there.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: an attack on Ghul'Thak could be launched from the Dawnish-held Barrens, and the Karass of the Barrens are named as an earlier Unshackled contact.
n.Druj: The Dreamers despise the Druj, raid them constantly, and fear the Druj will slaughter the half of their sept still held in Ghul'Thak rather than lose it, as they nearly did with the Great Forest Orcs.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun, who could otherwise break the chains in Ghul'Thak, is currently in Grendel-held Mareave.
n.Highguard: Highborn who had armed and trained the Dreamers accompanied the expedition as advisors, were keenly interested in the sept's six precepts, and are among those the Dreamers ask to rescue their kin.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Unshackled assembly led the expedition under its highest calling. The Dreamers rejected sharing their ancestors with the Illarawm and grew guarded on learning Bloodcrow Knott had been executed, but they asked the Imperial Orcs to help reunite their sept.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarri magicians have granted Irra Harah access to the Forest of Ulnak, and the Druj use of the vallorn in Therunin is cited.
n.Thule: The Dreamers regard the Thule as barely better than the Druj and not truly people. They resent Otkodov for having held their Webwood kin, and Thule agreement to use Oerwealt would offer a bridgehead into Ghul'Thak.
n.Varushka: Varushkans who had worked with the Dreamers advised the expedition. The sept trades regularly with its Varushkan neighbours, has built a Varushkan-style walled village, and credits Varushkan spirit magic with clarifying its ancestors' voices.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Half the Dreamers' sept is scattered across Ulnak's Ghul'Thak Forest. Freeing them requires conquering that region against Druj armies and the garrisons of Cassad Ûln and the Thistle of Barbs.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun is stationed in Mareave and so cannot reach Ulnak to break the chains this season.
t.Ossium: A Spirit enchantment over Ossium confounded travel through its woods and gave the Dreamers unusually vivid dreams of their ancestors, while the Unshackled met the sept at Dimmorden in Echofell.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Thule of Otkodov begrudgingly let several hundred Dreamer kin leave Webwood, which has not endeared them to the sept.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Druj use of the vallorn in Sarangrave reinforces the Dreamers' fear that the Druj will destroy entire septs.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Dreamers earlier ignored the opportunity to leave Ossium and travel to Skarsind.
t.The Barrens: Without Thule agreement to use Oerwealt, an Imperial attack to free the Dreamers' kin in Ghul'Thak would need to come from the Barrens.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Druj use of the vallorn in Therunin is cited as evidence of their willingness to destroy rather than lose control.

r.Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest: The three missing families of the Dreamers are spread across Ghul'Thak. An Imperial attack this season would gain 2,000 strength from the Dreamers and 2,000 from Irra Harah, and would allow a Break the Chains order there.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt: Thule-held Oerwealt could serve as a bridgehead for an attack on Ghul'Thak, if the Thule agree.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Mentioned in passing: twice a year the Dreamers trek to Stinking Market in Drownbark to sell raid spoils and buy metal goods.
r.Ossium/Echofell: The Dreamers' village of Dimmorden near the Bonehives has been rebuilt in hardwood and stone, has doubled in size, and hosted the Unshackled expedition.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Mentioned in passing: several hundred Dreamer kin formerly held by the Thule in Webwood left to join the sept in Echofell.

It's all wrong, but it's all right.d: Although the Synod repealed the proscription treating false-virtue dedications as blasphemy, Faraden Pride was injured. Imperial fleets trading with Caitun suffered a two-rank penalty, the Azure Sutannir's Faraden benefits were halved, and the families trading with the Alder of Meade and Mediator of Fisk came under pressure to end those arrangements. Faraden had begun curbing Asavean influence and signed peace with the Jotun. The Iron Confederacy sent envoys to discuss its Brass Coast holdings, the Lasambrian conquest, the Hand of Dumon and trade. It offered Imperial warbands pay and plunder for fighting the Jotun in Reinos. Another curse struck Kalino, and a Synod proscription technically branded all Suranni heretics.

n.Dawn: General Hendrick of the Black Eagle Banner wished to fight alongside Dawnish knights, offering any Dawnish military unit that joined the Reinos campaign two extra ingots of green iron regardless of experience.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page; it is linked only through its shared hold on Feroz, where the Iron Confederacy controlled the Cazar Straits.
n.Jotun: The Jotun signed a peace treaty with Faraden but faced an Iron Confederacy war of conquest against the Lasambrian Jotun in Reinos, where Imperial warbands were invited to join the Suranni and share the plunder.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn ambassadors handled both nations; the Azure Sutannir's benefits from Faraden pilgrims to Kahraman were halved, and Suranni holdings on two former Freeborn island chains were to be discussed with the Suranni delegation.
n.The Marches: The Tseriyn family, who trade mithril to the Alder of Meade for Marcher produce, were pressed to reconsider the arrangement, and Marcher captains already troubled by Jotun ships in the Gullet faced the Caitun trading penalty.
n.Wintermark: The Salagiin traders supplying ilium to the Mediator of Fisk were pushed to reconsider their dealings with Wintermark, and Winterfolk captains faced both Jotun ships in the Gullet and the Caitun trading penalty.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the bay is not named, though the Iron Confederacy's capture of the former Children of Wrecks strongholds in its island chains is discussed.
t.Feroz: The Iron Confederacy controlled the Cazar Straits in Feroz after capturing the former Children of Wrecks stronghold, and Suranni holdings in the Brass Coast were on the agenda for treaty talks.
t.Kahraman: Faraden pilgrims grew reluctant to visit the Azure Chorus's Parador of Wind and Flame, halving the Azure Sutannir's Faraden benefits, though the Sutannir might help ease Faraden concerns through a Synod judgement.
t.Kalino: Known to the Suranni as Arbonne, Kalino was struck by another Winter curse resembling Naeve's Twisting Blight; the warding temple prevented total failure but the Autumn harvest would still be poor.
t.Kallavesa: Beggar's lye from the marshes of Kallavesa forms part of the Salagiin trade with the Mediator of Fisk, which Faraden pressure now threatened.
t.Madruga: The Iron Confederacy controlled Free Landing in Madruga, taken with help from Freeborn corsairs, and its Brass Coast holdings were expected to feature in the treaty negotiations.
t.Mitwold: The mithril trade between the Tseriyn family and the Alder of Meade, restored after the Jotun occupation of Meade, was at risk unless reassurance was found for Faraden.
t.Reinos: The Iron Confederacy waged a war of conquest in the hills of Reinos, having reportedly taken several regions, and Imperial warbands were offered pay and plunder to fight alongside the Black Eagle Banner there.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: Imperial efforts had created a new maritime trade route to Faraden through the Sea of Snow.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Iron Confederacy controlled the Cazar Straits after taking the former Children of Wrecks stronghold there.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Free Landing was held by the Iron Confederacy, whose navies took it with support from Freeborn corsairs, a success that prompted the Suranni offer to Imperial mercenaries.

It's my time.d: Responding to Yrkja Riansson Sigeing's Wintermark Assembly judgement on drawing inspiration from Wintermark's legacy, Jared's judgement (378=0) sent Highborn archivists and benefactors north. Welcomed in Wintermark's halls, they found three possible causes: recovering Foe-slayer and building a hall for Wintermark's banners, compiling the history of the Witan to restore its prominence, or aiding the exploration of Tsirku. The Highborn Assembly could enact one of three competing mandates, each costing 25 liao, or none if Jared is named and goes north personally. The chosen effort would exceed expectations if it supported Wintermark, or achieve something alone. Meanwhile, Highguard could not use archivists or benefactors for peerless kinship elsewhere that season.

n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly was offered a choice of three competing mandates directing its archivists and benefactors in Wintermark, and those groups were tied up there, unavailable for other peerless kinship that season.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark stood to gain Highborn help with whichever cause the Highborn Assembly chose: the banner-bearers' hall, the restoration of the Witan, or the exploration of Tsirku.

t.Tsirku: One of the three mandates would turn Highborn benefactors and archivists to helping Wintermark face the dangers of exploring Tsirku, even if Wintermark paused the exploration over winter.

Loud and proud.d: After Kish of the Flame Beneath the Earth's statement, aspiring Highborn cantors offered the Cat's Graces 6 thrones to stage a Winter Solstice concert, which Malachi of the Custodes Clavium would attend. Eli of the Cenotaph's call for inquisitorial rooms opened a 30-crown commission amendment. If it passes, the Blade of Wisdom would give the Imperial Inquisitor a yearly focus, and Magistrate Abraham would draft legal options for restoring the Inquisitorial Court. Sister Elysium's Ambition Assembly publicly committed to finishing the Grand Inspiration by the start of 389YE, and Bastion's trade boomed. Präst Stelltus listed six signs for Zemress, and the Sumaah offered to host historical research costing 5 thrones. They expect the Synod to rule.

n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly's focus on the Grand Inspiration brought offers to Highborn cantors and inquisitors, and a 30-crown amendment for inquisitorial chambers. Bastion's businesses also prospered as pilgrims prepared for the planned opening.

t.Bastion: Pilgrims booked inns and hostels across Bastion ahead of the promised opening ceremony. As a result, every business in the territory operates one rank higher following the Autumn Equinox.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Präst Stelltus's letter setting out the Sumaah case for Zemress was delivered to the Sumaah Embassy in Necropolis.

Metamorphosis.d: Orcs evicted from Thornfen by the Axou were starving in Urizeni-held lands. The Empire could spend the Imperial Breadbasket to prevent famine, forgoing its benefits for two seasons and inevitably feeding scattered Druj warriors, or let famine run its course, crippling the Druj but inflaming anti-Imperial feeling. Rebel leaders Halyx Fire-Eyes and Agoska were coming to Anvil to meet the Imperial Consul, wanting self-rule and the Bloodwater Marsh. Agoska's Waterwalkers destroyed the last miasma pillar using a Conclave ritual. Sentinels of Urizen were offered a venture to destroy Kroll's lair, or alternatively to learn its names and ward the lair so Urizen could control it.

n.Druj: Thousands of Druj warriors scattered across the Sarangrave would profit from any Breadbasket food sent there but would be too busy surviving to cause trouble if famine ran its course, and the loss of their last miasma pillar ended their grip on the septs.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: diverting the Imperial Breadbasket to feed the Sarangrave would deny its benefits to the Marchers for two seasons.
n.Urizen: Urizen's new territory faced famine among displaced orcs gathered around its settlements, negotiations that would shape relations with the septs, and a choice for its Sentinels to destroy Kroll's lair or attempt to bind the beast to Urizeni control.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Ossium, which Varushka held, was cited as a place where the Empire's liberation of Druj-ruled septs seemed to work.

t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page concerns spending the Imperial Breadbasket, which would stop its benefits to the Marchers for two seasons.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was cited as a place where liberating septs from the Druj appeared to have worked, in contrast to the Barrens and the Sarangrave.
t.Sarangrave: The territory faced winter famine among the Thornfen exiles, Druj remnants and advancing husks, rebel demands for land and self-rule, and the threat of Kroll, but the destruction of the last miasma pillar began to lift the spirits of all its inhabitants.

r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Bendol remained lost to the vallorn; retaking it would let the Empire grant the Bloodwater Marsh to the rebels while keeping the territory, so a future promise of the Marsh was possible though the timescale was difficult.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Halyx Fire-Eyes of the Bloodwater Spears was expected to demand the Marsh for its former occupants, but ceding it would cost the Empire control of the territory and its senator unless Thornfen or Bendol were also held.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: Kroll was regenerating in its lair and could rampage if the region were attacked or reached by husks, and the Sentinels of Urizen could either destroy its three Spring-fed sacs with 7,500 force strength or divine its names and ward the lair with seven rings of ilium to control it.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The rebels holding the forest took in exiles who could fight but turned most away for lack of food, and they seemed ready to defend the region to the death, though an Imperial army could take it with minimal losses.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Axou's eviction of Thornfen's orcs under their treaty with the Empire caused the famine crisis, and Axos held the region with one army and a huge fortification that would grow harder to take as its garrison resupplied.

Mud, blood, and manacles.d: Strong Reeds sympathisers struck Jotun positions as the Empire attacked. The Jotun were caught preparing a cautious foray into Gravenmarch and lost Sallow and the Rushes. Would-be Jarl Kiergmunt was found dead in the eel ponds. The Burning Falcon broke the Jotun at Sallow Walk at heavy cost. A flanking raid by the Bounders, Strong Reeds and Sparrow's Reckoning took Ottery after Jorgen Hylasson was wounded. Ottermire fell, and the Empire got seven-tenths of the way to claiming North Fens. Thousands died, mostly Imperials. The Lictors' curse limits Jotun armies to moving one territory. Battle opportunities offered a chance to kill Friar Bloughton of House Brawness, approach the Raven Jarl about Stephen of Sarcombe, and consult Ghodi Torvi about the coral husks.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun joined the advance into Bregasland, and at Ottery enchanted Jotun warbands sought out the knights of Dawn, breaking many Dawnish shields.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the page notes only that the Knights of Glory influence first showed itself during recent fighting in the Sarangrave.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Autumn Hammers fought alongside contracted Lictors of the City of Bar and Bond and cursed every Jotun army in Bregasland, so none can move more than one territory after the Equinox.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost Sallow, the Rushes and Ottermire, and with them Bregasland, suffering heavy defeats at Sallow Walk and Ottery. Their remaining armies are bound by the Lictors' curse and fall back on Fisher's Rock.
n.The League: The untested Sparrow's Reckoning used its bravos' skill at street fighting to help storm Ottery from the east, and a League crossbowman helped seize an archer tower.
n.The Marches: The Strong Reeds, Tusks and Bounders led the liberation of Bregasland, which is Imperial again and due to be assigned by Senate motion. Marchers who fought or hold resources there may gain hearth magic benefits, while House Brawness's treachery remains to be dealt with.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks, Green Shield and Narwhal's Spear fought in the campaign, with the Bloodcloaks running field hospitals in Ottery. Under the Knights of Glory's influence, the Green Shield cannot take cautious orders for a year.

t.Bregasland: The Empire took the Rushes and Ottermire and, holding Gravenmarch, regained the territory, though North Fens and Grey Fens remain contested. Spring magic from Graven Rock continues to heal those who use its waters.
t.Hordalant: Hordalant is one of only two places the cursed Jotun armies can retreat to, and it is where House Brawness plans to flee with Jotun help.
t.Liathaven: The Tower of the North brought lumber from Liathaven to fortify Ottery, and Liathaven is the other limit of the cursed Jotun armies' retreat.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun withdrew from Mitwold the previous season, and the Odd's Way runs east from Ottermire into it.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Sallow's Walk leads toward the Mournwold, the Valiant Pegasus's crusade began there, and Stephen of Sarcombe hails from it.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian armies had headed south toward their home in Reinos, beset by the Iron Confederacy.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: recent fighting in the Sarangrave was where the Knights of Glory influence first manifested.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: an earlier Imperial attack on Skallahn drew Jotun attention away, and coral husks have come ashore there.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Sparrow's Reckoning's general addressed the bravos of Tassato in his orders.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: The Jotun had planned a cautious foray to retake Gravenmarch, but the Imperial assault overwhelmed them. Graven Rock's Spring magic still ripples outward from here.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: The Grey Walkers drive out humans and orcs alike and are one-tenth of the way to claiming the region. No Jotun army would retreat into it.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: The Empire is seven-tenths of the way to claiming North Fens, where the Jotun hold Fisher's Rock. Friar Bloughton of House Brawness can be stopped at the Whelksquay before he leads rebels west.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: The Empire won the Battle of Ottery after its townsfolk rose to help, and the Bloodcloaks set up field hospitals. Ottermire is Imperial again.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: The Strong Reeds rose here, Sallow and the Rushes fell quickly to the Empire, and would-be Jarl Kiergmunt and his household were found cut down in the eel ponds.

Not from the benevolence.d: The Senator for Reikos agreed in principle to cede Remember Exile to Ephisis for 100 wains of white granite, on condition it is not sold to the Druj or Grendel. The deal needs Senate approval, and only the General Assembly may veto. Bastion's senator, Merari Navigators of Virtue, may offer a sale next. Seven contracts were offered for auction in the Hall of Worlds. Dorys Delgorokov, Damiàn i Martàn i Erigo and Terentia of Sarangrave were invited to submit contracts of their own. Following Terentia's declaration, plans for fanes at Treji, Fisk and Drycastle now await Senate motions. Each must be ceded to Ephisis and creates a national title, but building more than one reduces each fane's tax boost.

n.Dawn: Dawn stands to gain the Drycastle Emporium in the Barrens, which would create the Dawnish title Seneschal of the Drycastle Emporium. The holder must be a yeofolk in good standing to submit contracts, and could buy warm ashes and Pauper's Keys.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the sale of Remember Exile is conditional on Ephisis not selling the fortification on to the Druj or the Grendel.
n.Grendel: The Remember Exile deal forbids Ephisis from selling the fortification on to the Grendel. A detailed Map of Tathar offered in one contract is hinted to come from a single obvious source, implying the Grendel are the counter-party.
n.Highguard: To help pay for the Grand Inspiration of the Way, the Senator for Reikos arranged, through Eli of the Cenotaph, to cede Remember Exile for 100 wains of white granite, pending Senate approval. Necropolis passed on its turn, and Bastion's senator now has the chance to offer something for sale.
n.Navarr: The proposed Treji Plaza in Hercynia would create the Navarr title Broker of the Treji Plaza. The holder must be a broker in good standing to submit contracts, and could buy warm ashes and Rings of the Golden Market.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: one of Ephisis's contracts offers the deed to Rootha's Exports, a level seven business in Sarvos, in exchange for 70 thrones.
n.Wintermark: The proposed Fisk Wareroom in Kallavesa, which grew from a scheme involving the Wintermark merchant Erlend Gunnulfsson, would create the title Mediator of the Fisk Wareroom. The holder must be a mediator or maggot in good standing to submit contracts, and could buy warm ashes and tradesoil.

t.Bastion: A herald reminded the Empire that it is Bastion's turn this summit. Senator Merari Navigators of Virtue may choose whether to offer something from the White City or elsewhere in the territory for sale to Ephisis.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named directly in the page's text.
t.Hercynia: The Treji Plaza fane is proposed here, costing 20 white granite, 40 weirwood, 10 ilium and 180 crowns. It would add 4 thrones of taxation a season, boost herb gardens and raise Hercynian characters' income by 9 rings for a year, but must be ceded to Ephisis.
t.Kallavesa: The Fisk Wareroom fane is proposed here, costing 30 white granite, 30 weirwood, 10 ilium and 180 crowns. It would add 7 thrones of taxation a season, aid military units questing or guarding, and raise Kallavesa characters' income by 12 rings for a year, but must be ceded to Ephisis.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Necropolis chose to pass on their turn to sell a feature of the territory to Ephisis.
t.Reikos: The fortification of Remember Exile would be ceded to Ephisis for 100 wains of white granite if the Senate passes the motion. Heralds of the Iron Labyrinth have already gathered at the castle with measuring and excavation tools.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: Terentia of Sarangrave is named as one of the citizens invited to submit a contract to Ephisis, and as the Grandmaster whose declaration accepted all three fanes.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the deed to Rootha's Exports, a level seven business in Sarvos, is offered as payment in one of Ephisis's contracts.
t.Tathar: Mentioned in passing: a detailed, verified Map of Tathar suitable for scrying is offered as payment for 1000 thrones in one contract.
t.The Barrens: The Drycastle Emporium fane is proposed in Dawnguard, costing 35 white granite, 25 weirwood, 10 ilium and 180 crowns. It would add 5 thrones of taxation a season, aid military units, and raise Barrens characters' income by 10 rings for a year, but must be ceded to Ephisis.

r.Hercynia/The Glen of Shadows: The Treji Plaza would be built at Treji in the Glen of Shadows, giving Ephisis's heralds free passage there and a market for the region's herb gardens to trade unwanted herbs for herbalists' tools.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: The Fisk Wareroom would be built at Fisk in Wittal Grove, letting Ephisis's heralds come and go freely and giving local questing and guarding military units a market for their goods.

Out of these convertites.d: Most of the visitors were human priests, with some orcs who were once Grendel. They worked the Mournwold fields by day and listened to the Marcher orcs by night. The Marcher orcs renounce violence but hear their warrior ancestors through sport, and League orcs playing foot-the-ball heard Rucraic, Sheanduir and even Curstag van Apulian. The page confirms that League orcs hear their ancestors as well as any other orc. Two opportunities arose. Bishops of Mestra and Regario proposed rival foot-the-ball stadia in Tassato. Greumach von Apulian proposed a Duellists Colosseum in Apulian, and Cigno's orcs argued for Sarvos instead. Monks from Boarsford Monastery plan to visit Anvil and ask that reincarnation not be discussed.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: many League orcs are former Grendel, and the Grendel view of ancestors and their gladiatorial arenas inspire the colosseum proposal.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher orcs are former Jotun thralls who still hear Jotun warrior ancestors such as Ulven, Skaldi and Raðljóst.
n.The League: League priests and orcs made the pilgrimage, and League orcs learned to hear their ancestors through foot-the-ball. The nation may now build stadia in Tassato and a Duellists Colosseum, which would create titles including Mistress of Duels.
n.The Marches: Marcher farms gained willing if inexperienced hands for the harvest, and Leaguish coin flowed into Marcher taverns. The Marcher orcs shared their beliefs and their love of foot-the-ball with the visitors.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: pilgrims from Holberg were among those who travelled to the Mournwold.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold hosted the League pilgrims, whose fields were worked by mixed crews of orcs and humans. Its orcs taught the visitors how they hear their ancestors through foot-the-ball.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos pilgrims were among the first to arrive in the Mournwold. Cigno's orc community argues that Sarvos should host the proposed Duellists Colosseum.
t.Spiral: Greumach von Apulian proposed building the Duellists Colosseum in Apulian. It would host duelling contests and cheapen military unit upgrades in the territory for a year.
t.Tassato: Tassato's pilgrims arrived first, and rival bishops of Mestra and Regario proposed foot-the-ball stadia so the twin cities could field teams against the Marches and each other.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: pilgrims from Temeschwar followed the first arrivals to the Mournwold.

r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: A party of orc monks from Boarsford Monastery in Chalkdowns set out to meet League pilgrims at Anvil and talk of ancestors, but not reincarnation.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Cigno's League orcs proposed it as a central, wealthy home for the Duellists Colosseum as an alternative to Apulian.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Bishop Leonore Fidalgo di Mestra proposed a stadium and foot-the-ball team for Mestra, available as a commission until the end of the Summer Solstice 389YE.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Bishop Luis Calazan di Regario drew up plans for a rival stadium and team in Regario, on the other side of the river.

Outreach across the marshes.d: The visit followed the League Assembly's call to bring others into the Empire. The Sand Fishers are deeply grateful to the Empire and devoted to the Virtues, but they have four main objections. They cherish self-rule of Misericorde. They would be financially worse off, since they currently receive defence and education without paying taxes. Their reincarnation beliefs could see them executed under Imperial law. They also fear sharing culpability for massacres like those in the Barrens. Practical worries include losing League control of the Flaxen Pillars and the draining of Rebeshof and Utterlund. Three Hands will meet the League at Lia Adelaar's camp at 4pm on Saturday. Arios von Temeschwar also discovered that the sept is secretly drilling a small mithril-armed force.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers' horror at the conquest of the Barrens and the massacres of the septs there is cited, but Dawn itself is not named.
n.Druj: The Sand Fishers' decades of brutal Druj rule shape every objection they raise. They now suspect their belief in reincarnation was a lie the Druj spread to crush their spirits, and they refuse to belong to an Empire that imitates the Druj.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Sand Fishers have studied war magic with the Imperial Orcs in Skarsind, and the recent execution of the Imperial Orc Bloodcrow Knott for failing to observe the Doctrines feeds the sept's fears.
n.The League: League merchant princes pinned down why the Sand Fishers hesitate and concluded the problem cannot be solved with money. The League's leaders now have a rare chance at Anvil to address the sept's concerns and bring them into the nation.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers' communal decision-making is likened to the approach used by most Urizen spires.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers do not imagine they could have stopped the Varushkans wiping out the Montanians in the Barrens.

t.Holberg: Holberg's diplomats sought to bring its Sand Fisher neighbours in Misericorde into the Empire. Questions now hang over the Flaxen Pillars, the drained wetlands of Rebeshof and Utterlund, and a small orc army training within the territory.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is recalled as where the Sand Fishers suffered brutal Druj rule before the Empire freed them.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is not named, and the page touches the wider League only through references such as the Apulian Orcs having already joined the League.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: members of the sept have been sent to Skarsind to study war magic with the Imperial Orcs.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is not named. The nearest references are the Apulian Orcs' joining the League and the Sarcophan enclave on the Alivetti estates, which enjoys similar benefits without taxation.
t.The Barrens: The treatment of the Rahvin, Black Wind, Vendarri and Montanians during the conquest of the Barrens horrified the Sand Fishers. It is a key reason they fear sharing culpability for Imperial actions.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: The merchant princes visited Misericorde, which the Sand Fishers treasure as their self-ruled paradise and are reluctant to give up. Arios von Temeschwar found a hidden camp there where the sept is drilling perhaps five hundred soldiers in mithril arms and armour.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: The Adelaarskade dykes are slowly draining Rebeshof's wetlands, which will lose their marsh quality by Spring 389YE. The Sand Fishers worry no one, themselves included, will farm the new land.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund's marshes are being drained into farmland and will lose their marsh quality by Spring 389YE. The sept fears neither they nor League citizens will want to settle and farm there.

Rebellion's Ridge.d: The six Ore Hills rebels, recognised as exemplars of Pride in Winter 386YE, are honoured by Rebellion's Ridge. It was built by Alfred Aewulfson-Boon under an Imperial Wayleave, and Jedediah Boon's writ of consecration was upheld 296-10. If the General Assembly enacts the consecration mandate, every personal resource in the Mournwold suffers a two-rank penalty for a season, and from the Spring Equinox the Mournwold senator would be chosen by mine owners rather than farmers. If it is not enacted, Marcher priests in the Mournwold could preach rebellion to stoke the miners' anger. The egregores confirmed there is no compromise and that no other Marcher territory would be affected.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the writ describes the Mournwold as a territory stricken by the Jotun bootheel time and time again.
n.The Marches: Marcher priests and the General Assembly faced a generational choice over whether Mournwold miners or farmers choose their senator. The egregores warned of possible strife between cousins, and either outcome risked shunning, rough music or worse within the nation.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland is cited as a place where land, as in the Marches generally, means farmland.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is cited as farmland country. The page says the Mournwold decision would not change how it is governed.
t.Mournwold: If the consecration were enacted, personal resources here would suffer a two-rank penalty for a season and mine owners would elect the senator from the Spring Equinox. If it were refused, priests could preach rebellion to the miners.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is cited as farmland country. The page says the Mournwold decision would not change how it is governed.

r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The region gives its name to the Ore Hills Rebellion, whose six leaders Rebellion's Ridge commemorates. Their legacy was now at the heart of the struggle between the Mournwold's miners and farmers.

Rebuild Binding Oak Spire.d: Velasco i Guerra, Senator for Kahraman, proposed the motion and Bartimaeus, Senator for Sarangrave, seconded it. It followed the Architect of Hammers' announcement the previous season, and Architect Noether drew up the spire's design. The cost was set by the opportunity, with 70 thrones in labour and three months to complete. Able the Taller of Sarangrave Reforged paid the 70 thrones after the Autumn Equinox, so the project was self-funded. Once complete, the Arch of the Sky produces an additional two wains of white granite, and its custodian can purchase further wains. In return, the investment that businesses in Zenith received from the Bridge of the Air was removed and redirected to support the quarry workers.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, and the only link is that the Senator for Sarangrave, a territory they held, seconded the motion.
n.Urizen: Urizen gains a rebuilt spire in Zenith that boosts white granite production at the Arch of the Sky. The cost is that Zenith's businesses lose their investment from the Bridge of the Air.

t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: Bartimaeus, Senator for Sarangrave, seconded the motion, and Able the Taller of Sarangrave Reforged funded the labour costs.
t.Zenith: Zenith's Arch of the Sky quarry produces two extra wains of white granite and can buy more, but businesses in the territory lose their Bridge of the Air investment, which is redirected to the quarry workers.

r.Zenith/Proceris: The Binding Oak Spire is rebuilt in Proceris to Architect Noether's design, taking three months to complete.

Roses in the snow.d: Scouts found a mile-wide hole, possibly a starfall crater, and an ice-bound Thule outpost holding a score of buried Otkodov orcs. They also met an observing eternal in the form of a veiled orc skier. The scops may name the region. Winter doubles the strength needed to explore Tsirku, and the Imperial Spymaster chooses where explorers go next. Varushka's Assembly could pass competing mandates favouring treasure-hunting over exploration. Over five thousand Wintermark soldiers slaughtered Wemba's band, and Wemba is to face questioning and justice. Every Silent Bell member who entered Tsirku vanished, and the Whisper Gallery claimed this as revenge for Bella and Heliodoro, ending the sodality. Agramant offered to lure Kaarina White-Eye to the Grave of the Giants for Imperial heroes to kill.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish knights are cited as the sort who might have sought one-on-one glory against Wemba, in contrast with Wintermark's heroism.
n.Imperial Orcs: Varushka's alternative Synod mandate, if enacted, would let Imperial Orc units undertake the Adventure in Tsirku without penalty and grant strong units extra treasures, at the cost of slowing exploration.
n.Jotun: Kaarina White-Eye has long harried the Jotun from the northern ice in revenge for her Thane, and Agramant claims to be tired of her complaints about them. Any Jotun name for the region north of Warriors' Gate has not stuck.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr messenger delivered the Whisper Gallery's bloody masks and knife to Major Joshua Benson's grave at Pickham.
n.Thule: Explorers found a frozen Thule outpost north of Warriors' Gate, with a score of dead Otkodov orcs, including the warlock Deyadloth of the High Pass, buried before it. They marked the site and withdrew to avoid a diplomatic incident.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan National Assembly may pass one of two competing mandates encouraging Winter treasure-hunting in Tsirku. One rewards only Varushkan units; the other extends the benefits to Wintermark and the Imperial Orcs. Either would reduce exploration strength.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's soldiers cut down Wemba the Bloody's band and brought him in chains to their camp for questioning. Its scops may name Tsirku's new region and its crater, and its egregores are to arrange for the Spymaster to address the muster.

t.Otkodov: Orcs of Otkodov were found dead and buried at an ice-bound Thule outpost in Tsirku, decorated with Otkodov's five-headed dragon. The unexplored eastern region of Tsirku may border Otkodov's Urdur.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the western region of Tsirku may connect to the Sea of Snow, whose great beasts come to die at the Grave of the Giants.
t.Sermersuaq: Wemba the Bloody was dragged back through Sermersuaq on his way to Anvil. Agramant offered to lure Kaarina White-Eye back to the Grave of the Giants at the Winter Solstice if the Vigilance assembly urged watch over it.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: an unexplored barren, windswept region of Tsirku lies westward towards Tromsa.
t.Tsirku: The region north of Warriors' Gate was partly explored, revealing a vast crater, a dead Thule outpost and a watching eternal. Winter now doubles the effort needed to map further. Wemba was captured here, Kaarina White-Eye lurks east of Warriors' Gate, and the Silent Bell vanished here.

r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: the great hole in Tsirku is compared with the ilium-bearing starfall that struck Sküld in recent years.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Mentioned in passing: an unexplored ominous region of Tsirku lies eastward towards Urdur and may abut it, raising the chance of a Thule presence there.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Mentioned in passing: Kaarina White-Eye once struck out of Suaq Fount to harry the Jotun before abandoning her camps for Tsirku about a year ago.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Mentioned in passing: Kaarina White-Eye once struck out of Suaq Wastes to harry the Jotun before abandoning her camps for Tsirku about a year ago.
r.Tsirku/Warriors' Gate: Warriors' Gate is the base from which explorers pushed north into the nameless icy region. Two further unexplored regions border it, and Kaarina White-Eye is believed to be somewhere east of it.

Salt lions.d: Five armies joined the Wolves of War in Mareave, all enchanted with Day magic's Clarity and aided by Summer citadels, bronze giants and Polemarchs of the Master Strategist. The Wolves, Eastern Sky and Fire of the South attacked, while the Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave and Winter Sun defended Clisearn's Imperial quarter. Four Day-enchanted Grendel armies, backed by forces camped in Fleisardh and by navies bringing supplies, repelled every probe. The Spring curse kept losses down: the Empire lost just over a thousand soldiers and the Grendel more. The Golden Winds had withdrawn after the poisoning of their wells. A battle opportunity followed at the Syagrian Haven to collapse the Icarion tunnels and to coerce the Asavean prefectoi Zarides into standing down the Quintian Spears.

n.Dawn: The Eastern Sky, with a great host of warbands under captains from every nation but Navarr, attacked the Grendel lines in southern Mareave, and Dawnish lives were among those put at risk by the bitter fighting.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: invoked in the Eastern Sky's orders recalling battles in the Barrens, and by a Grendel admiral who called the poisoning of wells a Druj tactic.
n.Grendel: The Grendel held their conquered three-quarters of Clisearn with four Day-enchanted armies and naval supply, and suffered heavier losses than the Empire. The Golden Winds fled after their wells were poisoned, and their navies began building a temporary beachhead beneath Icarion's cliffs.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar held a quiet defensive line in Clisearn, while the Seventh Wave's scouts uncovered the Grendel scheme at Icarion. The Seventh Wave's general may also pursue a Polemarch-offered opportunity to learn about Grendel military capabilities.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun defended Clisearn alongside the Highborn, and the orc garrison of Rucraic's Redoubt took losses supporting the southern armies. Imperial Orcs with resources in Mareave could gain a stubbornness-enhancing boon from the servants of Cathan Canae.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: warband captains came from every Imperial nation except Navarr.
n.The Brass Coast: The Fire of the South left its garrison in Madruga, marched along the Bay of Catazar and threw itself straight into the fighting in southern Mareave, where Freeborn lives were at hazard.
n.The League: The Wolves of War remained in Mareave and led the offensive against the dug-in Grendel, bearing much of the perilous fighting.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar's general recalled liberating the Mournwold alongside the Seventh Wave.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky's orders recall Zenith, and the Icarion tunnels are thought to be remnants of an old Urizeni port near a former Urizen lighthouse.

t.Ayereed: Mentioned in passing: Grendel navies shipped in supplies to avoid the desiccating trek through Ayereed's Petrified Forest.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: only through the name of the Bastion of Rucraic's Redoubt, a fortification in Mareave, not this territory.
t.Bay of Catazar: Grendel ships worked its waters below Icarion, dumping rubble to build temporary quays that the Bay's tides would wear away within a year. The Fire of the South also marched along its northern coast.
t.Madruga: The Fire of the South, previously garrisoned in Madruga to defend the Brass Coast homeland, left to join the assault in Mareave.
t.Mareave: No land changed hands: the Empire kept its quarter of Clisearn, the Grendel held the rest, and Beoraidh stayed neutral, while a Grendel plan threatened to make Icarion coastal for a year and cut the Apulian Way.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: recalled in the Granite Pillar's speech as land liberated with the Seventh Wave.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: only through the name of Rucraic's Redoubt, a bastion in Mareave, not this territory.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar's general honoured the Imperial Orcs who bled to reclaim Reikos.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Icarion tunnels may once have let vessels from Spiral dock beneath the cliffs.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky's general recalled shining the way through Zenith.

r.Ayereed/Petrified Forest: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel avoided the desiccating overland trek through the Petrified Forest by bringing supplies by sea.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: The city-state stayed neutral, its Palace of Chains aiding neither side, though Seventh Wave scouts extended some attention there. Its stubborn neutrality remains a barrier to Grendel naval support.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: The main battleground: Imperial armies, backed by a Summer citadel on the border, probed Grendel lines without gaining ground, and the Grendel made no attacks into the Imperial quarter.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: Most of the Grendel host camped here to reinforce its front-line armies, and the cliffs along its coast had earlier been collapsed by the Hawser of the Drowned.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Grendel fleets were found building quays beneath the cliffs at the Syagrian Haven to reach inland tunnels. Unless the four active tunnels are collapsed, the Grendel could treat Icarion as coastal for a year and threaten the Apulian Way.
r.Mareave/Nadir: A Summer citadel loomed over Nadir, and warriors of the Queen of Ice and Darkness marched from it to join the Empire's armies and guard the orcs who live there.

Shadowed boughs of twilight.d: Everyone in Ossium dreamed of fantastical forests. Some woke injured, and around two dozen magicians vanished. Off-road travellers got lost and many never returned. Sung's heralds sang a threnody at the Field of Glory and posed questions on grief and forgetting to the Varushkan and Navarr assemblies. A boggart-like infestation drained the Towers of Zulgan Tash garrison to zero, which cannot recover until the curse is lifted. Azoth offered to take the Palace of Orieb for a year. Dubik attacks will cut forest output. Wisdom dreamers learned that the Dubik and the Stranger walk Ossium, and the Thule protested the enchantment's effect on their forests.

n.Dawn: Dawnish military units joining the Protect the Vales of Varushka venture after the Autumn Equinox will receive extra consumable rewards from the frightened vales, alongside their usual production.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is recalled as once held in the Druj's iron fist, the Palace of Orieb's shrines were built for Druj ghulai, and Kaela's Gift lets Imperial captives escape Druj defilement.
n.Navarr: The Navarr of Awstin's Rest and Navarr-held forests in Ossium share the dreams, the dangers and the dubik losses. The Navarr National Assembly is invited to answer Sung's questions on grief and being forgotten in return for possible boons.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: some dreamers in Ossium saw waterlogged willows and mangroves reminiscent of the Siroc Bayou.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Rat King of Temeschwar is listed among the known sovereigns of Varushka.
n.Thule: The Thule-held Bonewood and Webwood were shrouded by the enchantment. Through their ambassador Runa they expressed significant dissatisfaction and expect the Empire to deal with those responsible, while the Stranger reportedly seeks to poison relations between Thule and Varushkans.
n.Varushka: Varushka's people in Ossium faced dreams, disappearances, lost travellers, dubik raids and a forgotten garrison at the Towers of Zulgan Tash. Its assembly was offered Sung's questions and a chapel boon at the Field of Glory, and its Wise learned that the Dubik and the Stranger are loose in Ossium.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, allowing Imperial citizens to choose painless dissolution, is noted as extending into Brocéliande.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: an out-of-character note allows that something awful might yet lurk in the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Karsk: A conjunction revealed a band of Mirk Lizards from the Mallum attempting to camp on an island in the Semmerlak, with the Watcher of the Semmerlak, Romand Reinetova Remislav, tasked with killing them.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: dream forests in Ossium sometimes resembled the willows and mangroves of the Siroc Bayou.
t.Ossium: The whole territory was enchanted with Night magic, causing vivid dreams, dangerous woodlands and dubik attacks on forests. It also left a curse on the Towers of Zulgan Tash, an offer from Azoth for the Palace of Orieb, and both the Dubik and the Stranger at large.
t.Otkodov: The orcs of Otkodov, already negotiating with the Ambassador to Otkodov, are considering whether to invoke the treaty to resolve the enchantment's effects on their Ossium forests through diplomatic channels.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the Rat King of Temeschwar is named among Varushka's documented sovereigns.
t.The Semmerlak: The enchantment touched the domain of Dho'uala, whose servants were repelled by the Watcher and the Journeymage Towers, earning the Watcher two wains of mithril. A Mirk Lizard band is also trying to establish a camp on an island in the lake.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift is noted as extending into Therunin.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: some dreamers described the stalking beast as a brindled lion larger than any in the wild forests of Weirwater.

r.Karsk/Moresvah: A servant of Undertow emerged from the Semmerlak on a wet night to warn a cabalist in Moresvah of the approaching Mirk Lizards.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: Mentioned in passing: dreamers in Ossium saw waterlogged willows and mangroves reminiscent of the Siroc Bayou.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Bittershore's open lands were spared the woodland disorientation. Bandits who robbed a trader bound for Kostjyas Respite are to be brought to justice by the Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore, Kostjya, with a twelve-crown pledge offered, and Agramant's messenger shouted his approval at Kostjyas Respite's walls.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: This Thule-held forest was shrouded by the enchantment, and dubik are rumoured to be gathering there. The Academy's cadets are tasked with aiding an injured patrol in Bonewood that nobody remembers setting out.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: The Towers of Zulgan Tash here lost their entire garrison to a memory-eating curse that needs Piercing Light of Revelation at magnitude 60 to lift, and Azoth offered to take the Palace of Orieb for a year. Dho'uala's servants and dubik also troubled the forest, and grateful boyars gave mithril to the Watcher.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Echofell's great woodlands became hard to navigate, with travellers easily lost, and multiple dubik encounters were reported there.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: Thirteen heralds of Sung sang a day-long threnody at the Field of Glory. Sung offered seasonal feather tokens to the Grieftender if a chapel is built there by Autumn 389YE, while the open fields escaped the woodland dangers.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: Sung's heralds visited the Navarr at Awstin's Rest, and travellers in Nearweald reported multiple encounters with the vampiric dubik.
r.Ossium/Webwood: This Thule-held forest was shrouded by the enchantment, to the Thule's displeasure, and unsubstantiated reports suggest dubik may be gathering there.

Skull beneath the skin.d: The collapse of the Hidden Snake and Poison Crane loosed Winter spirits that now animate husks, among them fallen Imperial champions, while souls broken by Het Trakaa roam the Turan Flats. Trakaa and Sul Maggotgnaw still lead guerrillas. Given leave by the Ambassador to Axos, the Shield of Ipotavo, estimating some two thousand spirits, protected the Flats' spires and slave villages and delayed the spread into Kroll by about six weeks, but took significant casualties. Refugees, especially in Whisperwood, face mass starvation, and disguised Druj hide among them. Two conjunctions were offered: destroying a husk-drawing column at Tercia's Bluff, and unmasking a Druj Tepel among captured refugees bound for the Nesustak Forest.

n.Druj: Their armies in the Sarangrave are broken, but Trakaa and Sul Maggotgnaw still raise banners and gather guerrillas, Tower survivors hide in the territory's corners and among the refugees, and some have even settled within the vallorn of Béantal Dol.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Druj in Bendol are said to use lessons learned in Therunin and Brocéliande, and Kaela's Gift extends into those lands.
n.Urizen: Their newly claimed territory is beset by husks, tormented souls, Druj insurgents and a looming refugee catastrophe; the few spires depend on Axou protection, and Senator Bartimaeus is charged with destroying the husk-drawing column at Tercia's Bluff.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Druj in Bendol apply lessons learned in Brocéliande, and Kaela's Gift extends there.
t.Sarangrave: Though the Druj stranglehold is broken, the territory is plagued by Winter husks, tormented spirits, Druj guerrillas and starving freed slaves, with Thornfen under Axou control, the Nesustak Forest held by rebels and Bendol a vallornheart.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Druj in Bendol apply lessons learned in Therunin, and Kaela's Gift extends there.

r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Some Druj have taken up residence within the vallorn of Béantal Dol, building a kind of steading of their own, a move even other Druj consider mad.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Freed folk here are in a parlous position, working farms haphazardly after the Druj destroyed what supplies they could not carry.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: The Shield of Ipotavo delayed the spread of Winter spirits into Kroll by around six weeks, but they will keep rampaging while the region remains tormented, and its lakeland folk also face hardship.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The rebel septs still permit Imperial passage for now, and a conjunction tasked the Imperial Spymaster with unmasking a Druj Tepel hidden among captured refugees trying to reach the septs here.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Axou garrison of the Tower of the Skink, estimated at around 500, stayed behind its walls and offered sanctuary to Urizen settlers, while orcs exiled from the region swelled the refugee crisis elsewhere.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: Some two thousand Winter husks and Het Trakaa's tormented souls prey on the Flats; the Shield of Ipotavo prevented significant damage, but if the column at Tercia's Bluff is not destroyed husks will ravage the spires and leave the region underpopulated.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: Whisperwood holds the worst of the refugee crisis, with exiles from Thornfen and former Thornwasp thralls in Uklead facing hunger and the winter rains, with hundreds or even thousands of deaths feared.

So little I wanted, so little I got.d: From the Autumn Equinox the observers' cost of about 50 thrones a season falls on the treasury, unless the Senate removes them. The Purple Sails offered to fund the embassies if the Court were recognised and allowed to appoint ambassadors. The civil service will give private briefings to ambassadors with embassy staff and publish them after each summit. The Beoraidh and Grendel ambassadors have no staff unless the Senate pays five thrones a season each. War with Asavea continues, and the Loyalty assembly arranged a meeting with Ibarian rebels. The Sumaah answered Imperial tariffs with their own. A mandate was proposed to protect the theist Marracossan exiles. Morajasse asked for materials to expand Mora's Rock.

n.Grendel: The Grendel remain at war with the Empire, backed by Asavean warships and mercenaries. Their envoys sent missives after the Summer Solstice, believed to concern future embassies and ending hostilities, but Ambassador Starlight Starchaser now lacks embassy staff for briefings.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Michael of Crown's Quay, one of the Purple Sails' three spokespeople, reluctantly dropped his objection to withdrawing the fleet funding. Accalon of Highguard remains Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the observers are credited with stopping traitorous merchants from enriching the Jotun and the Grendel through illegal trade.
n.The Brass Coast: Olivero i Farad i Riqueza helped decide the Purple Sails' withdrawal. The Freeborn faced a proposed mandate to protect the theist Marracossan exiles in Madruga, and the Freeborn of Feroz have begun trading with Morajasse. The Brass Coast also continues to smuggle missionaries and resources westward against Asavea.
n.The League: Therese di Sarvos led the Purple Sails' decision and plans how to spend the money saved. League merchants' old contacts helped reach the Ibarian rebels, and the League assembly was suggested as one route to help the Marracossan exiles.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Marches are not named on the page. Its nearest reference is the rumoured Asavean backing of the Cult of the Falconer's attempted magical disaster in the northern Empire.
n.Urizen: Two Urizen hold key ambassadorships: Herminius of the House of the Wanderer, newly appointed to Asavea, has reopened correspondence with Lady Madrianna, while Starlight Starchaser handles the Grendel without embassy staff.

t.Bay of Catazar: Intelligence suggests four Asavean warships remain in the Bay supporting the Grendel navies. Grendel missives arrived from across the Bay for the first time in a long while.
t.Feroz: The Protectorate of Morajasse continues to flourish here and Ferozi merchants have begun trading with it. Wind Lord Saoirse warned that any curse on Feroz other than Rivers of Life would prompt the Protectorate to seek its source and recompense.
t.Madruga: The theist Marracossan exiles of Trajadoz face trouble under the new proscription. A proposed mandate would make Madruga resist any move against them for ten years. Madruga's quays also grumbled at tariffs on Sumaah merchants.
t.Mareave: The fighting with the Grendel is concentrated in southern Mareave, where Asavean mercenaries fight alongside the orcs. The Senator for Mareave is invited to meet a Brine Turtles delegation.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is not named on the page and nothing described takes place there.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the quays of Necropolis voiced some dissatisfaction at tariffs being imposed on Sumaah merchants without warning.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: eyewitnesses in Redoubt reported Asavean warships, and the former Grendel embassy in Cargo was shut down at the end of 387YE.
t.Sarvos: The Asavean Embassy in Sarvos received new missives from Lady Madrianna. Sarvos's quays grumbled at the abrupt tariffs on Sumaah merchants, and Therese di Sarvos of the Purple Sails plans her next moves there.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Mentioned in passing: Commander Gallum noted that an expanded Mora's Rock would only hinder invaders if Afarjasse had already fallen.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The Protectorate asked for thirty wains each of mithril and white granite to raise Mora's Rock higher. Construction could be sped up if the Conclave provides 60 or 120 mana crystals. Its garrison will keep defending Feroz if attacked.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: The Ambassador to Beoraidh has no embassy staff and will lose civil service briefings unless the Senate pays five thrones a season, or abrogates the title so the Imperial Consul handles relations.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: The Brine Turtles sept, at home in Fleisardh and at the forefront of reclaiming it from the Unshackled, are sending a representative to Anvil to discuss the future of Fioroult.

Spreading the Way.d: Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa, sought the appraisal at the Summer Solstice. Lisane de Terresford was engaged in Sumaah, so Gerard la Salle assigned Naomi. She gave three caveats: faith is hard to prognosticate, no one-size-fits-all solution exists, and conversion does not guarantee good relations, as the Lasambrians showed when they joined the Jotun. She outlined aura-led, doctrine-led and culture-led approaches, drawing on the Sand Fishers, Barrens septs, Apulian Orcs, Suranni and Asavea. She urged the Synod, Senate and other bodies to take small, careful steps, and to commission future appraisals on specific groups and simple goals.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: their miasma pillars, which the Sand Fishers lived under, and the rebellion of three Druj armies in the Barrens are cited as examples, as is the risk of Imperial Lore falling into Druj hands.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: former Grendel who joined the Empire are said to wear their new religious beliefs like a loose cloak, but still to hold them.
n.Jotun: Naomi judged that converting the Jotun would be incredibly difficult and dangerous, but that a doctrine-led approach would suit them best, given their established ancestor worship and respected ghodi. The Lasambrians, who were converted to the Way and then joined the Jotun, were cited as a warning.
n.The League: The League's willingness to give up land to the Sand Fishers was called pivotal in drawing that sept towards the Empire and the Way. Naomi also saw no reason why future League Orcs should not become bishops.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Highborn missionaries' debates in Urizen centuries ago are cited as an example of a doctrine-led approach, and Urizen also serves as an example of a fortification that can be divined precisely.
n.Wintermark: The appraisal was commissioned by Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa. A monument to a fallen Wintermark hero is used to illustrate what Night rituals can divine.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: a fortification built in Hahnmark is given as an example of a solution that works the same anywhere, unlike efforts to spread faith.
t.Holberg: The Sand Fishers' settlement in Holberg, on land given up by the League, is presented as the key example of conversion succeeding through auras combined with a secure homeland.
t.Kallavesa: The motion behind the appraisal came from Kallavesa's senator, and the consecration of Kallavesa's marshes is cited as a true aura that moves Imperial citizens.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: a fortification in Redoubt is used as an example of a solution that works the same anywhere.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Naomi credits the gift of Misericorde to the Sand Fishers, offered alongside the auras and the Virtues, with making them enormously well inclined towards the Empire and open to the Way.

Stand proud, you're strong.d: The Assembly's statement, upheld with a greater majority of 216-0 in Summer 388YE, gave it a year to direct Freeborn efforts. Each season it may choose one option by statement of principle. The options cover four areas: fortifying Kahraman, Feroz, Segura or Madruga; approaching eternals such as Adamant, Cathan Canae, Janon (who is under enmity), Sorin or Ephisis; seeking closer ties with the Suranni, Faraden, Morajasse or Marracossans; or building spy networks against the Lasambrians, Jotun or Suranni. For a year, Freeborn armies may also Burn Brightly when defending Freeborn territory. This greatly boosts their defence and the casualties they inflict, but doubles their own losses.

n.Grendel: The Grendel are named as the threat the Coast must fortify Feroz and Madruga against, while the Grendel Protectorate of Morajasse is offered as a possible mortal ally for further mutual military deals.
n.Imperial Orcs: The proposed Suranni espionage option depends on Imperial Orc military units operating the new Arbonne spy network, using the cover of guarding Freeborn merchants.
n.Jotun: The Jotun are treated as a likely source of attack through Liathaven, and spying on them there is one of the options open to the Assembly. The page also notes the Faraden recently re-signed their peace treaty with them.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Assembly can direct its people towards up to four defensive projects over the year. Meanwhile, Freeborn armies gain the Burn Brightly order to defend their homelands at great cost to themselves.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named directly, and the opening fiction only notes that the Suranni now hold the islands along the Coast.
t.Feroz: Fortifying Feroz is one option, to guard against an eventual Grendel return and possibly the southern border, alongside existing efforts to restore its people's livelihoods. Freeborn armies there may Burn Brightly in its defence.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman has been largely undefended since the fall of Fort Braydon despite holding three bourse seats. Fortifying it against renewed Lasambrian raids is one of the options offered.
t.Liathaven: A new spy network in Jotun-held Liathaven is proposed, since its earlier network was destroyed, Imperial maps are increasingly outdated and any Jotun attack on the Coast would likely come from there.
t.Madruga: The completed Well of Life in Madruga reduces Imperial casualties across the Coast. Further fortification is proposed against the Grendel armada and possible threats from Crucible, and the Marracossans are named as a potential ally with an interest in its safety.
t.Reinos: With the Imperial spy network in Reinos decommissioned almost two years ago, a new one is proposed to watch the Suranni campaign against the Lasambrian homeland.
t.Segura: Segura has only recently found quiet after nearly two decades of war, and Adamant has already offered protection now that the City of Wonders is complete. Further fortification of this remote territory is one of the options.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Mentioned in passing: in the opening fiction, the commander at Mora's Rock dreads the prospect of the Suranni taking Afarjasse.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: the Mora's Rock commander doubts the Suranni will stop at the Cazar Straits.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The fiction shows the Mora's Rock garrison under orders to hold the fortification, fearing both Imperial and Suranni attack. The Protectorate that controls it is offered as a possible partner for mutual military deals.
r.Madruga/Crucible: Mentioned in passing: several hakima have raised concerns about threats that might emerge from Crucible as a reason to fortify Madruga further.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction notes that news of the conquest of Free Landing has reached Mora's Rock.

The dose makes the poison.d: Guided by the Last Battle steading, nearly seven thousand Varushkans fought fragmented Druj rallied by Egrech, a self-styled het, at Razorhill, the ruined Holt of the Oak. Warriors of Dochas Weeping Glade, who bear Agramant's gifts, broke a Druj ambush. Egrech fired the camp, sacrificed his followers and fled west to the Upper Tarn Valley with his herbalists. The Golden Axe took five wains of Thimble weirwood. The Lower Tarn remains poisoned. The Apothecaries' Guild may cleanse it over two seasons at a cost of 30 thrones a season and heavy personal sacrifice. Highguard's herbs or healing armies could ease the cost or speed the work.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish knights are recalled as having helped save Peakedge Stead earlier in the war.
n.Druj: The Druj lost the Lower Tarn Valley and Egrech's Blackrazor rabble was burned or scattered at Razorhill. They still hold Peakedge Song, the Upper Tarn Valley and East Ashes.
n.Highguard: Highguard could supply herbs from High Chalcis to remove the treasury's cost of cleansing the poison, at the expense of Reikos's bounty and the High Herbalist of Sybella. The Valiant Pegasus could speed the cleansing.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Druj frenzy drug Warspice is noted as the preparation Imperial Orcs call Warming Armour.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held Liathaven is cited as a territory once troubled by a vallorn dividing it, as Therunin now is.
n.Navarr: Holdout Navarr steadings welcomed the Golden Axe as cousins and as proof they had not been forgotten. Dochas Weeping Glade's Agramant-tainted warriors turned the battle at Razorhill, and the Willowjoy thorns were cut down for consorting with Wasteland beasts.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe began its march from the Turan Flats of Sarangrave, where the route east is sealed against the Druj.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe under Vojsuli Cherenkov won the Lower Tarn Valley and deepened bonds with the Navarr. It lost up to three hundred soldiers, mostly to poison, and its general received five wains of weirwood.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks of Wintermark are named as one army that could use its physicks to halve the time needed to cleanse the poison, protected by the Winter ritual Why Sulemaine Walked Away From The Baker.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn is cited as creating a strategic challenge similar to the vallorn band now splitting Therunin.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: it is noted as a territory where a dividing vallorn once caused similar strategic problems.
t.Reikos: The bounty of Reikos can no longer simply be redirected to cure the poison. If the Benefactor of High Chalcis commits Highguard's herbs instead, the Gardens of High Chalcis would yield nothing until the cleansing ends.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe set out from the Turan Flats, and the Druj route east into Sarangrave is noted as sealed by the vallorn and the Empire.
t.The Barrens: The Last Battle Wayhouse in the Barrens provided the scouts and intelligence key to the victory. Hope's Rest offers an alternative, poison-free route to attack the Upper Tarn Valley.
t.Therunin: The Empire now holds the Lower Tarn Valley, the Druj hold three regions and the vallorn three, so no single force controls the territory. Agramant's influence lingers among the remaining Navarr but has not worsened this season.

r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe marched up out of the Turan Flats, fording the Unnamed River at Turan on their way north.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Imperial forces could pull back to Hope's Rest and attack the Upper Tarn Valley from there, avoiding the poison but needing a new beachhead.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Golden Axe stopped at the Last Battle Wayhouse, whose steading guided them south, and cut tree trunks on the edge of the Bleaks to bridge Razorhill's poisoned moat. Resentful Karass orcs watched but neither helped nor hindered.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: The Druj still hold East Ashes around the Feverwater Docks, cut off from the north by the vallorn, so any fight there is a separate engagement.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Eastring remains wholly dominated by the vallorn. A Druj shipment of five wains of Thimble weirwood was seized on the raised road that once led there.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Greenheart is completely dominated by the vallorn. Some Navarr steadings that withdrew into its depths survived and still strike at the Druj to the north.
