r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Golden Axe claimed the region after destroying Razorhill, but it remains poisoned and will inflict 250 casualties on any Imperial army passing through or fighting there. The Apothecaries' Guild may choose to cleanse it.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: The Druj still control Peakedge Song, whose warlords traded herbs for Egrech's hoarded weirwood and heard the drums warning of the Empire's approach.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Mentioned in passing: Sweetglades is listed among the regions completely dominated by the vallorn.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: Egrech fled here with his herbalists and core supporters, and the Druj still hold the region. Any Imperial attack from the Lower Tarn beachhead would suffer the poison's effects.

The little things.d: Thule scribes proposed that the civil service consult foreign landholders before territory-wide magic. A Senate administrative motion would put this forward, applying to the Thule alone, to all foreigners, or to none. As an example, Tathenon the Gyre announced that *Three Blasts Upon the Horn of Victory* would be cast on Ossium unless the Ambassador, the Throne or Ossium's senator objected before 6pm Saturday. The Dragons welcomed Regrow the Land's Heart on Sermersuaq. They disowned the Night darkness over Ossium. Runa supplied a primer on oath-based Thule law. Stürmherra of the White Mountain Fire took Bonewall and the Great Pit, then declined further Imperial support. Two Thule warlocks sought Imperial heroes against the Mirk Lizards.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is named as one of the nations shipping food north to feed Otkodov under the peace terms.
n.Druj: The Druj lost Bonewall and the Great Pit to the Thule, and their routed armies were left seriously damaged by a Spring curse. They also sent their Mirk Lizards to take vengeance on a Grimfen Mire clan allied with the Thule.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Regrow the Land's Heart is said to be washing away the scars left in Sermersuaq by the coalition against the Jotun.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr sends food to Otkodov, and the surge of Navarri into Ulnak is said to have flushed out the Mirk Lizards.
n.Thule: The Thule sought closer magical coordination with the Empire and planned a Summer enchantment on Ossium to improve the Jaws of Winter Lightning. They also won Bonewall from the Druj, after which Stürmherra ended military cooperation with the Empire in Ulnak.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is noted as sharing a long mountainous border with Otkodov.
n.Wintermark: Kindra Surefoot of Wintermark serves as Ambassador to Otkodov and can halt the Thule enchantment on Ossium. The Dragons also expressed contentment with the Regrow the Land's Heart enchantment on Sermersuaq.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which lets captured or dying Imperial citizens choose a painless death, is said to extend into Brocéliande.
t.Forest of Ulnak: The Thule took Bonewall and the Great Pit from the Druj in Ulnak, and the White Mountain Fire under Stürmherra replaced the Earthquake Drummers there. Stürmherra then declared Imperial military support would no longer be needed after the Autumn Equinox.
t.Ossium: Tathenon the Gyre intended to enchant Ossium with Summer magic unless the Empire objected in time. Separately, an unknown Night enchantment had wrapped the territory in darkness and caused travellers to become lost, which the Thule denied causing and called ill-advised.
t.Otkodov: Runa explained that Otkodov has no single legal code; its society is ordered by solemn oaths. Visitors must obey any warlock's instruction unless it is overridden by someone of higher status.
t.Sermersuaq: The Dragons were grateful for warning of Regrow the Land's Heart on Sermersuaq and comfortable with its effect. It is gently healing the remaining scars of war.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Mirk Lizards were first encountered during the invasion of Therunin, and Kaela's Gift extends there.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: Verthandi appears only in the further reading list as a territory in Otkodov.

r.Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest: Mirk Lizards, practitioners of the rite of excommunication, were trying to go to ground in Ghul'thak Forest. Warlock Krafvötn offered mana crystals to the Master of the School of Exorcism to root them out.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire: A band of Mirk Lizards was travelling to butcher a Grimfen Mire clan that had allied with the Thule. Warlock Tungjökull asked Rhydian de Rondell to slay them in return for mana crystals.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The Unbounded Tower of Feresh coven planned to cast the Thule Summer enchantment at 7pm on Saturday, at a regio near the Silent Pines in Bonewood, unless the Empire declined in time.

The wolves tempt you.d: Using the Throne's power to address the Empire, Emperor Vesna mourned Alderei the Fair, slain fighting in the Sarangrave, as the last pillar of the Iron Helms' memory, whose schlacta fell fighting for a nation not their own. The Emperor described the Empire as a promise of unbreakable loyalty and called on citizens tempted by the Wolves to remember who had stood with them. Commendations went to the Imperial Auxiliaries, Edward of Gwent, the Vallornguard, the Marches and Vesna's betrothed Sally B Baker. The address avoided naming any group, but seemed aimed at the Navarr struggling in Therunin while sidestepping a trap set by Agramant, whose response remained to be seen.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Vesna signs the address as Warden Queen of Dawn among the Emperor's titles.
n.Druj: The address recalls Druj cruelty, which held no terror over the Iron Helms, and appears crafted to blunt the temptation offered by Agramant, the Druj warlord, whose response is awaited.
n.Navarr: The address appears designed to reach the Navarr fighting desperately for survival in Therunin, urging them not to be lured from the path by the Wolves and to remember who has fought for them.
n.The Marches: The Emperor commended the Marches for self-funding their fifth army in a single season, and praised Edward of Gwent for his years of service to Mitwold.
n.Varushka: Vesna honoured Alderei the Fair and the Iron Helms, whose schlacta died fighting for another nation and whose legacy to Varushka and the Military Council endures; the Wolves imagery also echoes Varushkan tradition.

t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Edward of Gwent is commended for his years of service to the people of Mitwold.
t.Sarangrave: The Sarangrave is where Alderei the Fair was slain the previous season, and where the Vallornguard arranged military units to fight the Vallorn in Spring, for which they were commended.
t.Therunin: The address appears aimed at the Navarr fighting desperately for their survival in Therunin, encouraging them to resist the temptation set before them by Agramant.

There is hope.d: After Imperial magicians chose to forge ahead through the chaos, the constellations returned to normal, and an awareness rippled out from the Imperial regio that an unassuming star had become the Beacon. Its law, 'there is hope', caused consternation given hope's malign reputation, and like the Wanderer it moves unpredictably. Foreign magicians soon learned of it. Embodied tulpas vanished and can no longer be created, and stars cannot be deliberately bound to mortals, though constellations can still shape enchantments. The regio still did not enhance realm lore, but same-nation covens could cooperate and ritualists gained a sense of spiritual strength. Territory-scale magic remained unpredictable for one last season, with things expected to settle by Winter.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named, but the revelation of the Beacon rippled out from the Imperial regio at Anvil in Casinea, a territory Highguard held at the time.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial regio can still be used alongside the Citadel Guard to focus magic and channel rituals through the Urizen army.

t.Casinea: The awareness of the new Beacon constellation spread outward from the Imperial regio at Anvil in Casinea, where the regio still could not enhance realm lore but let same-nation covens work together and gave ritualists a peculiar source of spiritual strength during the Autumn Equinox.

This old house.d: Feroz was left financially ruined by Governor Rahab, and recovery had already begun, aided by an appraisal proposed by Lizzie Stamp of Bildewold. Last season the Prosperity Assembly sent Katya Vasillova Reznikov to aid the territory. Ivan Veralova Esskvich proposed a Prosperity Assembly mandate that would remove the abandoned quality from Oranseri and Afarjasse. It would also raise labour costs in Feroz to four crowns a wain until no region there is impoverished. Inspired by Mabel's statement, Marcelo i Porfirio i Guerra proposed a General Assembly mandate that would permanently raise labour costs for all commissions to four crowns a wain and lift the Senate's available commissions to fourteen. That mandate would not apply in Feroz. If both were enacted, the Feroz increase would also become permanent.

n.Grendel: Grendel held part of Feroz that season, so any increase in labour costs for commissions in the territory under the Prosperity Assembly mandate would bear on works there.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Mabel's statement of principle cites Casinea, a Highborn-held territory, as a place where the same work should earn the same pay as in Feroz.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Lizzie Stamp of Bildewold's appraisal of Feroz is credited from her time as Senator for Bregasland, a territory then held by the Jotun.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn are central to the story: their territory of Feroz is being rebuilt, and it is a Freeborn architect, Marcelo i Porfirio i Guerra, who urged higher wages across the Empire.
n.Urizen: If the General Assembly mandate passed without a greater majority, it would not affect commissions wholly in Urizen. The Urizen national assembly would then likely have the chance to enact a similar mandate.
n.Varushka: If the General Assembly mandate passed without a greater majority, it would not affect commissions wholly in Varushka. The Varushkan national assembly would then likely have the chance to enact a similar mandate.
n.Wintermark: If the General Assembly mandate passed without a greater majority, it would not affect commissions wholly in Wintermark. The Wintermark national assembly would then likely have the chance to enact a similar mandate.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Lizzie Stamp of Bildewold proposed her appraisal of Feroz while serving as Senator for Bregasland.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Mabel's statement holds that the people of Feroz should not accept less pay than for the same work in Casinea.
t.Feroz: Still recovering from Rahab's ruinous rule, Feroz could see its abandoned regions restored under the Prosperity Assembly mandate, with labour costs for new commissions there raised to four crowns a wain. Only that mandate can change things in Feroz, and the General Assembly proposal would not apply there.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: The proposed Prosperity Assembly mandate would immediately remove Afarjasse's abandoned quality.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Cazar Straits would remain impoverished even if the Prosperity Assembly mandate were enacted, so the higher Feroz labour costs would continue while it stays so.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The proposed mandate would immediately lift Oranseri's abandoned quality, though the region would remain impoverished, keeping the higher Feroz labour costs in place.

Those memories of you.d: The Sarcophan Delves stayed friendly but resented the Senate's new tariffs, which may complicate customs at the Alivetti estates in Sarvos. Hahnmark had ended its viezesmaak arrangement with the Kraft brothers, and Brenna's Gift reverted to 36 rings per farm. The Zuredruiven vintners offered draaikolkbloem cultivation and new Wintermark potion recipes, and invited an Apothecaries Guild assessment. The House of the Jackal sought 70 thrones to keep Jakhalsmarkt open, and a Sarcophan scholar offered to buy vallorn goods. Axos held Thornfen, removed its Druj inhabitants and was rebuilding the Tower of the Skink. It resented being left to defend Sarangrave, and Navarr captains still faced suspicion in Axou ports.

n.Druj: The Axou removed the former Druj subjects living in Thornfen, and still fight the Winter spirits the Druj drew into Sarangrave.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but the Sarcophan Delves extended their protection to the independent city-state of Beoraidh in Mareave.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn stevedores appear in the opening fiction at Crown's Quay, where a Sarcophan captain refuses to pay the new duty.
n.Navarr: Navarr ship captains visiting Axou ports still face suspicion and a trade penalty after the Autumn Equinox. This is expected to ease by the Winter Solstice unless something goes wrong.
n.The League: The tariffs that angered Sarcophan merchants were proposed by Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar, Senator for Temeschwar. The Sarcophan enclave at the Alivetti estates in Sarvos may now become a route for goods to slip past customs.
n.Urizen: Most Urizen still shun settling Sarangrave, while Axou settlers flow in and may eventually outnumber them there. The deBruin family also supplies weirwood to Urizen.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan have made inroads into Varushka, and the Varushkan example of the Apothecaries Guild assessing Elder's Gift inspired calls to examine draaikolkbloem.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk ended the Kraft brothers' viezesmaak trade, and Wintermark apothecaries gained two new draaikolkbloem potion recipes, subject to continued good relations with the Zuredruiven vintners. Wintermark's Thanmir Hrafnar serves as ambassador to Axos.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction takes place at Crown's Quay, where Sarcophan ships are turned away over the newly imposed duties.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: an earlier Wind of Fortune on growing Sarcophan influence in the Bay of Catazar is listed in further reading.
t.Hahnmark: Brenna's Gift returned to providing 36 rings per farm once the Kraft brothers left. Herb garden owners received a gift of draaikolkbloem and may now choose to cultivate it, at the cost of some other herbs.
t.Mareave: The Sarcophan Delves extended their protection to the city-state of Beoraidh, ostensibly to guarantee its neutrality.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Axou showed no interest in supporting the Imperial venture into the Salt Flats, at least not with their armies.
t.Sarangrave: Axou forces defended northern Sarangrave against Winter spirits, but the Grand Council resents the Empire leaving the defence to them. Axou settlers steadily arrived in the territory.
t.Sarvos: The Alivetti estates remain the centre of Sarcophan influence. The new tariffs mean goods are only inspected at the land border into Sarvos proper, making smuggling easier.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: The independent city-state of Beoraidh came under Sarcophan protection, ostensibly to help guarantee its neutrality.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Axou cleared Thornfen of its former Druj subjects and are rebuilding the Tower of the Skink with white granite and salvage from Sephals. Its garrison still struggles to grow while Axou settlers move in.

Towers of the moon.d: Sadogua offered a commission for the Toadstool Palace around the Toadstone in West Marsh. If built and ceded to him, it would create the chosen title Toadstool Wizard, grant the Froghaven quality and strengthen Dripping Echoes of the Fen in Kallavesa, though it would give him lasting magical leverage there. He also offered the Well of Shadows to Archmage of Night Brat Umbral Path, with future access as a prize for the largest Tithe of Bats. He proposed a Twilight Pier on the Lyceum isle for the Arcane Architect, a pre-wassail mushroom boon for Marcher farms and a Senate appraisal for arcane great works. He thanked the Conclave for its enmity against Apeiron, kept feuding with the Circle of Zulgan Tash and made peace with other Varushkans.

n.The Brass Coast: Sadogua's heralds visited Madruga, and he offered the Arcane Architect the chance to build a Twilight Pier on the Isle of the Lyceum. This would bring a Night-realm trading vessel offering Night foci, robes and crystal fire.
n.The Marches: Sadogua offered access to his Well of Shadows in Upwold and promised heralds for the Anvil wassail. Marcher farms enchanted with Fallow Fields and Dried Meat plus crystal fire could grow black mushrooms that yield Shinemoon elixirs.
n.Varushka: Sadogua continued his feud with the Circle of Zulgan Tash, accusing them of stealing a fortress protecting his western woods. He promised other Varushkan wizards a return to his usual friendly advice through missives, but refused to send heralds to Miekarova or Ossium for now.
n.Wintermark: Sadogua promised arcane projections to Tarqeq Icetongue and Sigebryht and offered the Toadstool Palace commission in Kallavesa. If built and ceded to him, it would create a Toadstool Wizard title, always held by a Wintermark magician without an Imperial title, who would use Night magic to protect the nation and harvest Shinemoon.

t.Kallavesa: If the Toadstool Palace is built and ceded, Sadogua will back every casting of Dripping Echoes of the Fen in Kallavesa, raising the victory points needed to take a region and inflicting casualties on invaders. However, he would also gain the power to shape Night enchantments and curses on the territory.
t.Madruga: Sadogua claimed dominion over the Isle of the Lyceum off Madruga and offered a Twilight Pier there, available only to the Arcane Architect until the end of Summer 389YE. Once built, it would host regular visits from the Twilight Barque.
t.Miekarova: Sadogua refused to send heralds to Miekarova, and he would be angered if the Senate named it in the appraisal for arcane great works.
t.Ossium: Sadogua's heralds have reportedly been fighting spider monsters in Ossium. He nonetheless excluded the territory from his proposed arcane great works appraisal and would be angered if it were chosen.
t.Upwold: The Well of Shadows, Sadogua's college of magic inside an oak tree near King's Stoke, was offered to Brat Umbral Path. The Vigilance assembly could post a priest with liao to watch who uses it, at the risk of irritating Sadogua and the Marcher assembly.

r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: The onyx Toadstone near Westerhal could become the Toadstool Palace, a garden ceded to Sadogua. This would grant West Marsh the Froghaven quality, making its frogs prosper and grow big and wise.
r.Upwold/Tower March: The Well of Shadows near King's Stoke would open to Brat Umbral Path after the Autumn Equinox. Its door could be placed under watch by a Vigilance mandate.

Towers of the sun.d: Meraud offered plans for wizard towers, available until the end of the Summer Solstice 389YE, each harnessing a Summer regio and granting a title four golden apples a season. The civil service judged them to be fanes that only work if the Senate concedes them to the eternal. Meraud proposed judging the most impressive tower before the Winter Solstice 389YE and rewarding it with a boon. He asked the Senate to let him choose the Churnspire Adjutor, offering a yearly missive and Rings of Majesty in return. He also asked the Conclave to accept Orchard Tender's Tribute in place of From the Mouth of Babes, and sent a herald to deliver golden missives at the Arcane Colloquium.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: several magicians invited to collect Meraud's golden missives bear Dawnish-style titles, among them Enchanter Vesper Lucentia, witch-warden of Weirwater.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Empire once used armies to retake Llofir's garden in Reikos, a warning about trying to reclaim a fane from an eternal.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are cited as building palaces for the Regents of Summer, from which heralds march out to fight alongside their armies, as an example of how useful fanes can be.
n.Urizen: Meraud asked the Senate to let him, rather than Urizen's senators, choose the Churnspire Adjutor, making the post his representative to Urizen. In return the Adjutor would gain a yearly missive to him and Rings of Majesty. Artemis Grey would remain in the role for now.

t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is recalled as the place where the Empire used armies to take back Llofir's garden many years ago.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Enchanter Vesper Lucentia, witch-warden of Weirwater, was among the magicians invited to receive a golden missive from Meraud's herald.

Twelfth of never.d: Citadel Guard scouts in the Salt Flats of Sanath took the Druj messengers into custody before the summit. The message to Emperor Vesna proposed that if the Empire withdrew all forces from the Salt Flats of Sanath and the Forest of Ulnak for a season and a year, no Druj would attack Imperial citizens or holdings. One complete Black Lotus plant had been placed with the Lictors of Bar and Bond, the Green Iron Gaolers, to be released to the Throne if the truce held for five seasons, or sooner if the Druj attacked. The Druj threatened to destroy every plant rather than let them be taken. Historians believe this may be the first formal Druj offer of terms. The messengers were sent away unharmed.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: one of the Druj signatories styles himself 'Livid-Eye, who is Dayne of the False Dawn'.
n.Druj: The Congress of Buruk Tepel made what may be the first formal Druj offer of surrender terms, staking a Black Lotus plant with the Lictors to guarantee a truce, while threatening to destroy all their Black Lotus rather than lose it in battle.

t.Forest of Ulnak: The Druj demanded that the Empire withdraw all its forces from the Forest of Ulnak for a season and a year as a condition of the proposed truce.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Druj messengers approached Citadel Guard pickets here under a white flag, and the offer required the Empire to pull all its forces out of the Salt Flats for a season and a year.

Value beneath the mountain.d: After the Ashen Flame raised Mount Polus (renamed Kespoena's Reach) with the Hand that Shakes the Heavens, a crevasse opened at its base. The Argent Sword's heralds explored it, delivering three wains of mithril to their general and finding a mithril vein. The vein could become the Kespoena's Nadir bourse seat (300 thrones, six months, 12 wains of mithril a season) by Senate motion or announcement by the Master of the Koboldi, whose heralds wish to build it. Six perilous conjunctions into the caverns, facing Disciples of Sulemaine, bandits and strange humanoid creatures, could each cut the cost by eight thrones, and all six would halve the build time. Once built, a suitable army could explore deeper still.

n.Urizen: Urizen's Argent Sword found the mithril vein, and several Urizeni title-holders, including Clytemnestra, Herminius, Felix of the Wise Citadel, Arephanes and Donato, were charged with clearing the caverns in return for rewards. Their nation stood to gain a new mithril seat in Zenith.

t.Zenith: Zenith gained a newly discovered mithril vein beneath its highest mountain and a possible new bourse seat. Its caverns, however, harboured hostile creatures, a band of Disciples of Sulemaine and fleeing bandits.

r.Zenith/Occursion: Beneath Kespoena's Reach in Occursion lay the mithril vein, an underground lake, lightstone deposits and a gemstone cache, all of them threatened by hostile dwellers in the dark. These caverns were where Kespoena's Nadir could be built.

Wayfaring strangers.d: Peleus of Maykop sought Robert Von Holberg and the Ambassador to Axos, bringing a gift from the Grand Ilarch. Robert Stewart of the Forge and Furnace Fellowship came to settle the Tassatan Hills ilium dispute. If no plan emerged, labour costs would rise by three crowns per wain in Tassato from Winter 388YE, spreading to all League territories if the dispute was unresolved by the end of Spring 389YE. Anka Karass sought a private meeting with the Envoy to the Karass. The Marsh Lantern Spire asked the Magpies to remove a shroud from a cursed Druj fear artefact. The Wraith King's crew came to meet the Magpies. Beoraidh's maistirs staged the Battle of the Bay in the Anvil arena. Sebastião Duarte di Tassato offered covenstones for cursing Vellenka Vanyanova.

n.Druj: An Urizeni spire uncovered a cursed Druj artefact of fear in old ruins in Sarangrave. The Karass' long-feared betrayal turned out to be aimed at the Druj, aiding the Imperial raid on Druj-held Ulnak and Sanath.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh's original arena was burned in an Imperial raid while the city was still under the Grendel banner.
n.Highguard: Highguard was one of three Imperial nations on the Bay of Catazar invited to field an eight-strong team in the Battle of the Bay against fighters from the Iron Confederacy and Morajasse.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs' raid with the Navarr on the Forest of Ulnak and the Salt Flats of Sanath succeeded only thanks to the Karass. Formerly enslaved Sannites among them had earlier derailed Beoraidh's overtures to the Empire, though negotiations have since smoothed matters.
n.Navarr: The Karass' assistance proved pivotal to the Navarr and Imperial Orc raid on the Forest of Ulnak and the Salt Flats of Sanath, though the Karass split from the rescue party along the way.
n.The League: League senators faced a Forge and Furnace Fellowship demand for redress over the Tassatan Hills, with strikes threatened first in Tassato and then across the League. Meanwhile a Tassatan merchant prince declared a vendetta against the Shadowed Torchbearer, and Robert Von Holberg was sought by an Axou emissary.
n.Urizen: The Marsh Lantern Spire, a new Urizeni settlement in Sarangrave, brought a cursed Druj artefact to the Magpies, and Urizen was invited to field a team in the Battle of the Bay.

t.Bay of Catazar: The maistirs of Beoraidh invited the friendly nations bordering the Bay of Catazar to compete in a gladiatorial tourney they named the Battle of the Bay.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: the Karass' part in the Imperial raid on the Forest of Ulnak drove interest in Anka Karass' visit.
t.Holberg: Holberg's senator had already paid the Forge and Furnace Fellowship 175 thrones in recompense. Holberg faced rising labour costs if the ilium dispute was not settled by the end of Spring 389YE.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: the Karass aided the Imperial raid on the Salt Flats of Sanath.
t.Sarangrave: A seer of the newly founded Marsh Lantern Spire uncovered Druj ruins in Sarangrave holding a shrouded artefact that radiates fear and would unleash a curse if destroyed carelessly.
t.Tassato: If Robert Stewart left unconvinced, labourers in Tassato would be encouraged to strike, adding three crowns per wain to new commissions from Winter 388YE. Tassato was also home to the merchant prince who declared a vendetta against the Shadowed Torchbearer.

r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: The disputed Tassatan Hills ilium mine lies in the hills of Tassato Mestra. The Fellowship sought its return to the League, the 85 thrones from its auction, or other compensation.

When something is lost.d: The Night magic brought dreams of a phantasmal forest and friendlier encounters with heralds of Sung, Sadogua and Azoth, along with a mooted idea of following it with Spring and Winter enchantments. The Star Forged, enchanted with Find the Best Path, completed the work in Siroc Bayou and helped claim Crucible. The Drakes, carrying Clarity of the Master Strategist, seem to be still exploring it. Only four units escaped. Hakima advise going to look for them. Military units may take the Find the Drakes venture, with Freeborn, Navarr and Marcher units most effective, and any Marcher may support the effort. Eternal plenipotentiaries or a Conclave Order could also help.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Fay Baker of Dawn commanded one of the four units that emerged from Crucible, and Dawnish units can join the rescue only at reduced effectiveness.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South left Madruga to campaign against the Jotun in Bregasland.
n.Navarr: Navarr's new army, the Star Forged, emerged muddied but triumphant after helping make Crucible truly Imperial, and Navarr units contribute fully to the rescue of the Drakes.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn territory of Madruga is now wholly Imperial but steeped in Night magic. Iñez i Azul-Mar i Riqueza led one of the escaped units, and Freeborn units are fully effective in the rescue.
n.The Marches: The Drakes, first army of the Marches under Alfred Houtman Fella, are lost in Crucible. That has sparked an outpouring of support, and any Marcher may now help bring them home.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South had joined the campaign against the Jotun there.
t.Madruga: A Night enchantment fills Madruga with dreams of a marshy forest and more frequent visits from heralds of Night, while its last two regions came under Imperial control and the Drakes were lost within it.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: in the story, lost Drakes soldiers remark that they are no longer in Mitwold.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold led the Marcher outpouring of support for the missing Drakes.

r.Madruga/Crucible: Crucible was mapped and garrisoned enough to become truly Imperial, but it grows wilder the deeper one goes, and the Drakes are trapped somewhere inside awaiting rescue.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: The Star Forged emerged from Crucible into Lightsea, expecting to meet the Drakes there, and rescuers may lead the lost army back to it.
r.Madruga/Quiet Grasses: Mentioned in passing: named as a place that might benefit from follow-up Spring and Winter enchantments, and as a possible exit for the rescued Drakes.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: The Drakes and Star Forged finished the Corsairs' work and brought the bayou into Imperial control, fighting phantasmal soldiers whose blows wounded only mind and spirit, though enigmas remain.
